docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
The North Wales Social Housing Newbuild on-Site Energy Generation and Storage (NewSEGS) project aims to identify and optimise opportunities for self-supply of renewable energy in newbuild social housing in North Wales.

The NewSEGS-modelling project builds on the work of Dr David Sprake to produce estimates of the financial performance of a local energy system.

docs.title: Model Concept
docs.text:
NewsegsMetamodel conceptual diagram

A metamodel combines an energy model (generation, grid, and consumption and storage modules acting on a site's environment) with a finance model and a set of variables that characterise the uncertainty in the model's parameters. Metamodels are collected in a project. A metamodel can be run deterministically, or analysed with deterministic (DSA) or probabilistic (PSA) sensitivity analysis and optimisation.

docs.title: Software structure
docs.text:
The software is split into four groups of Python packages (all under src/):

Package Purpose Documentation newsegsmodelframework The modelling framework: models, modules, finance, variables, metamodels, projects, sensitivity analysis and statistics. Has no dependency on the web app. Framework newsegsmodelapp The Dash web application, the database it relies upon and the background workers that run the models. Depends on the framework. Application newsegsmodelutils What the framework and the application share but neither owns: at present, the functions that draw figures from the framework's data. Uses the framework, but not the app. Plotting utilities newa, admdspenmw, config Supporting packages: New European Wind Atlas access, After Diversity Maximum Demand calculation and application settings. Supporting packages

Both the framework and the application are extended by plugins: the framework with new project types, and the application with new pages and models. See Architecture for how the pieces fit together.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
• To use the app: User guide.
  • To understand how the pieces fit together: Architecture.
  • To add a new kind of model: Framework plugins, then Application plugins.
  • To understand what is stored by the app: Database.

docs.title: The framework (newsegsmodelframework)
docs.text:
The framework knows nothing about the web application, and draws no figures: it uses neither Dash nor any plotting library. It provides:

  • core - the base classes: revision-tracked, serialisable components (NewsegsComponent), NewsegsModule, time spans, locations and the environment servers that supply weather data.
  • The model modules (newsegsgrid, newsegsgeneration, newsegscs), which are assembled by a model (newsegsmodel).
  • Finance (newsegsfinance) which values the output of a model.
  • Variables (newsegsvariable) which statistically characterise parameters of the model and finance.
  • The metamodel and project (newsegsmetamodel, newsegsproject), which bind models, finance and variables together and put them in a state ready to run.
  • Sensitivity analysis, optimisation and statistics (newsegssensitivity, newsegsstats).
  • Utilities (util).
  • Plugins which register the project types the framework offers.

Every object that is configured by the user is a NewsegsComponent or DataWithRevision, and can therefore be serialised to and from a dictionary. The app stores these dictionaries in its database (see Database).

docs.title: The plotting utilities (newsegsmodelutils)
docs.text: The plotting utilities draw figures from the data of the framework, such as the plots of a PSA, for the app (and for scripts). They use the framework, but the framework does not use them.

docs.title: The application (newsegsmodelapp)
docs.text:
The application consists of:

  • a Dash front end (app.py, newsegsmodelapp.components), a multi-page app whose pages and model-specific contents are supplied by plugins;
  • a backend (newsegsmodelapp.backend) containing the database layer, a ZeroMQ dispatcher, the workers that perform runs and the maintenance jobs;
  • a SQLite database holding configurations, snapshots, requests, runs and sessions. Result data are written to a results store on disk, and the database refers to them.

The front end never runs a model itself. User actions create requests in the database. The front end's action manager sends new requests to the dispatcher, which hands them to workers. Each worker records progress in a run, and writes results to the results store. The front end polls the database for progress and loads results from the results store when they are complete. Each completed run may trigger postprocessing and table-drawing requests (see Application plugins).

These processes are started as separate services in docker-compose.yml (dash-app, zmq-dispatcher, maintenance-cron).

docs.title: Supporting packages
docs.text:
• newa - retrieves wind resource data from the New European Wind Atlas.
  • admdspenmw - After Diversity Maximum Demand calculation.
  • config - the settings object (Dynaconf reading src/settings.toml).

docs.title: Development and releases
docs.text:
Work moves through three branches:

Branch Purpose Changed by development Integration of feature and fix pull requests Squash-merged pull requests canary Early release testing; each merge makes a prerelease vX.Y.Z-canary.N Merge-commit pull requests from development main Production; each merge makes a release vX.Y.Z Merge-commit pull requests from canary

docs.title: Making a change
docs.text:
1. Branch from development, and open the pull request against development.

  2. Give the pull request a Conventional Commit title. It is checked by the pull request title workflow, and it becomes the commit message when the pull request is squash-merged, so it sets the next version:

    Title Release fix: correct the export tariff patch feat: add a location to the map minor feat!: change the project file format, or a BREAKING CHANGE: ... footer in the description major docs:, test:, refactor:, ci:, chore:, ... none

  3. The unit tests workflow runs on the pull request. It first regenerates the default model artifacts and compares them with data/ (see CI checks and generated model artifacts for retrieving them if they differ), then runs the unit tests, excluding the PSA and DSA tests. The Excel validation tests run too, from the results extracted into data/sprake_validation/. Squash-merge the pull request.

Every push to development builds the Docker image.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
The unit tests are in test/unit_tests. Run them from the repository root with src on the path, as the unit tests workflow does:

PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest test/unit_tests \
    --ignore=test/unit_tests/test_dsa --ignore=test/unit_tests/test_psa \
    --ignore=test/unit_tests/test_dsa_multiple.py --ignore=test/unit_tests/test_psa_multiple.py

The excluded PSA and DSA tests are slow; they run in the enhanced unit tests workflow on a release. The tests are unittest test cases, so the VS Code test explorer (configured for unittest) runs them too.

docs.title: Callback tests
docs.text:
test/unit_tests/test_app_callbacks tests the Dash callbacks without a browser. Each test builds a minimal NewsegsDash holding the input container callbacks, with a temporary database and a sprake project, and posts requests to /_dash-update-component with the Flask test client. Dash itself then dispatches the request, so the tests cover the callback's registration, pattern matching, ctx and grouped outputs. They don't show that a browser emits a given event.

PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest test/unit_tests/test_app_callbacks

The tests depend on the format of Dash's requests, so requirements-test.txt pins the Dash packages to the versions in conda-environment.yml. Change them together.

  • dash_dispatch.py holds the helpers. dispatch_input_change posts a change of an input to react_to_input_change and returns a CallbackResponse: response.updated is false when Dash made no update, and response.get(id, prop) gives the value returned for a component, or NOT_UPDATED. The callback's inputs, outputs and state are read from /_dash-dependencies. The components sent with each wildcard are those of the "page": a list of components, usually rendered by the app's own input container content creators with render_input_containers, so the tests follow the layout.
  • base.py holds InputChangeTestCase. It sets up each test afresh, and has helpers to set up the project as the app does (add_configuration, make_independent, set_focus, remove_configuration) and to read what is stored: stored_variable and loaded_variable, revised (rows whose revision changed), stale_marks (configurations and processes marked stale) and assertNothingChanged. It reads through an uncached provider, so the assertions see the database rather than a cache.
  • Each test case runs with the uncached project provider, and again with the cached provider the app uses, through cached_variant.
  • test_row_anchors.py renders every registered input container for each model type, and fails if a row has an input of react_to_input_change but no component matching its first output. The Dash renderer never calls the callback for such a row, and a request-level test can't show that.

docs.title: Adding a test of an input handler
docs.text:
Add a test case to test_registered_handlers.py, or to a new test_*.py module in the package. Render the page that holds the input, dispatch a change, and assert on both the response and the database:

from .base import InputChangeTestCase, cached_variant
from .dash_dispatch import NOT_UPDATED, variable_id

class TestMyHandler(InputChangeTestCase):
    """`my-purpose` of an `input-toggle`"""
    n_metamodels = 2  # the configurations share every variable until made independent

    def test_saved(self):
        components = self.page(('dsa', None))  # (supersection, section) of each input container
        trigger = variable_id('input-toggle', 'my-purpose', 'gen_input', 'wind_capacity', supersection = 'dsa')
        t0 = self.now()

        response = self.dispatch(trigger, True, components)

        self.assertIsNot(
            response.get(variable_id('input-group-config-update-trigger', 'trigger', 'gen_input', 'wind_capacity', supersection = 'dsa'), 'data'),
            NOT_UPDATED,
        )
        self.assertTrue(self.loaded_variable('gen_input.wind_capacity.0', 1).my_setting)
        self.assertEqual(self.stale_marks(t0), {(x, 'dsa') for x in self.metamodel_ids})

TestMyHandlerCached = cached_variant(TestMyHandler)

If the input isn't rendered by a content creator, add a component for it to the page, such as dcc.Input(id = trigger). Change data through the app's own paths, or through the base.py helpers that copy them, so that caches see the change as they would in the app. A handler that should make no change must also leave the database as it was: check with database_state and assertNothingChanged.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The documentation is built with MkDocs from the markdown in docs/ and the docstrings in src/.

pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
mkdocs serve   # live preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000
mkdocs build   # writes static HTML to site/
  • On pushes to main the publish documentation workflow deploys the site to the gh-pages branch (GitHub Pages must be set to deploy from that branch).
  • The running app serves the built HTML from site/ (or DOCS_PATH) at /documentation/; the Docker image builds it automatically.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
• Prerelease. Open a pull request from development to canary, and merge it with a merge commit (not squash or rebase, which would separate the histories of the branches). The release workflow runs the unit tests, then tags vX.Y.Z-canary.N and makes a GitHub prerelease.
  • Release. Open a pull request from canary to main, and merge it with a merge commit. The unit tests run on the pull request; on the merge, the release workflow runs the PSA and DSA tests (enhanced unit tests), tags vX.Y.Z, makes a GitHub Release, and then merges main back into canary, so that the next prerelease is counted from this release.

Versions come from python-semantic-release, configured in pyproject.toml. A release is a tag and a GitHub Release only: nothing is committed back, so project.version in pyproject.toml is not updated. A vX.Y.Z tag pushed by hand also gets a GitHub Release.

docs.title: Branch protection
docs.text:
Rulesets on the repository enforce this:

  • main: changes only through a pull request with the unit-tests check passing, merged with a merge commit; no force pushes or deletion.
  • canary: no force pushes or deletion. Pull requests are not required, so that the release workflow can merge main back into it.
  • development: changes only through a squash-merged pull request; no force pushes or deletion.

docs.title: CI checks and generated model artifacts
docs.text:
Pull requests targeting development, canary or main run the unit-test workflow. The workflow first regenerates the default model artifacts and checks them against the files in data/; it does not modify the pull request. PSA/DSA tests run separately on pushes to main. The Excel-based validation tests compare against results extracted from the validation workbook into data/sprake_validation/, so they run in CI without it. After the workbook changes, rerun scripts/210_extract_sprake_validation_results.py on a computer with access to it and commit the updated files.

If generated artifacts differ from the checked-in files, the prerequisite check fails and uploads the generated files as the generated-default-model-artifacts workflow artifact. To retrieve them, open the failed workflow run from the pull request's Checks tab, then download the artifact from the run summary's Artifacts section. Update the corresponding files in data/ and push the changes to the pull request; the check must pass before the pull request can merge.

The artifact is available when generation reaches the comparison step. If generation fails earlier, generated files may not be available to download.

docs.title: Profiling
docs.text:
For profiling, use viztracer:

python -m viztracer --log_async --min_duration 500 -o trace.json src/app.py

Results can be viewed at https://www.speedscope.app/ or https://ui.perfetto.dev/.

docs.title: Docstring conventions
docs.text:
The API reference pages are generated from docstrings (Google style), so each level of the code documents a different thing:

Where Documents Example Package __init__.py What the package is for, and a guide to its modules. Does not repeat module or class documentation. newsegsmetamodel/__init__.py Module (.py file) The role of the module and anything that is not a class or function it defines, e.g. helpers it also contains. newsegsmetamodel.py Class What an instance represents, what it holds, its states and how to use it. Details of use belong here, not in the module. NewsegsMetaModel Function or method What it does, Args, Returns and Raises.

Rules of thumb:

  • Public classes, functions and methods (names not starting _) should have a docstring. Methods that override a documented method with @override inherit its documentation.
  • A first line that stands alone as a summary, then a blank line.
  • Docstrings that still contain TODO were generated as templates and need writing. Search for TODO: Add to find them.
  • Cross-reference with the full path, e.g. [`find_constructor`][newsegsmodelframework.core.find_constructor].

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
This guide gives an overview of the interactions and capabilities of the NewSEGS modelling framework as accessed via the web app. If you are looking for how to create your own models or run calculations in python, start with Modelling principles.

The guide will take you through the following actions:

  • Starting the app.
  • Selecting a model type.
  • Setting up a project.
  • Setting up a configuration.
  • Running deterministic analyses.
  • Optimising
  • Running deterministic sensitivity analyses (DSA).
  • Running probabilistic sensitivity analyses (PSA).

docs.title: Key terms
docs.text: Term Meaning Model type The energy model used, e.g. the Sprake model or the localised model. Each model type has its own projects. Project A set of configurations to compare. The app keeps your project between visits. Configuration One option for a site: its generation, storage, consumption and costs. Each configuration has a number and a colour, used in every input, header and plot. The first, Baseline, can't be moved or removed. Snapshot A saved copy of a project, which can be restored as a new project. Deterministic run A run of a configuration with the central value of every input. DSA Deterministic sensitivity analysis: runs with each selected input at its lower and upper bound in turn, to show which inputs matter most. PSA Probabilistic sensitivity analysis: many runs with the inputs drawn from their distributions, to show the spread of the results.

docs.title: Starting the app
docs.text: The app runs in a web browser. See Install and run to start it, with Docker or without. Once it is running, open http://localhost:8050.

docs.title: Selecting a model type
docs.text:
The first page offers the model types. Click one to open its landing page. The Documentation button opens this documentation.

The landing page describes the model: its structure, assumptions and the data it uses.

docs.title: Moving between pages
docs.text: The button at the top left of each page opens the navigation bar. Its buttons go to the landing page, the site configuration, the sensitivity analysis (DSA and optimisation) and the probabilistic analysis (PSA) pages, and to this documentation.

docs.title: Setting up a project
docs.text:
The app opens your last project of the model type, or a new project if you have none. Its name is shown at the top of each page. The button beside the name opens the project controls:

  • Project management: rename the project, load another, start a fresh project, duplicate this one, or delete it.
  • Snapshots: save a snapshot of the project, and load, rename or delete snapshots. Loading a snapshot restores it as a new project.

Give each project a meaningful name: new projects are called Untitled project.

docs.title: Setting up a configuration
docs.text:
The site configuration page holds the inputs of the focussed configuration, on the left, and the results of every configuration, on the right.

  • Configurations: the list under Results shows every configuration of the project. Its buttons focus a configuration (so its inputs are shown), duplicate it, download or upload it as a file, download its results, and remove it. A copy is named after its source, e.g. Baseline (copy); type a meaningful name in its name box.
  • Site: for the localised model, choose the site on the map or by its latitude and longitude, and give it a name. Get environmental data fetches the weather data of the site and shows its wind and solar conditions. The first fetch for a site can take several minutes.
  • Inputs: each section of inputs (generation, storage, consumption, costs...) can be opened to change its values. When configurations share an input, opening its summary shows the groups of configurations with the same value, and lets you move configurations between them.

docs.title: Running deterministic analyses
docs.text:
The run buttons beside Results run the focussed configuration, or every configuration. Progress is shown over the results while the run is under way. When it completes, the results of each configuration are shown in its colour: generation, storage, consumption and finance, per year or to the horizon of the model (the toggle under Results).

Results go out of date when an input they depend on changes; the header of each result shows when they are.

docs.title: Optimising the configuration
docs.text: The sensitivity analysis page also holds the optimisation. Choose the inputs to optimise and their bounds, and the statistic to optimise, then start the optimisation. When it finishes, the app reports what the optimisation achieved and, if it found an improvement, applies it to the configuration.

docs.title: Running deterministic sensitivity analyses (DSA)
docs.text:
On the sensitivity analysis page, choose the inputs to vary with their toggles, and their lower and upper bounds. Run DSA runs the focussed configuration, or every configuration, with each input at its bounds in turn.

The results are shown as a table and a tornado plot of the chosen statistic. Multiple compares the configurations, and Pairwise compares one configuration with a reference.

docs.title: Running probabilistic sensitivity analyses (PSA)
docs.text:
On the probabilistic analysis page, set the number of samples and the random seed, and choose the inputs to draw, with their distributions. Run PSA runs the configurations for each draw.

The results are shown as plots, chosen from the list above them, such as a scatter of costs and benefits, and as tables. As for the DSA, Multiple and Pairwise compare configurations.

docs.title: Application overview
docs.text:
newsegsmodelapp is the web application for the NewSEGS model. It is a multi-page Dash app (entry point src/app.py) supported by a SQLite database and background workers.

src/
├── app.py                   # creates the Dash app (NewsegsDash) and binds callbacks
├── app_logging.py
├── settings.toml            # settings read by config.settings
└── newsegsmodelapp/
    ├── registers.py         # registries that plugins add to (see Plugins)
    ├── register_plugins.py  # imports every plugin
    ├── types.py             # Page and LayoutConfiguration
    ├── dash_extension.py    # NewsegsDash - Dash app which holds the providers
    ├── backend/             # database, dispatcher, workers, maintenance
    ├── components/          # reusable Dash components, layouts and callbacks
    └── plugins/
        ├── pages/           # the pages of the app and the processes they launch
        └── models/          # model-type specific inputs, results and processing
Section Contents Plugins How to add pages and model types to the app Backend Database layer, dispatcher, workers and maintenance Components Reusable components, layouts and callbacks Database Tables and relationships

docs.title: Running a model
docs.text:
1. A user acts on a page (for example presses run). A callback calls the run request function registered for that action, which creates a RunRequest that is written to the requests table.
  2. The front end's action manager (manage_actions, in components/callbacks/action_callbacks.py) picks up AWAITING DISPATCH requests and sends them over ZeroMQ to the dispatcher, which hands each to a worker.
  3. The worker creates a run, looks up the run procedure registered for the request type and executes it, updating the run's progress and checking whether cancellation has been requested. Results are written to the results store and recorded in results.
  4. Completing a request triggers its post-actions: postprocess procedures convert results into the form needed by the interface, and table draw procedures prepare the tables. These are themselves requests, executed in the same way.
  5. The front end polls the runs table for progress and, when the run completes, loads the results and updates the page.

docs.title: Documentation inside the app
docs.text: The HTML of these pages is built with mkdocs build into the site/ directory, from where the app serves it at /documentation/. The help button on the navigation bar, and the documentation link on the model selection page, open it; the Back to the app link in the documentation header returns to the app launch page. The DOCS_PATH setting (see src/settings.toml) overrides the directory that is served. The Docker image builds the documentation as part of the image build.

docs.title: Backend API Reference
docs.text:
The backend contains everything that does not draw the user interface. Its processes are started separately from the Dash app (docker-compose.yml):

Module Purpose Service newsegsmodelapp.backend.dispatcher Proxy between the front end and the workers; supervises workers and writes a heartbeat file zmq-dispatcher newsegsmodelapp.backend.worker Executes requests - looks up and calls the registered procedures started by the dispatcher newsegsmodelapp.backend.maintenance Schedules backups and pruning maintenance-cron newsegsmodelapp.backend.db Database access, providers and tables all

The database layer includes providers - implementations of the framework's provider interfaces (NewsegsProjectProviderInterface, NewsegsResultProviderInterface) which read and write projects, components, variables and results to the database and results store, with caching - and the request handler.

Get the sqlalchemy engine for the database.

Source code in src/newsegsmodelapp/backend/db/db.py 
def get_engine(*, writer: bool = False, db_path: str | Path | None = None):
    """Get the sqlalchemy engine for the database."""
    db_path = str(db_path or settings['DB_PATH'])
    key = (os.getpid(), writer, db_path)           # fork-safe
    if key not in _engines:
        _engines[key] = _make_engine(db_path, writer=writer)
    return _engines[key]

docs.title: init_db(db_path=DB_PATH, recovery_path=DB_BACKUP_PATH)
docs.text:
Make sure the application database exists and is up to date.

If the database file is missing it is recovered from a backup or created; otherwise the migrations are applied. Raises FileNotFoundError if it cannot be found or created.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default db_path str

Path of the database file.

DB_PATH recovery_path str | Path

Directory from which a missing database is recovered.

DB_BACKUP_PATH Source code in src/newsegsmodelapp/backend/db/db.py 
def init_db(db_path: str = DB_PATH, recovery_path: str | Path = DB_BACKUP_PATH):
    """Make sure the application database exists and is up to date.

    If the database file is missing it is recovered from a backup or created; otherwise the migrations are applied. Raises `FileNotFoundError` if it cannot be found or created.

    Args:
        db_path: Path of the database file.
        recovery_path: Directory from which a missing database is recovered.
    """
    db_file_status = retrieve_db_file(db_path, recovery_path)
    match db_file_status:
        case 'missing':
            db_exists = create_db(db_path)
            if not db_exists:
                raise FileNotFoundError('Unable to find or create application database.')
        case _:
            run_migrations()

def retrieve_latest_backup(
    db_path: str | Path = DB_PATH,
    backup_dir: str | Path = DB_BACKUP_PATH
) -> RETRIEVAL_STATUS:
    """Finds the most recent backup in directory and retrieves it."""
    if not isinstance(db_path, Path):
        db_path = Path(db_path)
    if not isinstance(backup_dir, Path):
        backup_dir = Path(backup_dir)

    if not backup_dir.exists():
        return 'missing'

    # Find all backup files and sort by modification time (newest last)
    backup_files = sorted(
        backup_dir.glob(f"{settings['DB_FILENAME_ROOT']}_*.db"),
        key = os.path.getmtime
    )

    if not backup_files:
        return 'missing'

    latest_backup = backup_files[-1]
    logger.warning('Restoring database from latest backup: %s', latest_backup.name)

    # Ensure target directory exists
    db_path.parent.mkdir(parents = True, exist_ok = True)

    # Perform safe restore using SQLite backup API
    with sqlite3.connect(latest_backup) as source:
        with sqlite3.connect(db_path) as dest:
            source.backup(dest)

    logger.warning('Database restoration complete.')
    return 'from_backup'

) -> bool:

def init_db(db_path: str = DB_PATH, recovery_path: str | Path = DB_BACKUP_PATH):
    """Make sure the application database exists and is up to date.

    If the database file is missing it is recovered from a backup or created; otherwise the migrations are applied. Raises `FileNotFoundError` if it cannot be found or created.

    Args:
        db_path: Path of the database file.
        recovery_path: Directory from which a missing database is recovered.
    """
    db_file_status = retrieve_db_file(db_path, recovery_path)
    match db_file_status:
        case 'missing':
            db_exists = create_db(db_path)
            if not db_exists:
                raise FileNotFoundError('Unable to find or create application database.')
        case _:
            run_migrations()

Execute stmt with engine, retrying on lock/operational errors using exponential backoff and randomized jitter.

def write_with_retries(
    engine: sa.Engine, 
    stmt,
    parameters: Optional[Any] = None,
    n_retries: int = 10,
    base_sleep: float = 0.05, 
    max_sleep: float = 4.0
):
    """Execute stmt with engine, retrying on lock/operational errors 
    using exponential backoff and randomized jitter.
    """
    attempt = 0
    while True:
        try:
            with write_transaction(engine) as conn:
                if parameters is None:
                    conn.execute(stmt)
                else:
                    conn.execute(stmt, parameters)
            logger.debug("Successfully completed database write.")
            return True
        except (OperationalError, DBAPIError) as e:
            # Check if it's actually a lock or timeout error
            err_msg = str(e).lower()
            is_lock = any(k in err_msg for k in ["locked", "timeout", "deadlock", "busy"])

            if not is_lock or (n_retries >= 0 and attempt >= n_retries):
                raise e

            attempt += 1
            # Exponential backoff with random jitter (prevents thundering herd)
            sleep_time = min(max_sleep, base_sleep * (2 ** attempt)) + random.uniform(0, 0.05)

            logger.warning(
                f"Encountered lock/operational error (attempt {attempt}/{n_retries if n_retries >= 0 else 'inf'}): {e}. "
                f"Retrying in {sleep_time:.2f}s... SQL: {stmt}"
            )
            time.sleep(sleep_time)

class FromDatabaseNewsegsComponentProvider(
    NewsegsComponentManagerInterface
):
    """Provider and store of components, in the component configs table.

    Components are held as JSON payloads with the metadata (type, class, version, revision and label) in columns. Components which own child
    components record their ids, and the children are fetched and reattached when the component is reconstructed. Lightweight descriptions of components
    can be fetched without constructing them.

    Args:
        get_engine: Function returning the SQLAlchemy engine.
    """
    _table = tbls.component_configs

    _lightweight_component_columns = tuple(
        tbls.component_configs.columns[x] for x in (
            'id',
            'revision'
        )
    )

    _lightweight_dataholding_component_columns = tuple(
        tbls.component_configs.columns[x] for x in (
            'id',

            'component_type',
            'component_class',
            'component_version',

            'revision',
        )
    )
    def __init__(self, get_engine: Callable[[], sa.Engine]):
        self._get_engine = get_engine

    def _component_from_json(self, json_payload: str) -> NewsegsComponent:
        constr_dict = json.loads(json_payload)
        return cast(
            NewsegsComponent,
            find_constructor(constr_dict['constructor_class'], constr_dict['class'])(constr_dict)
        )

    def _assign_updated_child_uids(self, obj, row):
        """Given the row for the component, get the live ids for each of the child components.

        Also take the opportunity to update any metadata that may have changed."""
        obj.name = row._mapping['label']
        return obj

    def _reattach_children(self, obj):
        """Once the component has updated uids for retrieving children, get them using the necessary providers."""
        return obj

    def _reconstruct_component(self, json_payload, row) -> NewsegsComponent:
        obj = self._component_from_json(json_payload)
        obj.id = row.id # The ID may have changed from the payload - set it now
        obj = self._assign_updated_child_uids(obj, row)
        obj = self._reattach_children(obj)
        if obj.revision != row.revision:
            obj.revision = row.revision
            obj._config._last_syncronised = obj.revision
        return obj

    def _reconstruct_lightweight_component(self, row) -> LightweightNewsegsComponent:
        metadata = dict(row._mapping)
        revision = metadata.pop('revision')
        comp = LightweightNewsegsComponent.from_dict(metadata)
        comp.revision = revision
        comp._syncronise()
        return comp

    def _reconstruct_lightweight_dataholding_component(self, row) -> LightweightDataHoldingNewsegsComponent:
        metadata = dict(row._mapping)
        revision = metadata.pop('revision')
        comp = LightweightDataHoldingNewsegsComponent.from_dict(metadata)
        comp.revision = revision
        comp._syncronise()
        return comp

    def _component_to_table_data(self, component: NewsegsComponent) -> dict:
        if component.modified:
            raise ValueError(f'{component.id} is being upserted in a modified state')
        return component_to_raw_table_data(component)

    @overload
    def get_component(self, component_id: str) -> NewsegsComponent:
        ...

    @overload
    def get_component(self, component_id: SequenceNotStr[str]) -> SequenceNotStr[NewsegsComponent]:
        ...

    @override
    def get_component(self, component_id: str | SequenceNotStr[str]) -> NewsegsComponent | SequenceNotStr[NewsegsComponent]:
        prevstate = RevisionNotifierMixin._set_notification_state('disabled')
        try:
            is_sequence = False
            if isinstance(component_id, str):
                stmt = (
                    self._table.select()
                    .where(self._table.c.id == component_id)
                )
            else:
                is_sequence = True
                stmt = (
                    self._table.select()
                    .where(self._table.c.id.in_(component_id))
                )

            with read_transaction(self._get_engine()) as conn:
                # MUST fetch, otherwise holding the connection open too long
                rows = conn.execute(stmt).fetchall()
            reconstructed_components = [self._reconstruct_component(row.payload, row) for row in rows]

        finally:
            RevisionNotifierMixin._set_notification_state(prevstate)

        if not is_sequence:
            if len(reconstructed_components) == 0:
                raise ValueError(f'Component not found: {component_id} in table {self._table}')
            return reconstructed_components[0]

        compmap = {x.id: x for x in reconstructed_components}
        return [compmap[x] for x in component_id]

    def get_lightweight_component(
        self, component_id: str | SequenceNotStr[str]
    ) -> LightweightNewsegsComponent | SequenceNotStr[LightweightNewsegsComponent]:
        """Get the lightweight description of a component (or components).

        Contains the information needed to display the component, without constructing it.

        Args:
            component_id: Id(s) of the component(s).

        Returns:
            The lightweight component(s).
        """
        prevstate = RevisionNotifierMixin._set_notification_state('disabled')
        try:
            is_sequence = False
            if isinstance(component_id, str):
                stmt = (
                    sa.select(*self._lightweight_component_columns)
                    .where(self._table.c.id == component_id)
                )
            else:
                is_sequence = True
                stmt = (
                    sa.select(*self._lightweight_component_columns)
                    .where(self._table.c.id.in_(component_id))
                )
            with read_transaction(self._get_engine()) as conn:
                rows = conn.execute(stmt).fetchall()

            reconstructed_components = [self._reconstruct_lightweight_component(row) for row in rows]
        finally:
            RevisionNotifierMixin._set_notification_state(prevstate)

        if not is_sequence:
            return reconstructed_components[0]
        compmap = {x.id:x for x in reconstructed_components}
        return [compmap[x] for x in component_id]

    def get_lightweight_dataholding_component(
        self, component_id: str | SequenceNotStr[str]
    ) -> LightweightDataHoldingNewsegsComponent | SequenceNotStr[LightweightDataHoldingNewsegsComponent]:
        """Get a representation of (a) component(s) with sufficient detail to save results against"""
        prevstate = RevisionNotifierMixin._set_notification_state('disabled')
        try:
            is_sequence = False
            if isinstance(component_id, str):
                stmt = (
                    sa.select(*self._lightweight_dataholding_component_columns)
                    .where(self._table.c.id == component_id)
                )
            else:
                is_sequence = True
                stmt = (
                    sa.select(*self._lightweight_dataholding_component_columns)
                    .where(self._table.c.id.in_(component_id))
                )

            with read_transaction(self._get_engine()) as conn:
                rows = conn.execute(stmt).fetchall()

            reconstructed_components = [self._reconstruct_lightweight_dataholding_component(row) for row in rows]
        finally:
            RevisionNotifierMixin._set_notification_state(prevstate)

        if not is_sequence:
            return reconstructed_components[0]
        compmap = {x.id:x for x in reconstructed_components}
        return [compmap[x] for x in component_id]

    def _create_duplicate_component(self, original: NewsegsComponent) -> NewsegsComponent:
        comp1 = original
        comp2 = copy.deepcopy(comp1)
        comp2.anonymise_ids()
        return comp2

    @override
    def duplicate_component(self, component_id: str | NewsegsComponent) -> NewsegsComponent:
        if isinstance(component_id, str):
            orig = self.get_component(component_id)
        else:
            orig = component_id
        comp2 = self._create_duplicate_component(orig)
        comp2.revision = orig.revision
        self.upsert_component(comp2, force = False)

        return comp2

    @override
    def add_component(self, component: NewsegsComponent) -> str:
        self.upsert_component(component, force = True)
        return component.id

    # REVIEW (unreferenced): no references to `get_default_component` found in src/, scripts/ or data/.
    @override
    def get_default_component(
        self,
        component_type: str,
        index: int = -1
    ) -> NewsegsComponent:
        stmt = (
            self._table.select()
            .where(self._table.c.component_type == component_type)
        )

        with read_transaction(self._get_engine()) as conn:
            rows = conn.execute(stmt).fetchall()

        if not rows:
            raise KeyError(f'Component type {component_type} not found - a first application of this component must be added via add_component.')

        row = rows[index]
        return self._reconstruct_component(row.payload, row)

    def _expand_component_sequence(self, component) -> list:
        components = []
        if isinstance(component, NewsegsComponent) and not isinstance(component, Variable):
            components.append(component)
        elif isinstance(component, Mapping):
            for v in component.values():
                if isinstance(v, NewsegsComponent) and not isinstance(v, Variable):
                    components.append(v)
                elif isinstance(v, Mapping) or (not isinstance(v, str) and isinstance(v, Sequence)):
                    components.extend(self._expand_component_sequence(v))
        elif not isinstance(component, str) and isinstance(component, Sequence):
            for v in component:
                if isinstance(v, NewsegsComponent) and not isinstance(v, Variable):
                    components.append(v)
                elif isinstance(v, Mapping) or (not isinstance(v, str) and isinstance(v, Sequence)):
                    components.extend(self._expand_component_sequence(v))
        return components

    def upsert_children(self, component: NewsegsComponent, force: bool = False):
        # Expect to override this for different types of component
        # to deal with different tables
        """Insert or update the child components of a component.

        Args:
            component: The component(s).
            force: Write the component(s) even if their revisions have not changed.
        """
        component_children = component.get_components(component_group= 'component_configs')
        if component_children:
            self.upsert_component(component_children, force = force)

    @override
    def upsert_component(
        self, 
        component: NewsegsComponent | SequenceNotStr[NewsegsComponent], 
        force: bool = False,
        tbl: Optional[sa.Table] = None,
        project_id: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Insert or update a component, or components, in the store.

        A component is written if it is not present, or if its revision differs from the saved revision (or `force`).

        Args:
            component: The component or components.
            force: Write the components even if their revisions have not changed.
            tbl: The table to write to; the table of the provider by default.
            project_id: Project whose cache to invalidate if the upsert changes a table.
        """
        if tbl is None:
            tbl = self._table
        component = self._expand_component_sequence(component)

        if len(component) == 0:
            return

        current_revisions = {x.id: x.revision for x in component}
        uids = list(current_revisions.keys())

        # Get saved revision if exists
        stmt = (
            sa.select(
                tbl.c.id,
                tbl.c.revision
            )
            .where(tbl.c.id.in_(uids))
        )
        with read_transaction(self._get_engine()) as conn:
            rows = conn.execute(stmt).fetchall()

        saved_revisions = {x.id: x.revision for x in rows}
        existing_uids = set(saved_revisions.keys())
        new_inserts = [x for x in uids if x not in existing_uids]
        if not force:
            requires_update = [x for x in existing_uids if current_revisions[x] != saved_revisions[x]]
            # TODO: Remove this logic - all revision handling should be outside of the provider
            # If the object exists and has a matching version number but its children have been modified
            # then we do a simple bump of the revision number to indicate that downstream results are stale
            requires_revision_increment = []
            # for comp in component:
            #     if comp.id not in new_inserts and comp.id not in requires_update:
            #         if comp.chain_modified:
            #             requires_revision_increment.append(comp.id)
            #             comp.revision += 1
            #             # Update the table config revision if components have been modified.
            #             if hasattr(comp, 'table_config'):
            #                 if not comp.table_config.modified:
            #                     comp.table_config.revision += 1
        else:
            requires_update = existing_uids
            requires_revision_increment = []

        requires_data = set(requires_update)
        requires_data.update(set(new_inserts))

        requires_sync = copy.copy(requires_data)
        requires_sync.update(set(requires_revision_increment))

        # First, do the updates, then do the inserts
        for cmp in component:
            if cmp.id in requires_sync:
                # TODO: Consider whether to set a rollback here in case we can't access DB

                #### Save out all child components ####
                self.upsert_children(cmp, force = force)

                cmp.syncronise()

        cmpdata = {cmp.id: self._component_to_table_data(cmp) for cmp in component if cmp.id in requires_data}

        revdata = {cmp.id: {'id': cmp.id, 'revision': cmp.revision,} for cmp in component if cmp.id in requires_revision_increment}

        update_payload = [cmpdata[x] for x in requires_update]
        insert_payload = [cmpdata[x] for x in new_inserts]
        rev_payload = [revdata[x] for x in requires_revision_increment]

        if not (update_payload or insert_payload):
            return

        with write_transaction(self._get_engine(writer = True)) as conn:
            if rev_payload:
                # Cannot use 'id' as the bindparam - rename it
                rev_payload = [{'b_id': x.pop('id'), **x} for x in rev_payload]
                rev_stmt = sa.update(tbl).where(tbl.c.id == sa.bindparam('b_id'))
                conn.execute(rev_stmt, rev_payload)

            if update_payload:
                # Cannot use 'id' as the bindparam - rename it
                update_payload = [{'b_id': x.pop('id'), **x} for x in update_payload]
                update_stmt = sa.update(tbl).where(tbl.c.id == sa.bindparam('b_id'))
                conn.execute(update_stmt, update_payload)

            if insert_payload:
                insert_stmt = tbl.insert()
                conn.execute(insert_stmt, insert_payload)

            if project_id and (rev_payload or update_payload or insert_payload):
                # Cache invalidate by touching the project table
                conn.execute(sa.update(tbls.projects).where(tbls.projects.c.id == project_id).values(id = project_id))

        logger.debug(
            'Inserted %d components into table %s: %s',
            len(insert_payload),
            self._table.name,
            [x.get('id', str(x)) for x in insert_payload]
        )
        logger.debug(
            'Updated %d components in table %s: %s',
            len(update_payload),
            self._table.name,
            [x.get('b_id', str(x)) for x in update_payload]
        )
        logger.debug(
            'Revised %d components in table %s: %s',
            len(rev_payload),
            self._table.name,
            [x.get('b_id', str(x)) for x in rev_payload]
        )

    def _delete_one_component(
            self, 
            component_id: str,
            ignore_ids: list[str] = []
            ) -> None:
        # Assume that we are dealing only with members of the component_config table.

        # Any energy model configurations using this component must be identified
        get_em_count_stmt = (
            sa.select(sa.func.count())
            .select_from(tbls.em_configs)
            .where(
                sa.and_(
                    tbls.em_configs.c.id.not_in(ignore_ids),
                    (
                        (tbls.em_configs.c.grid_config_id == component_id) |
                        (tbls.em_configs.c.generation_config_id == component_id) |
                        (tbls.em_configs.c.cs_config_id == component_id) |
                        (tbls.em_configs.c.modeldata_config_id == component_id) |
                        (tbls.em_configs.c.table_config_id == component_id)
                    )
                )
            )
        )

        # Any finance model configurations using this component must be identified
        get_fm_count_stmt = (
            sa.select(sa.func.count())
            .select_from(tbls.fm_configs)
            .where(
                sa.and_(
                    tbls.fm_configs.c.id.not_in(ignore_ids),
                    (
                        (tbls.fm_configs.c.financedata_config_id == component_id) |
                        (tbls.fm_configs.c.table_config_id == component_id)
                    )
                )
            )
        )

        # Any metamodels using this component directly must be identified
        get_mm_count_stmt = (
            sa.select(sa.func.count())
            .select_from(tbls.metamodels)
            .where(
                sa.and_(
                    tbls.metamodels.c.id.not_in(ignore_ids),
                    (
                        (tbls.metamodels.c.table_config_id == component_id) |
                        (tbls.metamodels.c.optim_config_id == component_id)
                    )
                )
            )
        )

        # Any projects using this component directly must be identified
        get_proj_count_stmt = (
            sa.select(sa.func.count())
            .select_from(tbls.projects)
            .where(
                sa.and_(
                    tbls.projects.c.id.not_in(ignore_ids),
                    (
                        (tbls.projects.c.dsa_component_config_id == component_id) |
                        (tbls.projects.c.psa_component_config_id == component_id) |
                        (tbls.projects.c.table_config_id == component_id)
                    )
                )
            )
        )

        # All associated results must be deleted
        del_res_stmt = (
            tbls.results.delete()
            .where(tbls.results.c.component_config_id == component_id)
        )

        # And then the component will be free to delete
        del_comp_stmt = (
            tbls.component_configs.delete()
            .where(tbls.component_configs.c.id == component_id)
        )

        with read_transaction(self._get_engine(writer=True)) as conn:
            for trial_stmt in (
                get_em_count_stmt,
                get_fm_count_stmt,
                get_mm_count_stmt,
                get_proj_count_stmt
            ):
                count = conn.execute(trial_stmt).scalar()
                if count:
                    raise DependentObjectsExistError(f'Cannot delete - dependents exist for component {component_id}')

            # Proceed with deletion
            conn.execute(del_res_stmt)
            conn.execute(del_comp_stmt)
            conn.commit()

    @override
    def delete_component(
        self, 
        component_id: str | SequenceNotStr[str],
        ignore_ids: list[str] = []
    ) -> list[str]:

        if isinstance(component_id, str):
            component_id = [component_id, ]

        failures = []
        for id in component_id:
            try:
                self._delete_one_component(id)
            except DependentObjectsExistError:
                failures.append(id)

        return failures

    @overload
    def get_component_metadata(
        self,
        component_id: str,
        metadata_ids: str | SequenceNotStr[str]
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        ...

    @overload 
    def get_component_metadata(
        self,
        component_id: SequenceNotStr[str],
        metadata_ids: str | SequenceNotStr[str]
    ) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
        ...

    def get_component_metadata(
        self,
        component_id: str | SequenceNotStr[str],
        metadata_ids: str | SequenceNotStr[str]
    ) -> dict[str, Any] | dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
        """Get columns of the components table for a component (or components) without constructing them.

        Args:
            component_id: Id(s) of the component(s).
            metadata_ids: Name(s) of the metadata fields wanted.

        Returns:
            Dictionary of the metadata, or a dictionary of these by id.
        """
        is_single_id = isinstance(component_id, (str, bytes))
        component_id = [component_id] if is_single_id else list(component_id)

        cols = [metadata_ids] if isinstance(metadata_ids, (str, bytes)) else list(metadata_ids)

        if not component_id:
            return {}

        pk_col = list(self._table.primary_key.columns)[0]
        select_cols = [self._table.c[col_name] for col_name in cols]

        fetch_cols = list({pk_col, *select_cols})
        stmt = sa.select(*fetch_cols).where(pk_col.in_(component_id))
        with read_transaction(self._get_engine()) as conn:
            results = conn.execute(stmt).mappings().all()

        mapped_data = {
            row[pk_col.name]: {c: row[c] for c in cols} for row in results
        }

        if is_single_id:
            return mapped_data.get(component_id[0], {})

        return mapped_data

    @override
    def set_component_metadata(
        self, 
        component_id: str | SequenceNotStr[str], 
        metadata_id: str, 
        metadata_value: Any,
        increment_revision: bool = True,
        project_id: Optional[str] = None,
    ):

        pk_col = list(self._table.primary_key.columns)[0]
        update_col = self._table.c[metadata_id]

        if isinstance(component_id, str):
            stmt = (
                sa.update(self._table)
                .where(pk_col == component_id)
            )
        else:
            stmt = (
                sa.update(self._table)
                .where(pk_col.in_(component_id))
            )

        if increment_revision and not metadata_id == 'revision':
            changed = sa.or_(
                update_col.is_distinct_from(metadata_value)
            )
            stmt = stmt.values(
                revision= sa.case(
                    (changed, self._table.c.revision + 1),
                    else_ = self._table.c.revision
                ),
                **{update_col.name: metadata_value}
            )
        else:
            stmt = stmt.values(
                **{update_col.name: metadata_value}
            )

        with write_transaction(self._get_engine(writer = True)) as conn:
            conn.execute(stmt)
            if project_id:
                # Cache invalidate by touching the project table
                conn.execute(sa.update(tbls.projects).where(tbls.projects.c.id == project_id).values(id = project_id))

        return

    def increment_revision(
        self,
        component_id: str | SequenceNotStr[str]
    ):
        """Increment revision by one on nominated components"""
        pk_col = list(self._table.primary_key.columns)[0]

        if isinstance(component_id, str):
            stmt = (
                sa.update(self._table)
                .where(pk_col == component_id)
            )
        else:
            stmt = (
                sa.update(self._table)
                .where(pk_col.in_(component_id))
            )
        stmt = stmt.values(revision = self._table.c.revision + 1)

        with write_transaction(self._get_engine(writer = True)) as conn:
            conn.execute(stmt)

        try:
            self.invalidate_cache_for_component(component_id)
        except AttributeError:
            pass

        return

def get_lightweight_component(
    self, component_id: str | SequenceNotStr[str]
) -> LightweightNewsegsComponent | SequenceNotStr[LightweightNewsegsComponent]:
    """Get the lightweight description of a component (or components).

    Contains the information needed to display the component, without constructing it.

    Args:
        component_id: Id(s) of the component(s).

    Returns:
        The lightweight component(s).
    """
    prevstate = RevisionNotifierMixin._set_notification_state('disabled')
    try:
        is_sequence = False
        if isinstance(component_id, str):
            stmt = (
                sa.select(*self._lightweight_component_columns)
                .where(self._table.c.id == component_id)
            )
        else:
            is_sequence = True
            stmt = (
                sa.select(*self._lightweight_component_columns)
                .where(self._table.c.id.in_(component_id))
            )
        with read_transaction(self._get_engine()) as conn:
            rows = conn.execute(stmt).fetchall()

        reconstructed_components = [self._reconstruct_lightweight_component(row) for row in rows]
    finally:
        RevisionNotifierMixin._set_notification_state(prevstate)

    if not is_sequence:
        return reconstructed_components[0]
    compmap = {x.id:x for x in reconstructed_components}
    return [compmap[x] for x in component_id]

@override
def upsert_component(
    self, 
    component: NewsegsComponent | SequenceNotStr[NewsegsComponent], 
    force: bool = False,
    tbl: Optional[sa.Table] = None,
    project_id: Optional[str] = None,
) -> None:
    """Insert or update a component, or components, in the store.

    A component is written if it is not present, or if its revision differs from the saved revision (or `force`).

    Args:
        component: The component or components.
        force: Write the components even if their revisions have not changed.
        tbl: The table to write to; the table of the provider by default.
        project_id: Project whose cache to invalidate if the upsert changes a table.
    """
    if tbl is None:
        tbl = self._table
    component = self._expand_component_sequence(component)

    if len(component) == 0:
        return

    current_revisions = {x.id: x.revision for x in component}
    uids = list(current_revisions.keys())

    # Get saved revision if exists
    stmt = (
        sa.select(
            tbl.c.id,
            tbl.c.revision
        )
        .where(tbl.c.id.in_(uids))
    )
    with read_transaction(self._get_engine()) as conn:
        rows = conn.execute(stmt).fetchall()

    saved_revisions = {x.id: x.revision for x in rows}
    existing_uids = set(saved_revisions.keys())
    new_inserts = [x for x in uids if x not in existing_uids]
    if not force:
        requires_update = [x for x in existing_uids if current_revisions[x] != saved_revisions[x]]
        # TODO: Remove this logic - all revision handling should be outside of the provider
        # If the object exists and has a matching version number but its children have been modified
        # then we do a simple bump of the revision number to indicate that downstream results are stale
        requires_revision_increment = []
        # for comp in component:
        #     if comp.id not in new_inserts and comp.id not in requires_update:
        #         if comp.chain_modified:
        #             requires_revision_increment.append(comp.id)
        #             comp.revision += 1
        #             # Update the table config revision if components have been modified.
        #             if hasattr(comp, 'table_config'):
        #                 if not comp.table_config.modified:
        #                     comp.table_config.revision += 1
    else:
        requires_update = existing_uids
        requires_revision_increment = []

    requires_data = set(requires_update)
    requires_data.update(set(new_inserts))

    requires_sync = copy.copy(requires_data)
    requires_sync.update(set(requires_revision_increment))

    # First, do the updates, then do the inserts
    for cmp in component:
        if cmp.id in requires_sync:
            # TODO: Consider whether to set a rollback here in case we can't access DB

            #### Save out all child components ####
            self.upsert_children(cmp, force = force)

            cmp.syncronise()

    cmpdata = {cmp.id: self._component_to_table_data(cmp) for cmp in component if cmp.id in requires_data}

    revdata = {cmp.id: {'id': cmp.id, 'revision': cmp.revision,} for cmp in component if cmp.id in requires_revision_increment}

    update_payload = [cmpdata[x] for x in requires_update]
    insert_payload = [cmpdata[x] for x in new_inserts]
    rev_payload = [revdata[x] for x in requires_revision_increment]

    if not (update_payload or insert_payload):
        return

    with write_transaction(self._get_engine(writer = True)) as conn:
        if rev_payload:
            # Cannot use 'id' as the bindparam - rename it
            rev_payload = [{'b_id': x.pop('id'), **x} for x in rev_payload]
            rev_stmt = sa.update(tbl).where(tbl.c.id == sa.bindparam('b_id'))
            conn.execute(rev_stmt, rev_payload)

        if update_payload:
            # Cannot use 'id' as the bindparam - rename it
            update_payload = [{'b_id': x.pop('id'), **x} for x in update_payload]
            update_stmt = sa.update(tbl).where(tbl.c.id == sa.bindparam('b_id'))
            conn.execute(update_stmt, update_payload)

        if insert_payload:
            insert_stmt = tbl.insert()
            conn.execute(insert_stmt, insert_payload)

        if project_id and (rev_payload or update_payload or insert_payload):
            # Cache invalidate by touching the project table
            conn.execute(sa.update(tbls.projects).where(tbls.projects.c.id == project_id).values(id = project_id))

    logger.debug(
        'Inserted %d components into table %s: %s',
        len(insert_payload),
        self._table.name,
        [x.get('id', str(x)) for x in insert_payload]
    )
    logger.debug(
        'Updated %d components in table %s: %s',
        len(update_payload),
        self._table.name,
        [x.get('b_id', str(x)) for x in update_payload]
    )
    logger.debug(
        'Revised %d components in table %s: %s',
        len(rev_payload),
        self._table.name,
        [x.get('b_id', str(x)) for x in rev_payload]
    )

class FromDatabaseNewsegsEMProvider(FromDatabaseNewsegsComponentProvider):
    """Provider and store of NewSEGS Energy Models (the `em_configs` table), with the modules and data that they own.
    """
    _table = tbls.em_configs

    _lightweight_component_columns = tuple(
        tbls.em_configs.columns[x] for x in (
            'id',

            'label',
            'model_type',

            'modeldata_config_id',
            'table_config_id',
            'grid_config_id',
            'generation_config_id',
            'cs_config_id',

            'revision'
        )
    )

    def _create_component_provider(self) -> NewsegsComponentManagerInterface:
        return FromDatabaseNewsegsComponentProvider(self._get_engine)

    def __init__(
        self, *args, 
        component_provider: Optional[NewsegsComponentManagerInterface] = None, 
        **kwargs
    ):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self._component_provider = component_provider if component_provider else self._create_component_provider()

    @override
    def _assign_updated_child_uids(self, obj, row):
        super()._assign_updated_child_uids(obj, row)
        if isinstance(obj, NewsegsModelInterface):
            obj._component_ids['grid'] = row.grid_config_id
            obj._component_ids['generation'] = row.generation_config_id
            obj._component_ids['consumption_storage'] = row.cs_config_id
            obj._component_ids['table_config'] = row.table_config_id
        return obj

    @override
    def _reattach_children(self, obj):
        r0 = obj.revision
        obj = super()._reattach_children(obj)
        obj.reattach_components(self._component_provider)
        if obj.revision != r0:
            raise ValueError('Model revision incremented during subcomponent attachment - from {r0} to {obj.revision}')
        return obj

    @override
    def _reconstruct_lightweight_component(self, row):
        metadata = dict(row._mapping)
        revision = metadata.pop('revision')
        metadata['name'] = metadata.pop('label')
        child_ids = [
            metadata.pop(x) for x in (
                'modeldata_config_id',
                'table_config_id',
                'grid_config_id',
                'generation_config_id',
                'cs_config_id',
            )
        ]
        child_components = {
            k:v for k, v in zip(
                (
                    'model_data',
                    'table_config',
                    'grid',
                    'generation',
                    'consumption_storage'
                ),
                self._component_provider.get_lightweight_component(child_ids)
            )
        }
        metadata.update(child_components)
        comp = LightweightNewsegsModel.from_dict(metadata)
        comp.revision = revision
        comp._syncronise()
        return comp

    # REVIEW (unreferenced): no references to `get_lightweight_em` found in src/, scripts/ or data/.
    def get_lightweight_em(
            self, model_id: str | SequenceNotStr[str]
        ) -> LightweightNewsegsModel | SequenceNotStr[LightweightNewsegsModel]:
        """Get the lightweight description of a NewSEGS Energy Model (or models).

        Args:
            model_id: Id(s) of the NewSEGS Energy Model(s).

        Returns:
            The lightweight model(s).
        """
        return self.get_lightweight_component(model_id)

    @override
    def _component_to_table_data(self, component: NewsegsComponent) -> dict:
        if not isinstance(component, NewsegsModelInterface):
            return super()._component_to_table_data(component)
        if component.modified:
            raise ValueError(f'{component.id} is being upserted in a modified state')
        return energy_model_to_raw_table_data(component)

    @override
    def upsert_component(
        self,
        component: NewsegsComponent | SequenceNotStr[NewsegsComponent], 
        force: bool = False,
        tbl: sa.Table | None = None,
        project_id: Optional[str] = None
    ) -> None:
        if isinstance(component, NewsegsModelInterface) or isinstance(component, Sequence) and all(isinstance(x, NewsegsModelInterface) for x in component):
            return super().upsert_component(component, force, tbl, project_id = project_id)
        else:
            return self._component_provider.upsert_component(component, force, tbl, project_id = project_id)

    @override
    def _delete_one_component(
        self, 
        component_id: str,
        ignore_ids: list[str] = [],
    ) -> None:
        # Assume that we are dealing only with members of the em_configs table

        # Any metamodel configurations using this model must be identified
        get_mm_count_stmt = (
            sa.select(sa.func.count())
            .select_from(tbls.metamodels)
            .where(
                sa.and_(
                    tbls.metamodels.c.id.not_in(ignore_ids),
                    (
                        (tbls.metamodels.c.em_config_id == component_id)
                    )
                )
            )
        )

        # Child components should be identified and subsequently deleted, where appropriate
        get_child_component_id_stmt = (
            sa.select(
                self._table.c.grid_config_id,
                self._table.c.generation_config_id,
                self._table.c.cs_config_id,
                self._table.c.modeldata_config_id,
                self._table.c.table_config_id,
            )
            .where(self._table.c.id == component_id)
        )

        del_stmt = (
            self._table.delete()
            .where(self._table.c.id == component_id)
        )

        # use of a writer in a read transaction deliberate here
        child_ids = []
        with read_transaction(self._get_engine(writer = True)) as conn:
            for trial_stmt in (
                get_mm_count_stmt,
            ):
                count = conn.execute(trial_stmt).scalar()
                if count:
                    raise DependentObjectsExistError(f'Cannot delete - dependents exist for energy model {component_id}')

            # Get child ids
            row = conn.execute(get_child_component_id_stmt).fetchone()
            if row:
                child_ids = [x for x in row if x]

            # Delete model
            conn.execute(del_stmt)
            conn.commit()

        # Delete children
        _ = self._component_provider.delete_component(child_ids)

    def _create_component_provider(self) -> NewsegsComponentManagerInterface:

    def __init__(
        self, *args, 
        component_provider: Optional[NewsegsComponentManagerInterface] = None, 
        **kwargs
    ):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self._component_provider = component_provider if component_provider else self._create_component_provider()

    def _assign_updated_child_uids(self, obj, row):

    @override
    def _reattach_children(self, obj):

        return obj

    @override
    def _reconstruct_lightweight_component(self, row):

        child_ids = [
            metadata.pop(x) for x in (
                'financedata_config_id',

            )
        ]
        child_components = {
            k:v for k, v in zip(
                (
                    'finance_data',
                    'table_config',
                ),
                self._component_provider.get_lightweight_component(child_ids)
            )
        }
        metadata.update(child_components)
        comp = LightweightNewsegsFinance.from_dict(metadata)
        comp.revision = revision
        comp._syncronise()
        return comp

    # REVIEW (unreferenced): no references to `get_lightweight_fm` found in src/, scripts/ or data/.
    def get_lightweight_fm(
        self, finance_id: str | SequenceNotStr[str]
    ) -> LightweightNewsegsFinance | SequenceNotStr[LightweightNewsegsFinance]:
        """Get the lightweight description of a finance model (or models).

        Args:
            finance_id: Id(s) of the finance model(s).

        Returns:
            The lightweight finance model(s).

    @override
    def _component_to_table_data(self, component: NewsegsComponent) -> dict:
        if not isinstance(component, NewsegsFinanceInterface):
            return super()._component_to_table_data(component)
        if component.modified:
            raise ValueError(f'{component.id} is being upserted in a modified state')
        return finance_model_to_raw_table_data(component) # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]

    @override
    def upsert_component(
        self,
        component: NewsegsComponent | SequenceNotStr[NewsegsComponent], 
        force: bool = False,
        tbl: sa.Table | None = None,
        project_id: Optional[str] = None
    ) -> None:
        if isinstance(component, NewsegsFinanceInterface) or isinstance(component, Sequence) and all(isinstance(x, NewsegsFinanceInterface) for x in component):
            return super().upsert_component(component, force, tbl, project_id = project_id)
        else:
            return self._component_provider.upsert_component(component, force, tbl, project_id = project_id)

    @override
    def _delete_one_component(
        self, 
        component_id: str,
        ignore_ids: list[str] = [],
    ) -> None:
        # Assume that we are dealing only with members of the fm_configs table

        # Any metamodel configurations using this model must be identified
        get_mm_count_stmt = (
            sa.select(sa.func.count())
            .select_from(tbls.metamodels)
            .where(
                sa.and_(
                    tbls.metamodels.c.id.not_in(ignore_ids),
                    (
                        (tbls.metamodels.c.fm_config_id == component_id)
                    )
                )
            )
        )

        # Child components should be identified and subsequently deleted, where appropriate
        get_child_component_id_stmt = (
            sa.select(
                self._table.c.financedata_config_id,
                self._table.c.table_config_id,
            )
            .where(self._table.c.id == component_id)
        )

        del_stmt = (
            self._table.delete()
            .where(self._table.c.id == component_id)
        )

        # Deliberately use writer in read transaction
        child_ids = []
        with read_transaction(self._get_engine(writer = True)) as conn:
            for trial_stmt in (
                get_mm_count_stmt,
            ):
                count = conn.execute(trial_stmt).scalar()
                if count:
                    raise DependentObjectsExistError(f'Cannot delete - dependents exist for energy model {component_id}')

            # Get child ids
            row = conn.execute(get_child_component_id_stmt).fetchone()
            if row:
                child_ids = [x for x in row if x]

            # Delete model
            conn.execute(del_stmt)
            conn.commit()

        # Delete children
        _ = self._component_provider.delete_component(child_ids)
