def psa_ce_plane_plot(
    pairwise: pd.DataFrame,
    discount: str = 'discounted',
    comparator: str = 'Comparator',
    reference: str = 'Reference',
    color_index: int = 0,
):
    """Plot the cost-effectiveness plane of a pairwise comparison of a whole-project PSA.

    Each draw is a point of its incremental benefits and costs. Below the line of equal increments the comparator
    has the greater net present value; the proportion of draws below it is shown.

    Args:
        pairwise: The pairwise comparison, from `psa.psa_pairwise`.
        discount: Whether to plot the `discounted` or `undiscounted` increments.
        comparator: Label of the comparator.
        reference: Label of the reference.
        color_index: Index of the color of the comparator in `COMPARATOR_COLORS`.

    Returns:
        The figure.
    """
    cost, benefit = f'incremental_total_costs_{discount}', f'incremental_total_benefits_{discount}'
    if pairwise.empty or cost not in pairwise.columns:
        return _empty_psa_figure()
    sampled = pairwise.loc[~pairwise['deterministic'].astype(bool), :]
    if sampled.empty:
        return _empty_psa_figure()
    det = pairwise.loc[pairwise['deterministic'].astype(bool), :]
    color = COMPARATOR_COLORS[color_index % len(COMPARATOR_COLORS)]
    x = sampled[benefit].to_numpy(dtype = float)
    y = sampled[cost].to_numpy(dtype = float)
    p_ce = float(np.mean(x - y > 0))

    fig = go.Figure()
    if not det.empty:
        # Drawn first and open, so that draws close to it remain visible
        fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
            x = det[benefit], y = det[cost], mode = 'markers',
            marker = dict(color = _PSA_FRONTIER_COLOR, size = 14, symbol = 'diamond-open', line = dict(width = 2)),
            name = 'Deterministic',
            hovertemplate = 'Deterministic<br>Incremental benefits: %{x:,.0f}<br>Incremental costs: %{y:,.0f}<extra></extra>',
        ))
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x = x, y = y, mode = 'markers',
        marker = dict(color = color, size = 8, opacity = 0.5, line = dict(color = 'white', width = 1)),
        name = 'Draws',
        customdata = sampled['draw'],
        hovertemplate = 'Draw %{customdata}<br>Incremental benefits: %{x:,.0f}<br>Incremental costs: %{y:,.0f}<extra></extra>',
    ))
    lo = float(np.nanmin(np.concatenate([x, y, [0.]])))
    hi = float(np.nanmax(np.concatenate([x, y, [0.]])))
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x = [lo, hi], y = [lo, hi], mode = 'lines',
        line = dict(color = _PSA_REFERENCE_LINE_COLOR, width = 1, dash = 'dot'),
        name = 'Equal increments', hoverinfo = 'skip',
    ))
    fig.add_hline(y = 0, line = dict(color = _PSA_REFERENCE_LINE_COLOR, width = 1))
    fig.add_vline(x = 0, line = dict(color = _PSA_REFERENCE_LINE_COLOR, width = 1))
    fig.add_annotation(
        text = f'Probability {comparator} has the greater NPV: {p_ce:.1%}',
        xref = 'paper', yref = 'paper', x = 0.01, y = 0.99, xanchor = 'left', yanchor = 'top',
        showarrow = False, bgcolor = 'rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.8)',
    )
    _psa_layout(
        fig, f'Cost-effectiveness plane: {comparator} vs {reference} ({discount})',
        f'Incremental total benefits ({discount})', f'Incremental total costs ({discount})',
    )
    return fig

def psa_marginal_plot(
    marginals: Mapping[str, object],
    variable: str,
    statistic: str,
    color_indexes: Mapping[str, int] | None = None,
    title: str | None = None,
):
    """Plot the marginal (univariate) sensitivity of a statistic of a PSA to the draws of a variable.

    For each comparator, the draws as points, the mean of the statistic by quantile group of the variable as a
    line, with a band of the 5th to 95th percentiles of each group. The Spearman rank correlation, the slope of the
    least-squares line and its R² label the comparator in the legend.

    Args:
        marginals: The marginal sensitivity (from `psa.psa_marginal`), by the label of the comparator.
        variable: Label of the variable.
        statistic: The statistic, for the label of the axis.
        color_indexes: Index of the color of each comparator in `COMPARATOR_COLORS`; by default the order of `marginals`.
        title: Title of the plot; by default from the variable and statistic.

    Returns:
        The figure.
    """
    marginals = {k: v for k, v in marginals.items() if len(v.points)}
    if not marginals:
        return _empty_psa_figure(f'No draws of {variable} in these PSA results')
    color_indexes = color_indexes or {k: i for i, k in enumerate(marginals)}
    label = PSA_ALL_STATISTIC_LABELS.get(statistic, statistic)

    fig = go.Figure()
    for i, (comparator, m) in enumerate(marginals.items()):
        color = _comparator_color(color_indexes, comparator, i)
        fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
            x = m.points['x'], y = m.points['y'], mode = 'markers',
            marker = dict(color = color, size = 6, opacity = 0.35),
            name = f'{comparator} - draws', legendgroup = comparator, showlegend = False,
            hovertemplate = f'<b>{comparator}</b><br>{variable}: %{{x:,.3g}}<br>{label}: %{{y:,.0f}}<extra></extra>',
        ))
        binned = m.binned
        if len(binned) > 1:
            fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
                x = np.concatenate([binned['x'], binned['x'][::-1]]),
                y = np.concatenate([binned['y_upper'], binned['y_lower'][::-1]]),
                fill = 'toself', fillcolor = color, opacity = 0.12, line = dict(width = 0),
                name = f'{comparator} - 5th to 95th percentile', legendgroup = comparator, showlegend = False,
                hoverinfo = 'skip',
            ))
        fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
            x = binned['x'], y = binned['y'], mode = 'lines+markers',
            line = dict(color = color, width = 2), marker = dict(color = color, size = 8),
            name = f'{comparator} ({psa_marginal_summary(m)})', legendgroup = comparator,
            customdata = binned['count'],

def create_dsa_input_vector_parameter_input(
    parameter_names: str | Sequence[str] | OrderedDict[str, Sequence[str]],
    parameter_types: Sequence[variable.PARAMETER_TYPE],
    type_id: str,
    key: str,
    section: str | None = None,
):
    """Create the inputs of the parameters of a vector variable.

    Args:
        parameter_names: Names of the parameters.
        parameter_types: Types of the parameters.
        type_id: The type field of the component ids.
        key: The interface key of the variable.
        section: The interface section of the variable.

    Returns:
        The inputs.
    """
    are_scalars = [i for i, x in enumerate(parameter_types) if x == 'scalar']
    are_vectors = [i for i, x in enumerate(parameter_types) if x == 'vector']
    are_matrices = [i for i, x in enumerate(parameter_types) if x == 'matrix']

    if isinstance(parameter_names, OrderedDict):
        param_class = list(parameter_names.keys())
    elif isinstance(parameter_names, str):
        param_class = [parameter_names]
    else:
        param_class = parameter_names

    def make_input(placeholder: Any):
        return dbc.Input(type = 'number', debounce = True, placeholder = placeholder, class_name = 'numeric-input') # pyright: ignore[reportCallIssue]

    def make_inputgroup(label: str, placeholder: Any):
        return dbc.InputGroup([
            dbc.InputGroupText(label+':'), # pyright: ignore[reportCallIssue]
            make_input(placeholder)
        ]) # pyright: ignore[reportCallIssue]

    rval = []
    for idx in are_scalars:
        rval += [make_inputgroup(str(param_class[idx]), param_class[idx])]

    if not isinstance(parameter_names, OrderedDict):
        for idx in are_vectors:
            rval += [html.Div([
                html.P(param_class[idx]),
                make_inputgroup('Value[0]', '[0]')
            ])]
    else:
        for idx in are_vectors:
            rval += [html.Div([
                html.Table([
                    html.Thead([
                        html.Th(
                            param_class[idx]     
                        )
                    ]),
                    html.Tbody([
                        html.Tr(html.Td(make_inputgroup(x, x))) for x in parameter_names[param_class[idx]]
                    ])
                ])
            ])]

    for idx in are_matrices:
        # TODO: Make this responsive to a variable's dimensions
        NVAL = 2
        rval += [html.Div([
                html.Table([
                    html.Thead([
                        html.Th(
                            param_class[idx],
                            colSpan = NVAL
                        )
                    ]),
                    html.Tbody([
                        html.Tr([
                            html.Td(make_input(f'[{x},{y}]'))
                            for y in range(NVAL)
                        ])
                        for x in range(NVAL)
                    ]),
                ])
            ])]

    return rval

def create_dsa_bounds_inputs_scalar(
    bounds_type: variable.DSA_BOUNDS_TYPE,
    var: FullLightweightVariable,
    id_lower: VariableInstanceParameterComponentID | None = None,
    id_upper: VariableInstanceParameterComponentID | None = None,
):
    """Create the inputs of the lower and upper DSA bounds of a scalar variable.

    The form of the inputs depends upon the type of bound: absolute, offset, relative or interval.

    Args:
        bounds_type: How the DSA bounds are specified.
        var: The variable.
        id_lower: Identification of the lower bound's input; by default the focussed configuration's.
        id_upper: Identification of the upper bound's input; by default the focussed configuration's.

    Returns:
        The inputs.
    """
    variable_id_lower = id_lower if id_lower is not None else VariableInstanceParameterComponentID.from_lightweight_variable(
        var,
        type = 'single-input-config',
        supersection = 'dsa',
        purpose = 'bound-lower',
    )

    variable_id_upper = id_upper if id_upper is not None else VariableInstanceParameterComponentID.from_lightweight_variable(
        var,
        type = 'single-input-config',
        supersection = 'dsa',
        purpose = 'bound-upper',
    )

    match bounds_type:
        case 'absolute' | 'relative' | 'offset':
            if bounds_type == 'relative':
                step_size = 0.05
            else:
                step_size = float(f'{var.last_deterministic_value / 10:2g}')
                if step_size == 0:
                    step_size = 0.05

            return [
                dbc.InputGroup([
                    dbc.InputGroupText('Lower:'), # pyright: ignore[reportCallIssue]

                    create_numeric_variable_parameter_input(
                        variable_id_lower,
                        value = var.dsa_lower, # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]
                        step = step_size
                    ),
                ]
                ), # type: ignore
                dbc.InputGroup([
                    dbc.InputGroupText('Upper:'), # pyright: ignore[reportCallIssue]
                    create_numeric_variable_parameter_input(
                        variable_id_upper,
                        value = var.dsa_upper, # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]
                        step = step_size
                    ),
                ]
                ),
            ]
        case 'interval':
            return [
                dbc.InputGroup([
                    dbc.InputGroupText('Confidence:'), # pyright: ignore[reportCallIssue]
                    create_numeric_variable_parameter_input(
                        variable_id_lower,
                        value = var.dsa_lower, # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]
                    )
                ])
            ]

def create_dsa_input_parts(
    var: FullLightweightVariable,
    id_for: Callable[..., VariableInstanceParameterComponentID] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, list]:
    """Create the inputs of a Variable's DSA settings: its distribution's parameters, its bound type and its bounds.

    Args:
        var: The Variable.
        id_for: Makes the identification of an input from its purpose (`group-value`, `group-dsaboundtype`,
            `group-dsa-bound-lower` or `group-dsa-bound-upper`) and parameter index, for a group other than the
            focussed configuration's. By default, the inputs are the focussed configuration's, with their usual ids,
            and the bounds are held in the `bounds-container` which `update_dsa_input_contents` redraws.

    Returns:
        `parameters`, `bound_type_selector` and `bounds`, each a list of components.
    """
    distribution = var.distribution if isinstance(var, FullLightweightVariable) else var.distribution.distribution
    if distribution not in _DSA_PARAMETERS:
        raise ValueError(f'Distribution {distribution} not currently supported')
    permitted = ['absolute', 'relative', 'offset'] + ([] if 'constant' in distribution else ['interval'])

    parameters = [
        _create_numeric_inputgroup_from_var(
            var, label, index, stepscale = stepscale,
            min = var.interface_min if limited else 0, max = var.interface_max if limited else None,
            supersection = 'dsa',
            variable_id = id_for('group-value', index) if id_for else None,
        )
        for label, index, stepscale, limited in _DSA_PARAMETERS[distribution]
    ]
    selector = create_dsa_bound_type_selector(
        permitted, var.dsa_bounds_type, var, # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]
        id_ = id_for('group-dsaboundtype') if id_for else None,
    )
    if id_for:
        bounds = create_dsa_bounds_inputs_scalar(
            var.dsa_bounds_type, var, # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]
            id_lower = id_for('group-dsa-bound-lower'), id_upper = id_for('group-dsa-bound-upper'),
        )
    else:
        bounds_container_id = VariableInstanceParameterComponentID.from_variable(
            var, type = 'input-component', supersection = 'dsa', purpose = 'bounds-container'
        )
        bounds = [html.Span(create_dsa_bounds_inputs_scalar(var.dsa_bounds_type, var), id = bounds_container_id.as_dict())] # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]
    return {'parameters': parameters, 'bound_type_selector': selector, 'bounds': bounds}

def compose_dsa_input(
    header_component,
    var: variable.Variable | FullLightweightVariable,
    summary_contents: list | None = None,
    n_configurations: int = 1,
):
    """Compose the DSA input of a variable: its toggle, and a row which opens to its group editor.

    The row's summary holds the header, and below it a summary of the groups (see
    `dsa_group_editor.create_dsa_sharing_summary_contents`), which its refresh trigger redraws. Opening the row builds
    the editor (`dsa_group_editor.create_dsa_group_editor_contents`), which holds the focussed configuration's inputs
    and, with several configurations, the other groups'. The row has a hidden anchor, so that the toggle reaches
    `react_to_input_change` while the editor's inputs aren't built (see `input_components.create_lazy_input_details`).

    Args:
        header_component: The header.
        var: The variable.
        summary_contents: The summary of the groups.
        n_configurations: The number of configurations of the project; with several, the row can move them.

    Returns:
        The input.
    """
    def row_id(type_: str, purpose: str):
        return VariableInstanceParameterComponentID.from_variable(var, type = type_, supersection = 'dsa', purpose = purpose) # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]

    if var.dsa_selected:
        cn = 'dsa-input-single-value-block'
    else:
        cn = 'dsa-input-single-value-block deselected'

    stores = [
        dcc.Store(id = row_id('input-group-config-update-trigger', 'trigger').as_dict()),
        dcc.Store(id = row_id('variable-summary-refresh-trigger', 'trigger').as_dict()),
    ]
    if n_configurations > 1:
        stores.append(dcc.Store(id = row_id('group-move-request', 'move').as_dict()))

    return html.Div([
        daq.ToggleSwitch(
            #vertical = True,
            className = 'dsa-toggle',
            size = 30,
            value = var.dsa_selected,
            id = row_id('input-toggle', 'dsa-active').as_dict(),
        ),
        html.Details([
            html.Summary(
                [
                    html.Div(header_component, id = row_id('single-input-header', 'header').as_dict(), className = 'dsa-configuration-header'),
                    html.Div(
                        summary_contents or [],
                        id = row_id('variable-sharing-summary', 'summary').as_dict(),
                        className = 'variable-sharing-summary dsa-sharing-summary',
                    ),
                ],
                className='dsa-configuration-summary',
                id = row_id('input-summary', 'group-editor-toggle').as_dict(),
            ),
            html.Div([], id = row_id('input-group-editor', 'editor').as_dict()),
            dcc.Input(id = row_id('single-input-config', 'editor-anchor').as_dict(), type = 'hidden'),
        ],
        className = 'group-editor-details dsa-group-editor-details',
        ),
        *stores,
    ],
    className=cn,
    id = row_id('input-component', 'input-group-container').as_dict(),
    )

def create_dsa_header(

    """Create the header of the DSA input of a variable.

    Args:

    is_lvar = isinstance(var, FullLightweightVariable)
    fmt = dsa_value_formatter(var)

def create_psa_header(
    var: variable.Variable | FullLightweightVariable,
):
    """Create the header of the PSA input of a variable.

    Args:
        var: The variable.

    Returns:
        The header.
    """
    is_lvar = isinstance(var, FullLightweightVariable)
    dist = var.distribution if is_lvar else var.distribution.distribution
    if dist == 'constant':
        fmt = _autoformat
    else:
        if is_lvar:
            dp = var.formatter_dp
            if dp is not None:
                fmt = _default_formatter_scalar(dp)
            else:
                fmt = _autoformat
        else:
            fmt = var.value_formatter

    if var.unit == '':
        label = var.label
    else:
        label = f'{var.label} ({var.unit})'

    if is_lvar:
        hdr = create_psa_input_scalar_numeric_header(
            label,
            fmt(var.last_deterministic_value),
            fmt(var.last_std) if var.last_std is not None else '-',
            fmt(var.psa_ci_lower) if var.psa_ci_lower is not None else '-',
            fmt(var.psa_ci_upper) if var.psa_ci_upper is not None else '-'
        )
    else:
        ci = var.get_confidence_interval(0.95)
        hdr = create_psa_input_scalar_numeric_header(
            label,
            fmt(var.get_deterministic_value()),
            fmt(var.get_std()),
            fmt(ci[0]),
            fmt(ci[1])
        )

    return hdr

def compose_psa_input(
    header_component,
    var: variable.Variable | FullLightweightVariable,
    summary_contents: list | None = None,
    n_configurations: int = 1,
):
    """Compose the PSA input of a variable: its toggle, and a row which opens to its group editor.

    As the DSA input (see `compose_dsa_input`): the row's summary holds the header and a summary of the groups (see
    `psa_group_editor.create_psa_sharing_summary_contents`), and opening it builds the editor
    (`psa_group_editor.create_psa_group_editor_contents`), with the distribution and the focussed configuration's inputs.

    Args:
        header_component: The header.
        var: The variable.
        summary_contents: The summary of the groups.
        n_configurations: The number of configurations of the project; with several, the row can move them.

    Returns:
        The input.
    """
    def row_id(type_: str, purpose: str):
        return VariableInstanceParameterComponentID.from_variable(var, type = type_, supersection = 'psa', purpose = purpose) # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]

    if var.psa_selected:
        cn = 'psa-input-single-value-block'
    else:
        cn = 'psa-input-single-value-block deselected'

    stores = [
        dcc.Store(id = row_id('input-group-config-update-trigger', 'trigger').as_dict()),
        dcc.Store(id = row_id('variable-summary-refresh-trigger', 'trigger').as_dict()),
    ]
    if n_configurations > 1:
        stores.append(dcc.Store(id = row_id('group-move-request', 'move').as_dict()))

    return html.Div([
        daq.ToggleSwitch(
            className = 'psa-toggle',
            size = 30,
            value = var.psa_selected,
            id = row_id('input-toggle', 'psa-active').as_dict(),
        ),
        html.Details([
            html.Summary(
                [
                    html.Div(header_component, id = row_id('single-input-header', 'header').as_dict(), className = 'psa-configuration-header'),
                    html.Div(
                        summary_contents or [],
                        id = row_id('variable-sharing-summary', 'summary').as_dict(),
                        className = 'variable-sharing-summary psa-sharing-summary',
                    ),
                ],
                className = 'psa-configuration-summary',
                id = row_id('input-summary', 'group-editor-toggle').as_dict(),
            ),
            html.Div([], id = row_id('input-group-editor', 'editor').as_dict()),
            dcc.Input(id = row_id('single-input-config', 'editor-anchor').as_dict(), type = 'hidden'),
        ],
        className = 'group-editor-details psa-group-editor-details',
        ),
        *stores,
    ],
    className = cn,
    id = row_id('input-component', 'input-group-container').as_dict(),
    )

def create_psa_input(
    var: FullLightweightVariable,
    summary_contents: list | None = None,

):

            `psa_group_editor.create_psa_sharing_summary_contents`).

@dataclass
class VariableComponentID(SerialisableDataclass):
    """Data to describe some component associated with a variable."""
    type: str
    purpose: str = 'variable'
    supersection: str = 'global'
    section: str = 'global'
    key: str = 'component'

    @classmethod
    def from_variable(
        cls,
        var: variable.Variable,
        type: str = 'notype',
        supersection: str = 'deterministic',
    ):
        """Create the id of a component of a variable.

        The section and key are those of the variable (the first, if it has several).

        Args:
            var: The variable.
            type: The type field of the component id.
            supersection: The supersection of the container.

        Returns:
            The id.
        """
        section = var.interface_section
        section = 'None' if section is None else section
        if not isinstance(section, str):
            # Take the first section if is a sequence
            section = section[0]
        key = var.interface_key
        if not isinstance(key, str):
            key = key[0]

        return cls(
            type = type,
            supersection = supersection,
            section = section,
            key = key,
        )

    @classmethod
    def from_lightweight_variable(
        cls,
        var: LightweightVariable,
        type: str = 'notype',

            supersection: The supersection of the container.

            The id.

        section = var.interface_section

        if not isinstance(section, str):
            # Take the first section if is a sequence
            section = section[0]
        key = var.interface_key

docs.title: Application database
docs.text:
The newsegsmodelapp Dash app stores configurations, results metadata, job requests and sessions in a SQLite database. The tables are defined with SQLAlchemy in newsegsmodelapp.backend.db.db_tables and migrated with Alembic (alembic/versions).

Large result payloads are not stored in the database: the results table records the result_file in the results store, and the database holds only the metadata needed to find it.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Dotted lines are relationships without a foreign key.
  • metamodel_variables.key_order is the position of the variable's key ({section}.{key}, without the subindex) among the metamodel's variables, so that they are loaded in the order they were saved. It is null for rows saved before it was recorded, whose order is taken from the metamodel's payload.
  • variable_configs holds the settings of a variable for each analysis in columns of their own (dsa_*, psa_*, optim_*), with its parameterisation (parameterisation_index, raw_parameter_*), the limits and formatting of its input (interface_*, formatter_dp, unit, icon_name), and the full variable in payload.
  • process_staleness has no foreign key, so that deleting a metamodel is never blocked by its staleness rows. It records, per metamodel and per process (see db_staleness.PROCESSES), when the inputs relevant to the process last changed and when the last completed run began. A process is stale when its inputs changed after its last run started.
  • metamodels.optim_config_id is the OptimComponent holding the method and statistic of optimisation. It is null for metamodels saved before it existed; they are given the default component when loaded. The bounds of optimisation are held by each variable, in the optim_min, optim_max and optim_plot_intervals columns of variable_configs.
  • variable_configs.component_version is the version of the Variable class that saved the row, null if it was saved before versions were recorded. As with the other components, the payload records the version too, and a payload newer than the app supports is rejected.
  • The times of runs are in UTC, without a timezone: created_at is filled in by SQLite, and modified_at by the app (db_tables.utc_now). The dispatcher marks a run as failed once modified_at is older than DEAD_CALCULATION_INTERVAL_SECONDS, and pruning compares both with a cutoff in UTC, so both work whatever the host's timezone. projects.modified_at is still in local time.
  • requests are created by the front end (from the actions in the app) and picked up by the dispatcher; each request is executed as one or more runs by a worker. The run carries the progress and cancellation flag that the front end polls.
  • results.request_id and results.run_id are for convenience and are deliberately not foreign keys.
  • Users, groups and read/write access to projects are planned (see the TODO in db_tables.projects) but are not yet implemented.

docs.title: Snapshot tables
docs.text:
A snapshot freezes a copy of a project - its metamodels, models, components, variables and results - so that it can be restored later. Each live table x has a snapshot_x twin whose primary key is extended with snapshot_id, and whose remaining columns are cloned from the live table (without its foreign keys). Foreign keys between snapshot tables are composite, so they refer to the rows within the same snapshot.

docs.title: Application plugins
docs.text: The application has no knowledge of any particular model. Everything specific is added by plugins: Python modules that, on import, add entries to the registries in newsegsmodelapp.registers.

docs.title: How plugins are loaded and used
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    subgraph load["On import (app, dispatcher and workers)"]
        direction TB
        fw["newsegsmodelframework.register_plugins<br/>project factories"]
        pages["plugins/pages<br/>pages and their processes"]
        models["plugins/models<br/>page configurations, contents and processing per model type"]
        comps["components<br/>input handlers"]
        fw --> pages --> models --> comps
    end
    load -->|"decorators and add_ functions fill"| reg[("registers")]
    reg --> create["create_app: validation layout and page callbacks, from PAGE_REGISTER"]
    reg --> runtime["At run time: callbacks and workers look up by key and model type"]
  1. Loading. newsegsmodelapp.register_plugins imports every module under newsegsmodelapp.plugins.pages, then every module under newsegsmodelapp.plugins.models, then the modules directly in newsegsmodelapp.components. Pages must be loaded first, since model plugins configure them. Plugins are found by walking the packages (pkgutil.walk_packages), in alphabetical order, so adding a module in the right place is all that's needed. The module is imported by app.py, the dispatcher and the workers, so that every process has the same registries. The framework's own project plugins are loaded separately, by import newsegsmodelframework.register_plugins.
  2. Registering. Importing a plugin runs its decorators (e.g. @register_input_container_content_creator) and add_ calls (e.g. add_page), which add its functions and objects to the registers. A key may be registered once for each model type: registering it again raises an error.
  3. Building the app. create_app builds the validation layout from the layouts of every page in PAGE_REGISTER, and calls each page's attach_callbacks (see Callbacks).
  4. Looking up. Callbacks and workers look up what to call by its key and the model type of the page (from the app-state store) or of the request. A model type registers only what it changes, and falls back to the defaults for the rest.

docs.title: Defaults and fallbacks
docs.text:
The first function registered for a key under a model type other than default is also registered as the default for the key. Other model types then fall back to it. Plugins are imported in alphabetical order, so the directory that provides the defaults is named aaa_default, to be imported first.

Registers Looked up by Fallbacks, in order Input container, editor and section header content creators; single input header and result content creators (supersection or key, section, model type) the default model type; the generic section (ALL); both Page layout configurations (page, model type) a copy of the page's default configuration Input handlers (purpose, component type, model type) the default model type; any component type Postprocess and table draw procedures, table getters and subindex maps, feedback graph and environment feedback artists (name, model type) the default model type Environment data sources model type none: a model type without one has no environmental feedback Run requests and procedures, postprocess and table draw requests request type none

Why aaa_default?

The directory that provides the defaults must be imported first (see Defaults and fallbacks). aaa_default currently serves the sprake model type.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text:
A page is a Page registered with registers.add_page. The page id is the last element of the URL (/{model_type}/{page_id}), and app.py looks the page up and calls its layout function with the LayoutConfiguration for the model type being used.

from dataclasses import dataclass
from dash import html

from newsegsmodelapp import registers
from newsegsmodelapp.components import icons, navigation
from newsegsmodelapp.dash_extension import NewsegsDash
from newsegsmodelapp.types import LayoutConfiguration, Page

PAGE_TYPE = 'my-page'

@dataclass
class MyPageLayoutConfiguration(LayoutConfiguration):
    page_type: str = PAGE_TYPE
    title: str = 'My page'               # settings which model types may override

def create_my_page_layout(config: MyPageLayoutConfiguration):
    return html.Div([navigation.create_navigation_component(config.model_type), html.H1(config.title)])

def add_my_page_callbacks(app: NewsegsDash):
    ...                                  # @app.callback(...) definitions

my_page = Page(
    id = PAGE_TYPE,
    nav_label = 'My page',
    nav_icon = html.I(className = icons.get_icon('nav-landing', style_name = 'raw')),
    layout = create_my_page_layout,
    default_configuration = MyPageLayoutConfiguration(),
    attach_callbacks = add_my_page_callbacks,
)
registers.add_page(my_page)
  • default_configuration is registered as the 'default' configuration for the page. A model type customises the page by registering its own configuration with registers.add_page_layout_configuration (see models/aaa_default/page_contents/configurations.py, which copies the default configuration and overrides the text, navigation and input/result sections).
  • attach_callbacks is called once from create_app to bind the page's Dash callbacks.
  • Navigation buttons are created from the pages in PAGE_REGISTER. A model type chooses which appear, and in what order, with the pages argument of navigation.create_navigation_component. The buttons sit in a drawer, collapsed until the navigation toggle is clicked; it opens as a row when the panes are side by side and as a column when they are stacked.
  • The pNNN_ prefix of the page modules is only a convention to set the import order.

docs.title: Models
docs.text: A model type needs its page contents and its processing.

docs.title: Page contents
docs.text:
Registered with decorators that take the supersection (the page or group of inputs, for example dsa), the optional section, and the model type:

@register_input_container_content_creator('dsa', None, 'sprake')
def create_dsa_inputs(...): ...         # builds the Dash components for the inputs

@register_result_container_content_creator(KEY, SECTION, 'sprake')
def create_results(...): ...            # builds the Dash components for a result

docs.title: Input handlers
docs.text:
react_to_input_change (in components/callbacks/input_container_callbacks.py) receives almost every change to an input. An input's id gives its type, purpose, supersection, and the section, key and subindex of its variable. The callback handles the DSA bounds, bound type and selection, and the optimisation bounds and plot resolution itself. It passes every other purpose to the handler registered for it:

@register_input_handler('my-purpose', 'input-toggle')        # purpose, component type (None for any)
def handle_my_purpose(triggered_id, input_ids, header_ids, trigger_ids, calling_dict,
                      active_project_id, project_provider, return_dict):
    ...                                  # save the change, mark what it makes stale
    return return_dict                   # with any input_values, header_children and trigger_data set

The handler is looked up for the purpose, the component type and the model type in the app-state store. It falls back to the default model type, then to any component type. A purpose with no handler makes no update. Each handler should have a callback test.

A handler that saves a value shown on the site configuration page, or changes which configurations share a Variable, should set return_dict['summary_refresh']. That redraws the input's sharing summary and its card's label, which counts the inputs whose configurations differ.

A handler that saves something a run depends on, outside the project's own row (a Variable, or a component such as the optimisation settings), must also update the project's row: with provider.increment_revision(project_id), or provider.touch_project(project_id) to change only its modification stamp. The workers cache projects, and load one again only when its row changes (see CachedFromDatabaseNewsegsProjectProvider). invalidate_cache_for_component clears only the cache of the app's own process, so without it, a worker that has run the project before runs it with the old settings.

docs.title: Lazily built editors
docs.text:
A row can build its editor only when it is opened, so that expensive content isn't built for every row of a page. html.Details doesn't report open to callbacks, so the row counts the clicks on its summary instead. input_components.create_lazy_input_details makes the row: a Details holding a Summary, an empty input-group-editor container, and a hidden single-input-config anchor. Dash only calls the callback for a row with a component matching its first output, and the editor's own inputs don't exist until it's built. When a click opens the row, react_to_input_change calls the editor content creator registered for its supersection and section, and puts what it returns in the container:

@register_input_editor_content_creator('dsa', None, 'sprake')    # supersection, section (None for all), model type
def create_dsa_editor(varid, active_project_id, project_provider) -> list[Component]:
    ...                                  # the children of the editor container

Reopening the row builds the editor again, so it shows the current values. Closing it builds nothing.

  • Redraw only the children of the editor container, never the Details or Summary, or the count of clicks and the open state will disagree. Rebuilding the whole input container is safe.

The deterministic inputs use this for their group editor (components/group_editor.py). Opening an input's sharing summary shows every group's value, and buttons that move configurations between groups. Selecting a configuration and choosing where to move it, or dragging its icon to a row, happens in the browser (assets/group_editor.js), which writes the move to the row's group-move-request store. A drop moves nothing in the page: the server redraws the editor, so the script never conflicts with the DOM that React owns. react_to_input_change passes moves, and edits of other groups' values (group-value-input), to the handlers in that module. Code that moves configurations between Variables should use move_metamodels_to_group, which keeps the junctions, revisions, staleness and orphaned Variables right.

The DSA rows have a group editor too (components/dsa_group_editor.py), in which every group's parameters, bound type and bounds can be edited. Its focussed row holds the focussed configuration's usual inputs, so the existing handlers act on them; the other groups' inputs are group-value-inputs carrying their Variable's id, with the purposes group-value, group-dsaboundtype, group-dsa-bound-lower and group-dsa-bound-upper. A change of a Variable's DSA settings should go through set_dsa_bound or set_dsa_bound_type, which save it and mark the DSA stale for the configurations using it.

The PSA rows follow the same pattern (components/psa_group_editor.py): the editor shows the distribution, and each group's Mean and SD (or Value, for a constant) and confidence interval. The other groups' parameters are edited through the group-value handler. The PSA's selection and its project settings (samples, seed, draws) aren't grouped. * Don't put interactive components in the Summary, since clicks on them are counted too.

docs.title: Environmental feedback
docs.text:
The site configuration page can show plots and tables of the environmental conditions at the site, to help compare sites. It is shown for a model type when its layout configuration sets layout_environment_feedback, usually to create_environmental_conditions_card with a list of EnvironmentFeedbackItems (see plugins/models/sprakeloc/page_contents/configurations.py). A "Get environmental data" button then appears under the map. Other model types have the components hidden.

Fetching the data is slow, so it happens only when the user clicks the button. A model type registers a data source, which says whether the data of a site are cached or being fetched, and fetches them. It also registers an artist for each item, which draws from the cache only:

class MyEnvironmentData:
    def is_available(self, location, metamodel) -> bool: ...   # all the data are cached
    def is_pending(self, location, metamodel) -> bool: ...     # another process is fetching them
    def fetch(self, location, metamodel) -> None: ...          # fetches and caches them

register_environment_data_source(MyEnvironmentData(), 'sprakeloc')

@register_environment_feedback_artist('wind-rose', 'sprakeloc')     # item key, model type
def draw_wind_rose(location, sites, metamodel) -> Component:   # sites: names and locations of the project's other sites
    ...                                  # the children of the item

metamodel is the focussed configuration, loaded in full. The data should be what a run of it at the site requests, such as at the heights of its generators and over its run period, so that the feedback and runs share the cached data.

The callbacks are in components/callbacks/environment_feedback_callbacks.py:

  • Status. Runs when the site location changes. If the data aren't cached, the feedback of the previous site stays, greyed out, with a badge saying why. It checks only that a location is set; validating the location is left to the map.
  • Fetch. A background callback, using the DiskcacheManager set up in app.py, with its jobs under BACKGROUND_CALLBACK_CACHE_PATH. Its result holds only the error, if any; the data go to the environment cache.
  • Draw. Runs once the data are ready and the panel is open, and doesn't draw again for the same site.

The environment cache locks data while they're fetched (see environment_cache.get_or_set). If a model run needs data that the feedback is fetching, or the other way round, it waits for that fetch and doesn't start another.

For sprakeloc, the data are taken from the focussed configuration: its run period, the wind at the height of its turbine, and the wind at the height of its PV array (which runs also request). A run after the feedback then fetches nothing.

docs.title: Processes
docs.text:
A process is work done in the background by a worker. Processes are chained by naming the request type that triggers them:

@register_run_request('deterministic_run_metamodel')              # build the request
def request_run(project_id, project_provider, config = None): ...

@register_run_procedure('deterministic_run_metamodel')            # do the work, in a worker
def execute_run(request, project_provider, result_provider, run_id,
                progress_callback, cancelled_callback): ...

@register_postprocess_procedure('postproc_grid', 'sprake',
                                triggers = ['deterministic_run_metamodel'])
def postprocess_grid(...): ...                                    # runs after the trigger

@register_table_draw('results-table', 'sprake', triggers = ['postproc_grid'])
def draw_grid_table(...): ...                                     # runs after postprocessing

Processes tied to a page's own functionality (the deterministic, DSA, PSA and optimisation runs) are in plugins/pages/processes, because they are not specific to a model. The postprocessing and table drawing that translate the results of a model into what is displayed are in plugins/models/<model>/processes.

Every procedure receives the progress and cancellation callbacks from the worker. Return 'ok' on success.

The model run reports its own progress through an optional progress_callback(fraction, message) argument of run: the module it is running, and any wait for environmental data. The deterministic run (common_deterministic) adds these to its "Running model" step. A first run at a new site may say, for example:

Running model - config 1: Running the generation module - Awaiting environmental data: wind speeds for
(53.255, -3.477) at 10 m from NEWA (requests usually take 1 to 8 minutes)

The environment server reports each wait (see environment_progress), including a wait for data that another request, such as the site's environmental feedback, is already fetching. The typical durations in the messages are constants in pvgis_newa_env_servers.

docs.title: Adding a model type
docs.text:
1. Add a project plugin to the framework, registering the model type.
  2. Add the model type to AVAILABLE_MODELS in src/app.py, and a button for it on the model selection page (p000_model_selection_layout.py).
  3. Add a directory in newsegsmodelapp/plugins/models/ with the page configurations, input and result sections, and processing for the model type. Anything not provided falls back to the default registrations.

def add_page_layout_configuration(
    configuration: LayoutConfiguration, 
    page_name: str,
    model_type: str = 'default'
):
    """Register the layout configuration of a page for a model type.

    Raises:
        KeyError: if the page already has a configuration for a (non-default) model type.
    """
    key = (page_name, model_type)
    if model_type != 'default':
        if key in PAGE_LAYOUT_CONFIGURATION_REGISTER:
            raise KeyError(f'Page layout configuration already exists for key {key}')
    add_page_layout_configuration_class(type(configuration), page_name)
    PAGE_LAYOUT_CONFIGURATION_REGISTER[key] = copy.copy(configuration)
    if model_type != 'default':
        key_default = (page_name, 'default')
        if key_default not in PAGE_LAYOUT_CONFIGURATION_REGISTER:
            config = copy.copy(configuration)
            config.model_type = 'default'
            PAGE_LAYOUT_CONFIGURATION_REGISTER[key] = config

def get_page_layout_configuration(
    page_name: str,
    model_type: str = 'default'
):
    """Get the layout configuration of a page for a model type.

    The configuration registered for the model type; otherwise a copy of the default configuration of the page for that model type. Raises `KeyError` if the page has no default configuration.

    Args:
        page_name: Name (id) of the page.
        model_type: The model type (e.g. `sprake`); `default` for the fallback.

    Returns:
        The configuration (a copy for the default model type).
    """
    key_default = (page_name, 'default')
    default_config = PAGE_LAYOUT_CONFIGURATION_REGISTER.get(key_default)
    if not default_config:
        raise KeyError(f'No default page configuration for page {page_name} - available pages are {set(x[0] for x in PAGE_LAYOUT_CONFIGURATION_REGISTER.keys())}')
    if model_type == 'default' :
        return copy.copy(default_config)

    key = (page_name, model_type)
    specific_config = PAGE_LAYOUT_CONFIGURATION_REGISTER.get(key)

    if not specific_config:
        conf = copy.copy(default_config)
        conf.model_type = model_type
        return conf
    return specific_config

def register_input_handler(purpose: str, type_: str | None = None, model_type: str = 'default'):
    """Decorator which registers a function which handles a change in an input.

    Keyed by the purpose and type of the triggering component, and the model type. See `INPUT_HANDLERS` for the arguments and return of the function.

    A function registered for a model type other than `default` is also registered as the `default` for the key, if there is none yet, so that other model types fall back to it. Raises `KeyError` if a function is already registered for the key under a model type other than `default`.

    Args:
        purpose: The purpose of the triggering component (the `purpose` field of its id).
        type_: The type of the triggering component (the `type` field of its id), or None for any.
        model_type: The model type (e.g. `sprake`); `default` for the fallback.

    Returns:
        The decorator.
    """
    type_ = 'ALL' if type_ is None else type_
    key = (purpose, type_, model_type)
    def decorated(func):
        if model_type != 'default':
            if key in INPUT_HANDLERS:
                raise KeyError(f'Input handler already exists for key {key}')
        INPUT_HANDLERS[key] = func
        key_default = (key[0], key[1], 'default')
        if key_default not in INPUT_HANDLERS:
            INPUT_HANDLERS[key_default] = func
        return func
    return decorated

def register_run_procedure(
    name: str,
    triggers: SequenceNotStr[str] = [],
):
    """Add a background run procedure to the register.

    The name should correspond to the request_type of the RunRequest
    """
    if isinstance(triggers, str):
        triggers = [triggers]
    def decorated(func):
        if name in RUN_PROCEDURE_REGISTER:
            raise KeyError(f'A run procedure already exists for key {name}')
        def wrapped(request: RunRequest, *args, **kwargs):
            logger.info(
                'Run procedure %s for Request ID = %d; initiated - Run ID = %d; Triggering Request ID = %d; Project ID = %s;', 
                name, request.request_id, request.run_id, request.trigger_request_id, request.project_id
            )
            rval = func(request, *args, **kwargs)
            logger.info(
                'Run procedure %s for Request ID = %d; completed with message %s - Run ID = %d; Triggering Request ID = %d; Project ID = %s;', 
                name, request.request_id, rval, request.run_id, request.trigger_request_id, request.project_id
            )
            return rval
        RUN_PROCEDURE_REGISTER[name] = wrapped
        for trig in triggers:
            pa = POST_ACTION_REGISTER.setdefault(trig, Postactions(trig))
            pa.run_procedures.add(name)
        return wrapped
    return decorated

def register_postprocess_procedure(
        name: str, model_type: str = 'default',
        triggers: SequenceNotStr[str] = []
    ):
    """Decorator which registers a postprocessing procedure.

    Keyed by the name of the procedure and the model type. The procedure is wrapped so that it logs when it starts and completes. Each of `triggers` is the name of a request whose completion starts the procedure (via `POST_ACTION_REGISTER`). See `POSTPROCESS_REGISTER` for the arguments of the procedure.

    A function registered for a model type other than `default` is also registered as the `default` for the key, if there is none yet, so that other model types fall back to it. Raises `KeyError` if a function is already registered for the key under a model type other than `default`.

    Args:
        name: Name of the object.
        model_type: The model type (e.g. `sprake`); `default` for the fallback.
        triggers: Names of the requests whose completion triggers the procedure.

    Returns:
        The decorator.
    """
    key = (name, model_type)
    if isinstance(triggers, str):
        triggers = [triggers]
    def decorated(func):
        if model_type != 'default':
            if key in POSTPROCESS_REGISTER:
                raise KeyError(f'Postprocess procedure already exists for key {key}')
        def wrapped(request: RunRequest, *args, **kwargs):
            logger.info(
                'Postprocess procedure %s for Request ID = %d; initiated - Run ID = %d; Triggering Request ID = %d; Project ID = %s;', 
                name, request.request_id, request.run_id, request.trigger_request_id, request.project_id
            )
            rval = func(request, *args, **kwargs)
            logger.info(
                'Postprocess procedure %s for Request ID = %d; completed with message %s - Run ID = %d; Triggering Request ID = %d; Project ID = %s;', 
                name, request.request_id, rval, request.run_id, request.trigger_request_id, request.project_id
            )
            return rval

def register_table_draw(
    name: str, model_type: str = 'default',
    triggers: SequenceNotStr[str] = [],
    also_draws: SequenceNotStr[str] = [],
):
    """Decorator which registers a procedure which draws the data of a table.

    Keyed by the table section and the model type. The procedure is wrapped so that it logs when it starts and completes. Each of `triggers` is the name of a request whose completion starts the procedure (via `POST_ACTION_REGISTER`). See `TABLE_DRAW_REGISTER` for the arguments of the procedure.

    A function registered for a model type other than `default` is also registered as the `default` for the key, if there is none yet, so that other model types fall back to it. Raises `KeyError` if a function is already registered for the key under a model type other than `default`.

    Args:
        name: Name of the object.
        model_type: The model type (e.g. `sprake`); `default` for the fallback.
        triggers: Names of the requests whose completion triggers the procedure.
        also_draws: Other table sections whose tables the procedure saves, e.g. those of each configuration saved by
            the table draw of a whole project. They are redrawn when the procedure completes, as its own are.

    Returns:
        The decorator.
    """
    key = (name, model_type)
    if isinstance(triggers, str):
        triggers = [triggers]
    if isinstance(also_draws, str):
        also_draws = [also_draws]
    def decorated(func):
        if model_type != 'default':
            if key in TABLE_DRAW_REGISTER:
                raise KeyError(f'Table draw artist already exists for key {key}')
        if also_draws:
            TABLE_DRAW_ALSO_DRAWS.setdefault(name, set()).update(also_draws)
        def wrapped(request: RunRequest, *args, **kwargs):
            logger.info(
                'Table draw procedure %s for Request ID = %d; initiated - Run ID = %d; Triggering Request ID = %d; Project ID = %s;', 
                name, request.request_id, request.run_id, request.trigger_request_id, request.project_id
            )
            rval = func(request, *args, **kwargs)
            logger.info(
                'Table draw procedure %s for Request ID = %d; completed with message %s - Run ID = %d; Triggering Request ID = %d; Project ID = %s;', 
                name, request.request_id, rval, request.run_id, request.trigger_request_id, request.project_id
            )
            return rval
        TABLE_DRAW_REGISTER[key] = wrapped
        for trig in triggers:
            pa = POST_ACTION_REGISTER.setdefault(trig, Postactions(trig))
            pa.table_draw_artists.add(key)

        key_default = (key[0], 'default')
        if key_default not in TABLE_DRAW_REGISTER:
            TABLE_DRAW_REGISTER[key_default] = wrapped
            for trig in triggers:
                pa = POST_ACTION_REGISTER.setdefault(trig, Postactions(trig))
                pa.table_draw_artists.add(key_default)
        return wrapped
    return decorated

def trigger_name_clash(purpose: str) -> bool:
    """Whether a purpose is also the name of a run, postprocess or table draw request.

    Used to avoid ambiguity between components and requests that share a name.

    Args:

class NewsegsDash(Dash):
    """A Dash app which holds the providers used by the pages and callbacks.

    Callbacks reach the providers through the app instead of through globals.

    Args:
        project_provider: Provider of projects, metamodels and variables.
        results_provider: Provider of results.
        request_handler: Creator and monitor of requests for background procedures.
    """
    @override
    def __init__(
        self,
        *args,
        project_provider: NewsegsProjectProviderInterface,
        results_provider: NewsegsResultProviderInterface,
        request_handler: RequestHandlerInterface,
        #background_callback_manager: DiskcacheManager | CeleryManager,
        **kwargs
    ):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self._project_provider = project_provider
        self._results_provider = results_provider
        self._request_handler = request_handler
        #self._bcm = background_callback_manager

    @property
    def project_provider(self) -> NewsegsProjectProviderInterface:
        """Provider of projects, metamodels and variables.
        """
        return self._project_provider

    @property
    def results_provider(self) -> NewsegsResultProviderInterface:
        """Provider of results.
        """
        return self._results_provider

    @property
    def request_handler(self) -> RequestHandlerInterface:
        """Creator and monitor of requests for background procedures.
        """
        return self._request_handler

@register_input_handler('psa-settings')
def handle_psa_settings(
    triggered_id: dict,
    input_ids: list[dict[str, str]],
    header_ids: list[dict[str, str]],
    trigger_ids: list[dict[str, str]],
    calling_dict: dict,
    active_project_id: str,
    project_provider: NewsegsProjectProviderInterface,
    return_dict: dict[str, Any],
    new_val: Optional[Any] = None, # Include this so we can call from other parameter setting functions, not just dash callbacks
):
    """Input handler for a change to a setting of the PSA (number of samples, seed or return of draws).

    Updates the PSA configuration of the project.

    Args:
        triggered_id: The id of the component which triggered the callback.
        input_ids: The ids of the input components of the callback.
        header_ids: The ids of the header containers of the callback.
        trigger_ids: The ids of the trigger stores of the callback.
        calling_dict: Other keyword arguments of the calling callback.
        active_project_id: Id of the active project.
        project_provider: Provider of projects, metamodels and variables.
        return_dict: Dictionary of the outputs of the callback, to be updated and returned.
        new_val: The new value.

    Returns:
        The updated `return_dict`.
    """
    if new_val is None:
        new_val = callback_utils.get_triggered_value()
        if new_val is None and triggered_id['key'] != 'seed':
            new_val = 0

    provider = cast(FromDatabaseNewsegsProjectProvider, project_provider)
    logger.debug('Getting lightweight project - Handling PSA settings change')
    lproj = provider.get_lightweight_project(active_project_id)
    psa_config = provider._component_provider.get_component(lproj.psa_config.id)

    now = time.time_ns()

    r0 = psa_config.revision
    modified = False
    match triggered_id['key']:
        case 'seed':
            if psa_config.seed != new_val:
                old_val = psa_config.seed
                psa_config.seed = new_val
        case 'samples':
            new_val = max(min(int(new_val), 10000), 10) 
            if psa_config.samples != int(new_val):
                old_val = psa_config.samples
                psa_config.samples = int(new_val)
        case 'return_draws':
            if psa_config.return_draws != new_val:
                old_val = psa_config.return_draws
                psa_config.return_draws = new_val 
        case _:
            logger.exception('No PSA setting handler for key: %s', triggered_id['key'])

    modified = psa_config.revision != r0
    if not modified:
        return return_dict

    logger.debug(
        'PSA setting changed - %s: %s -> %s',
        triggered_id["key"], old_val, new_val
    )

    # Feed back current parameters
    for idx, id in enumerate(input_ids):
        if id['purpose'] == 'psa-settings':
            return_dict['input_values'][idx] = new_val

     # Update triggers
    for idx, id in enumerate(trigger_ids):
        return_dict['trigger_data'][idx] = now

    # Sync configuration to store
    provider._component_provider.upsert_component(psa_config, project_id = active_project_id)

    # TODO: Invalidate only PSA outputs
    # Currently, we have to invalidate all outputs even though these
    # settings only apply to the PSA.
    provider._component_provider.increment_revision(lproj.table_config.id)

    provider.increment_revision(lproj.id)

    # PSA settings are held for the project, so apply to every configuration
    db_staleness.mark_inputs_changed([x.id for x in lproj.metamodels], 'psa')

    return return_dict

@register_input_handler('psa-active')
def handle_psa_active(
    triggered_id: dict,
    input_ids: list[dict[str, str]],
    header_ids: list[dict[str, str]],
    trigger_ids: list[dict[str, str]],
    calling_dict: dict,
    active_project_id: str,
    project_provider: NewsegsProjectProviderInterface,
    return_dict: dict[str, Any],
    new_val: Optional[Any] = None, # Include this so we can call from other parameter setting functions, not just dash callbacks
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Input handler for a variable being selected or deselected for the PSA.

    Args:
        triggered_id: The id of the component which triggered the callback.
        input_ids: The ids of the input components of the callback.
        header_ids: The ids of the header containers of the callback.
        trigger_ids: The ids of the trigger stores of the callback.
        calling_dict: Other keyword arguments of the calling callback.
        active_project_id: Id of the active project.
        project_provider: Provider of projects, metamodels and variables.
        return_dict: Dictionary of the outputs of the callback, to be updated and returned.
        new_val: The new value.

    Returns:
        The updated `return_dict`.
    """
    if new_val is None:
        new_val = callback_utils.get_triggered_value()

    provider = cast(FromDatabaseNewsegsProjectProvider, project_provider)
    logger.debug('Getting lightweight project - Handling PSA activation change')
    lproj = provider.get_lightweight_project(active_project_id)
    lmm = cast(LightweightNewsegsMetaModel, lproj.metamodels[lproj.focussed_metamodel_index])

    varid =  make_varid(**triggered_id)
    var_uid = lmm.variables[varid]
    var = project_provider.variable_provider.get_variable(var_uid)

    if not var or new_val == var.psa_selected:
        return return_dict

    var.psa_selected = new_val

    now = time.time_ns()
    # Update triggers with a dictionary, not an integer
    trig_val = json.dumps({
        'message': 'psa_selection_status_modified',
        'time': now
    })
    for idx, id in enumerate(trigger_ids):
        match id['supersection']:
            case 'psa':
                return_dict['trigger_data'][idx] = trig_val

    # Sync variable
    project_provider.variable_provider.upsert_variable(var)

    # Sync the selection onto the independent instances of the variable in the other metamodels,
    # so that a whole-project PSA varies the same variables in every metamodel
    changed_mm_ids = list(staleness.metamodels_using_variable(lproj, var_uid))
    for other_lmm in lproj.metamodels:
        other_uid = other_lmm.variables.get(varid)
        if not other_uid or other_uid == var_uid:
            continue
        other_var = project_provider.variable_provider.get_variable(other_uid)
        if (
            not other_var
            or not (other_var.psa_possible and other_var.psa_selectable)
            or other_var.psa_selected == new_val
        ):
            continue
        other_var.psa_selected = new_val
        project_provider.variable_provider.upsert_variable(other_var)
        for mm_id in staleness.metamodels_using_variable(lproj, other_uid):
            if mm_id not in changed_mm_ids:
                changed_mm_ids.append(mm_id)

    # Don't need to invalidate metamodels, as PSA will run anyway,
    # but do need to invalidate at project level
    # TODO: Invalidate only PSA outputs
    # Currently, we have to invalidate all outputs even though these
    # settings only apply to the PSA.
    provider._component_provider.increment_revision(lproj.table_config.id)

    provider.increment_revision(lproj.id)

    db_staleness.mark_inputs_changed(changed_mm_ids, 'psa')

    return return_dict

def get_result_list(
    result_type: str,
    lproject: LightweightNewsegsProject,
    result_provider: NewsegsResultProviderInterface,
    allow_stale: bool = True
) -> tuple[list, bool]:
    """Get the result of each metamodel of a project, for results that are shown side by side.

    The results are those of the table configuration of the model (or, for finance results, the finance model) of each metamodel.

    Args:
        result_type: The type of the result.
        lproject: The lightweight project.
        result_provider: Provider of results.
        allow_stale: Allow results which are not for the present revision.

    Returns:
        The list of results, and whether any is stale (not for the present revision).
    """
    is_finance = 'finance' in result_type
    results_list = []

def is_improvement(start: float, final: float, maximised: bool) -> bool:
    """Whether a final value of a statistic is better than its start, beyond rounding error.

    Args:
        start: The value before optimisation.
        final: The value after.
        maximised: Whether the statistic is maximised.

    Returns:
        True if the final value is better.
    """
    change = final - start if maximised else start - final
    return change > _relative_tolerance(start)

def format_value(value: float) -> str:
    """A value of a variable, to 6 significant figures (or the nearest whole number, if larger), with
    thousands separators and without trailing zeros, e.g. '1,234,567' or '135.5'."""
    if not math.isfinite(value):
        return 'none'
    if value == 0:
        return '0'
    decimals = max(0, 6 - (math.floor(math.log10(abs(value))) + 1))
    text = f'{value:,.{decimals}f}'
    return text.rstrip('0').rstrip('.') if decimals else text

def improvement_summary(result: dict) -> str:
    """One sentence saying how the statistic changed in an optimisation.

    The relative change is given only when the start is positive, as it is undefined or misleading
    otherwise.

    Args:
        result: The `optimisation_result` of a successful optimisation.

    Returns:
        The sentence, e.g. 'NPV (discounted) improved by £12,345 (+8.2%), from £150,000 to £162,345.'
    """
    label = optim.OPTIM_TARGET_STATISTIC_LABELS.get(result['statistic'], result['statistic'])
    start, final = result['start_value'], result['final_value']
    if not is_improvement(start, final, result['maximised']):
        start_outside_bounds = any(not v['lower'] <= v['before'] <= v['upper'] for v in result['variables'])
        if start_outside_bounds and is_improvement(final, start, result['maximised']):
            # The optimiser searched only within the bounds, so could not return to the start
            return (
                f'{label} did not improve: the best value within the bounds ({format_money(final)}) is worse than '
                f'the current configuration\'s ({format_money(start)}), which lies outside them.'
            )
        return (
            f'{label} did not improve: the configuration is already at or near its best within the bounds '
            f'({format_money(start)}).'
        )
    change = abs(final - start)
    verb = 'improved' if result['maximised'] else 'reduced'
    relative = f' ({(final - start) / start:+.1%})' if start > 0 else ''
    return f'{label} {verb} by {format_money(change)}{relative}, from {format_money(start)} to {format_money(final)}.'

def create_optimisation_feedback(result: dict) -> list:
    """The feedback shown after an optimisation.

    Args:
        result: The `optimisation_result` saved by the optimisation.

    Returns:
        The components.
    """
    status = result.get('status')
    if status is None:
        # Saved before the feedback recorded the statistic
        return _legacy_feedback(result)

    if status == 'not_run':
        return [
            html.H4('Optimisation not run'),
            html.P('No variables are selected for optimisation. Select the variables to vary, and set their bounds, then run it again.'),
        ]

    label = optim.OPTIM_TARGET_STATISTIC_LABELS.get(result['statistic'], result['statistic'])
    if status == 'success':
        children = [
            html.H4('Optimisation complete'),
            html.P(improvement_summary(result), className = 'lead'),
            variables_table(result),
        ]
        if is_improvement(result['start_value'], result['final_value'], result['maximised']):
            children.append(html.P([
                'The optimised values are in the new configuration ',
                html.B(result['new_metamodel_name']),
                ', added to the project and now focussed.',
            ]))
        children.append(_diagnostics(result))
        return children

    children = [
        html.H4('Optimisation did not succeed'),
        html.P(f'The optimiser stopped without finding a best value of {label}: {result["message"]}'),
    ]
    if is_improvement(result['start_value'], result['final_value'], result['maximised']):
        children.append(html.P(
            f'The best value it found, {format_money(result["final_value"])}, is better than the configuration\'s '
            f'{format_money(result["start_value"])}, but has not been saved.'
        ))
    children += [
        html.P('To try again:', className = 'mb-1'),
        html.Ul([html.Li(x) for x in _SUGGESTIONS]),
        _diagnostics(result),
    ]
    return children

def dsa_results_to_tables(
    dsa_data: pd.DataFrame
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:

    """Convert the results of a DSA into tables.

    The first row of the data is the deterministic run, the others the runs with each variable at its bounds. Raises `TypeError` if the data are not long enough.

    Args:
        dsa_data: Dataframe of the results of the DSA.

    Returns:
        The tables: the deterministic result, and the sensitivities with their labels.
    """
    if len(dsa_data) < 2:
        raise TypeError('dsa_data is not long enough')

    # Deterministic results
    det = dsa_data.loc[[('deterministic', 'central')], :]
    det_value_data = det.drop(columns = ['value'])

    # Cannot anti-join on Pandas < 3.0
    #sens = pd.merge(dsa_data, det, how='left_anti', left_index = True, right_index=True)
    sens = dsa_data.iloc[range(1, len(dsa_data)), :] # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType, reportCallIssue]
    sens_label_data = sens.loc[:, ['value']]
    sens_value_data = sens.drop(columns = ['value'])

    det_long = _melt_dsa(det_value_data)
    sens_long = _melt_dsa(sens_value_data)

    intervals = _interval_width(sens_long)

    deltas_long = _deltas_dsa(
        det_value_data,
        sens_value_data
    )

    dsa_table_data = (
        sens_long
        .join(intervals)
        .join(deltas_long)
        .reset_index()
        .set_index('statistic')
        .join(
            det_long
            .reset_index()
            .set_index('statistic')
            .drop(columns = ('variable', ''))
        )
        .reset_index()
        .set_index(['variable', 'statistic'])
    )

    dsa_label_data = _melt_dsa(sens_label_data.rename(columns={'value': 'variable_value'}))

    return (dsa_table_data, dsa_label_data)

def calculate_sprake_admd(n_units, n_evs):
    """Estimate the After Diversity Maximum Demand (ADMD) of a site of the Sprake model.

    Assumes that every household has an 8 kW air source heat pump, and that every EV charger is at a household with a heat pump. Uses the ADMD calculation (`admdspenmw`).

    Args:
        n_units: Number of households.
        n_evs: Number of EVs.

    Returns:
        The standard ADMD (kW).
    """
    site_details = {
        'N_customers': int(n_units),
        'N_EV_chargers': np.min([n_evs, n_units]),
        'N_EV_and_HP': np.min([n_evs, n_units])
    }

    ASHP_dist = {
        'N_ASHP_5kW': float(0),
        'N_ASHP_8kW': float(n_units),
        'N_ASHP_16kW': float(0)
    }

    ip = default_model_inputs.copy()
    ip.update(site_details)
    ip.update(ASHP_dist)

    op = default_model_outputs.copy()
    dr = _ADMD_DR

    o = dr.execute(op, inputs = ip) # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]

    return o.get('ADMD_standard')

def seasonal_and_profile_consumption_summary(grp):
    """Summarise consumption annually and per day, by season and by profile.

    Args:
        grp: Group of the consumption data.

    Returns:
        The summary dataframe.
    """
    summary_consumption_year = (
        grp
        .loc[:,['consumption', 'year_index']]
        .pipe(basic_summary_stats.meter_annual_summary)
        .assign(season = 'Year')
        .reset_index(names='statistic')
    )

    summary_consumption_perday = (
        grp
        .loc[:,['consumption', 'day_index']]
        .pipe(basic_summary_stats.meter_perday_summary)
        .rename(columns={'consumption':'per_day'})
        .assign(season = 'Year')
        .reset_index(names='statistic')
    )

    summary_consumption_year_season = (
        grp
        .loc[:,['consumption', 'year_index', 'season']]
        .groupby('season')
        .apply(basic_summary_stats.meter_annual_summary)
        .reset_index(names=['season','statistic'])
    )

    summary_consumption_perday_season = (
        grp
        .loc[:,['consumption', 'day_index', 'season']]
        .groupby('season')
        .apply(basic_summary_stats.meter_perday_summary)
        .reset_index(names=['season','statistic'])
        .rename(columns={'consumption':'per_day'})
    )

    odf = pd.concat([
        pd.merge(summary_consumption_year, summary_consumption_perday, on = ['statistic','season']),
        pd.merge(summary_consumption_year_season, summary_consumption_perday_season, on = ['statistic','season'])
    ]).reset_index(drop=True)

    return odf

def consumption_results_to_interface_sprake(
    mdl: SprakeModel
) -> dict:
    """
    Extracts the consumption results required for the Dash interface to Sprake model.
    """
    # This holds our final returned data structure
    results_to_interface = {}

    conr = mdl.get_consumption_storage_result()
    n_units = mdl.consumption_storage.n_units
    n_evs = mdl.consumption_storage.get_ev_params().get('n_evs')

    cons_data = (
        newsegscs.get_consumption_meters(conr)
        .assign(
            residential = lambda df: df['appliance_import'] + df['dhw_import'] + df['spaceheat_import'],
            residential_pu = lambda df: df['residential'] / n_units
        )
    )
    cons_data_ann = cons_data.pipe(assign_year_index).query('year_index>=0')
    cons_data_day = (
        agg_meters_daily.agg_meters_daily(cons_data.loc[:,'consumption'])
        .query('day_index >= 0')
    )

    results_to_interface['consumption_meter_summaries'] = (
        cons_data_ann
        .pipe(basic_summary_stats.meter_annual_summary)
        .pipe(basic_summary_stats.meter_annual_summary_to_interface)
    )

    ### Extreme values #####
    results_to_interface['max_consumption_day'] = locate_timeseries_extrema.report_ts_max(
        cons_data_day.set_index('datetime')['consumption']
    )

    results_to_interface['min_consumption_day'] = locate_timeseries_extrema.report_ts_min(
        cons_data_day.set_index('datetime')['consumption']
    )

    #### ADMD calculations #####
    results_to_interface['admd_calculated'] = {'value':calculate_sprake_admd(n_units, n_evs)}

    cons_data_power = (
        cons_data.loc[:,'consumption']
        .pipe(assign_delta_hours)
        .query('delta_hours > 0')
        .assign(power = lambda df: df['consumption'] / df['delta_hours'])
    )

    results_to_interface['admd_observed'] = locate_timeseries_extrema.report_ts_max(cons_data_power['power'])

    ##### Seasonal summaries ####
    cons_data_season = (
        pd.merge(
            cons_data.loc[:,['consumption']],
            (
                elexon_profiles.characterise_dates_elexon(cons_data.index)
                .set_index('datetime')
                .assign(elexon_day = lambda df: df['elexon_day'].shift(1, fill_value='wd'))
            ),
            left_index = True,
            right_index = True
        )
        .loc[:,['consumption','elexon_day']]
        .pipe(assign_year_index)
        .pipe(assign_season_index)
        .pipe(assign_day_index)
        .query('year_index >= 0')
        .assign(season = lambda df: SEASON_NAMES_MAP.loc[df['season_index'],'season'].values)
        .drop(columns='season_index')
    )

    seasonal_data = (
        cons_data_season
        .rename(columns={'elexon_day':'day'})
        .groupby('day')
        [['consumption','year_index','day_index','season']]
        .apply(seasonal_and_profile_consumption_summary)
        .droplevel(1,axis=0)
        .reset_index(drop=False)
    )

    # For per-day data, copy the mean across to the sum so we still get the mean consumption per day
    mn = (
        seasonal_data
        .query('statistic=="mean"')
        .loc[:,['day','season','per_day']]
        .rename(columns={'per_day': 'pd_mean'})
    )
    seasonal_data = (
        pd.merge(
            seasonal_data, mn, on=['day','season']
        )
        .assign(
            per_day = lambda df: np.where(df['statistic']=='sum', df['pd_mean'], df['per_day'])
        )
        .drop(columns=['pd_mean'])
        .set_index('day')
    )

    results_to_interface['seasonal_consumption'] = {
        k: (seasonal_data.loc[k,:].to_dict(orient='tight')) for k in np.unique(seasonal_data.index) # pyright: ignore[reportCallIssue]
    }

    return results_to_interface

def finance_benefits_results_to_interface_sprake(
    mdl: SprakeModel,
    fnc: SprakeFinance
) -> dict:
    """
    Extracts the financial benefits results required for the Dash interface
    """
    # This holds our final returned data structure
    results_to_interface = {}

    n_units = mdl.consumption_storage.n_units

    resident_receipts = fnc.resident_receipts_undiscounted
    ev_receipts = fnc.ev_receipts_undiscounted
    export_receipts = fnc.export_receipts_undiscounted

    receipts = (
        resident_receipts
        .loc[:,['receipts']]
        .rename(columns = {'receipts': 'receipts_resident'})
        .assign(receipts_resident_perunit = lambda df: df['receipts_resident'] / n_units)
        .join(
            ev_receipts
            .loc[:, ['receipts']]
            .rename(columns = {'receipts': 'receipts_ev'})
        )
        .join(
            export_receipts
            .loc[:, ['receipts']]
            .rename(columns = {'receipts': 'receipts_exports'})
        )
        .assign(
            receipts_total = lambda df: df.sum(axis=1)
        )
    )

    undiscounted_receipts_summaries = (
        receipts
        .pipe(assign_year_index)
        .query('year_index >= 0')
        .pipe(basic_summary_stats.meter_annual_summary2)
    )

    results_to_interface['undiscounted_receipts_summaries'] = (
        undiscounted_receipts_summaries
        .pipe(basic_summary_stats.meter_annual_summary2_to_interface)
    )

    results_to_interface['present_benefits_undiscounted'] = fnc.get_total_present_benefits_undiscounted()
    results_to_interface['present_benefits_discounted'] = fnc.get_total_present_benefits_discounted()
    results_to_interface['benefits_discount_rate'] = fnc.benefit_discount_rate

    # Results used by the summary headers
    undiscounted_receipts_summaries = undiscounted_receipts_summaries.set_index(['variable','statistic'])
    results_to_interface['smry_residential_peryear'] = float(undiscounted_receipts_summaries.loc[('receipts_resident', 'mean'), 'value']) # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]
    results_to_interface['smry_exports_peryear'] = float(undiscounted_receipts_summaries.loc[('receipts_exports', 'mean'),'value']) # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]

    return results_to_interface

    mdl: SprakeModel, # Unused
