class NewsegsComponent(
    SerialisedConfigurationMixin,
    metaclass = ABCMeta
):
    """
    Base class of a NewSEGS (meta)model component.

    Provides common functionality for model components including unique identification,
    serialization/deserialization, and configuration synchronization checks.
    """

    _name: str = 'Model component'
    _version: str = '0.0.1'

    # Override of SerialiseToDictMixin _constructor_class
    _constructor_class = 'NewsegsComponent'

    _serialisation_settings = dict(
        state_excludes = 'excluded_and_components'
    )

    _component_ids: dict[str, str]
    """IDs of subcomponents for reconstruction of component."""

    # NB - all ID generating attributes are now in ConfigurationMixin   

    @classmethod
    def set_state_exclusion_policy(cls, excludes: _STATE_EXCLUDES = 'excluded_and_components'):
        """Set which attributes are left out of the dictionary made by `to_dict`.

        Applies to the class. The default leaves out the attributes which are themselves components, which are stored separately; `to_dict_repr` temporarily includes them.

        Args:
            excludes: `'excluded'` omits the attributes excluded from the state; `'excluded_and_components'` also omits the attributes which are components, which are saved and reattached separately.
        """
        cls._serialisation_settings['state_excludes'] = excludes

    def __init__(self, *args, name: Optional[str] = None, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs) 
        self.uuid = str(mod_uuid.uuid4())
        if name is not None:
            self.name = name
        self._component_ids = {}

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        """Name of the type of component.
        """
        return self._name

    @name.setter
    def name(self, name: str) -> None:
        self._name = name

    @property
    def version(self) -> str:
        """Version of the component; changes when the structure of the configuration changes.
        """
        return self._version

    @property
    def config(self) -> DataWithRevision:
        """The revision-tracked configuration object.
        """
        return self._config

    @override
    def get_excluded_attributes(self) -> set[str]:
        excluded = super().get_excluded_attributes()
        if self._serialisation_settings['state_excludes'] == 'excluded_and_components':
            component_property_names = self.get_component_attributes()
            excluded = excluded.union({'_' + x for x in component_property_names})        
        return excluded

    @override
    def _prepare_object_state(self):
        super()._prepare_object_state()
        self.update_component_id_dict()

    @override
    def _get_state_class_values(self):
        values = super()._get_state_class_values()
        values['version'] = self._version
        return values

    @override
    def _preupdate_from_dict(self, config):
        # A dictionary without a version was saved before versions were recorded; it is loaded
        # with the defaults of anything added since. A newer version cannot be understood.
        version = config.pop('version', UNVERSIONED_COMPONENT_VERSION)
        if parse_component_version(version) > parse_component_version(self._version):
            raise ValueError(
                f'{type(self).__name__} was saved at version {version}, which is newer than the version '
                f'this app supports ({self._version}). Update the app to load it.'
            )
        super()._preupdate_from_dict(config)

    def to_dict_repr(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """A dictionary reproduction of the component including child components (not references)."""
        type_ = type(self)
        type_.set_state_exclusion_policy('excluded')
        odict = self.to_dict()
        type_.set_state_exclusion_policy('excluded_and_components')
        return odict

    def json_dumps_repr(self) -> str:
        """Serialise the representation made by `to_dict_repr` (including child components) to a JSON string.

        Returns:
            The JSON string.
        """
        return json.dumps(self.to_dict_repr(), cls = jsonfuncs.NumpyEncoder)

    def _repr_represent(self, value):
        if isinstance(value, object) and hasattr(value, 'to_dict_repr'):
            return value.to_dict_repr() # pyright: ignore[reportAttributeAccessIssue]
        return self._represent(value)

    @override
    def __setstate__(self, state: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        state = copy.copy(state)
        compnames = self.get_component_attributes()
        for cn in compnames:
            if '_'+ cn in state and not cn in state:
                state[cn] = state['_' + cn]
                del state['_' + cn]

        super().__setstate__(state)

    def __deepcopy__(self, memo):
        cls = self.__class__
        result = cls.__new__(cls)
        memo[id(self)] = result

        cls.set_state_exclusion_policy('excluded')
        state = copy.deepcopy(self.__getstate__())
        cls.set_state_exclusion_policy('excluded_and_components')

        result.__setstate__(state)

        return result

    @staticmethod
    def _anonymise_id_sequence(seq: SequenceNotStr):
        for x in seq:
            if isinstance(x, NewsegsComponent):
                x.anonymise_ids()
            elif isinstance(x, Mapping):
                NewsegsComponent._anonymise_id_sequence(tuple(x.values()))
            elif not isinstance(x, str) and isinstance(x, Sequence):
                NewsegsComponent._anonymise_id_sequence(x) # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]

    @override
    def anonymise_ids(self):
        super().anonymise_ids()
        self._anonymise_id_sequence(self.get_components())            

    def get_component_attributes(self) -> tuple['str', ...]:
        """A tuple of all the attributes of the object that are themselves NewsegsComponents"""
        type_ = type(self)

        # Strip out dunders and single unders - the properties will not have a leading underscore
        atts = tuple(k for k in dir(type_) if not k.startswith('_'))
        atts = tuple(k for k in atts if isinstance(getattr(type_, k), ComponentPropertyInterface))
        return atts

    @staticmethod
    def _recursive_get_component(atts: NewsegsComponent | Iterable) -> list['NewsegsComponent']:
        rlist = []

        if isinstance(atts, NewsegsComponent):
            rlist.append(atts)
        elif isinstance(atts, Mapping):
            for x in atts.values():
                rlist.extend(NewsegsComponent._recursive_get_component(x))
            #(rlist.extend(NewsegsComponent._recursive_get_component(x)) for x in atts.values())
        elif isinstance(atts, Iterable):
            for x in atts:
                rlist.extend(NewsegsComponent._recursive_get_component(x))
            #(rlist.extend(NewsegsComponent._recursive_get_component(x)) for x in atts)
        return rlist                

    def get_components(self, component_group: Optional[PREFIX_GROUP_KEY] = None) -> tuple['NewsegsComponent', ...]:
        """A tuple of all subcomponents that would require saving to store and reattaching after deserialisation."""
        attnames = self.get_component_attributes()
        excl = self._excluded_attributes
        attnames = (x for x in attnames if '_'+x not in excl)

        atts = []
        for nm in attnames:
            try:
                atts.append(getattr(self, nm))
            except AttributeError:
                pass

        components = self._recursive_get_component(atts)

        if component_group is not None:
            prefixes = set(x+'-' for x in PREFIX_GROUPS[component_group])
            # Creatig a generator function doesn't seem to work
            sublist = []
            for x in components:
                if any(x.id.startswith(y) for y in prefixes):
                    sublist.append(x)
            components = sublist
            #components = (x for x in components if not any(x.id.startswith(y) for y in prefixes))

        return tuple(components)

    def update_component_id_dict(self):
        """Update ._component_ids prior to serialisation."""
        self._component_ids.clear()
        att_names = self.get_component_attributes()
        for att in att_names:
            comp = getattr(self, att)
            if isinstance(comp, NewsegsComponent):
                self._component_ids[att] = comp.id

    def reattach_components(
        self,
        component_provider: NewsegsComponentProviderInterface
    ):
        """Using the component_provider, find all components for reattachment."""
        r0 = self.revision
        prefixes = tuple(x+'-' for x in PREFIX_GROUPS['component_configs'])
        for att_name, comp_id in self._component_ids.items():
            if any(comp_id.startswith(y) for y in prefixes):
                comp = component_provider.get_component(comp_id)
                setattr(self, att_name, comp)
        # Ensure that revision is not incremented due to reattachment
        self.revision = r0

    def _get_component_properties(self):
        # Stage 1 - strip out the dunders
        comp_props = [x for x in dir(self) if not x.startswith('__')]
        # Stage 2 - check has attribute
        comp_props = [x for x in comp_props if hasattr(self, x)]
        # Stage 3 - check has '_last_syncronised'
        comp_props = [x for x in comp_props if hasattr(getattr(self, x), '_last_syncronised')]
        # Stage 4 - keep only the single underscore versions
        comp_props.sort()
        r_props = set()
        for x in comp_props:
            if not '_' + x in r_props:
                r_props.add(x)
        return r_props

    def reset_revision(self, chain: bool = True):
        """Set the revision to 0 and _last_syncronised to -1

        If chain, also perform this for all ComponentProperties
    """
        if chain:
            comps = self.get_components()
            for att in comps:
                if hasattr(att, 'reset_revision'):
                    att.reset_revision(chain = chain)
                else:
                    att._revision = 0
                    att._last_syncronised = -1

            # Also go through the root attributes to get the containers
            comp_atts = self.get_component_attributes()
            for attname in comp_atts:
                att = getattr(self, attname)
                # No need to repeat for non-containers
                if not att in comps:
                    if hasattr(att, 'reset_revision'):
                        att.reset_revision(chain = chain)
                    else:
                        if att is not None:
                            att._revision = 0
                            att._last_syncronised = -1
        self._config._revision = 0
        self._config._last_syncronised = -1

    @property
    def dirty(self):
        """Whether the component, or any of its children, has been modified since it was last synchronised with storage.
        """
        return self.chain_modified

class NewsegsModule(newsegscomponent.NewsegsComponent):
    """
    Abstract base class for modules that run within a Newsegs model.

    Subclasses should implement the abstract run() method to perform a
    computation over a given TimeSpan and return a NewsegsModuleResult.

    This class provides common plumbing including tracking the associated
    NewsegsModelInterface instance, a "dirty" flag that indicates whether
    the module configuration has changed since the last run, and recording
    the last run time.
    """

    # Override of SerialiseToDictMixin _constructor_class
    _constructor_class = 'NewsegsModule'
    _excluded_attributes = newsegscomponent.NewsegsComponent._excluded_attributes.union({'_model'})

    _model: NewsegsModelInterface

    def __init__(self, *args, model: Optional[NewsegsModelInterface] = None, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        if model is not None:
            self.model = model

    @abstractmethod
    def run(
        self,
        timespan:TimeSpan,
        run_start: datetime.datetime | None = None
    ) -> NewsegsModuleResult:
        """Run the module over a time span.

        Subclasses extend this, calling it first so that the time of the run is recorded.

        Args:
            timespan: The period of time.
            run_start: See the description.

        Returns:
            The result of the run.
        """
        if run_start is None:
            run_start = datetime.datetime.now()
        self.last_run = run_start
        # Returns none as this is still abstract

    # NB - model is not a ComponentProperty in order to avoid circular references
    @property
    def model(self) -> NewsegsModelInterface:
        """
        The callback model associated with the module
        """
        if not hasattr(self, '_model'):
            raise AttributeError('model has not been set')
        return self._model

    @model.setter
    def model(self, model: NewsegsModelInterface):
        self._model = model

    @property
    def dirty(self) -> bool:
        """
        Has the model configuration changed since last run?
        """
        return self.modified

    @dirty.setter
    def dirty(self, val:bool) -> None:
        warnings.warn('Setting of dirty parameter is deprecated', DeprecationWarning)
        if val:
            self._config._revision += 1
        else:
            self._config._revision = self._config._last_syncronised
        self._dirty = val

def find_constructor(
    constructor_class: str,
    classname: str
) -> Callable[[dict[str, Any]], object]:
    """
    Retrieve a constructor callable from the registry.

    Looks up the registry associated with `constructor_class` and then the
    registered constructor for `classname`. If the constructor is a
    functools.partial, a deferred dictionary-based constructor is returned.
    Otherwise, the registered class must implement a `from_dict` classmethod.

    Args:
        constructor_class: Name of the constructor registry.
        classname: Name of the registered constructor.

    Returns:
        A callable that accepts a dictionary and returns an instantiated object.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the classname is not found in the constructor register.
        AttributeError: If the registered constructor does not implement `from_dict`.
    """
    reg = registers.get_register(constructor_class)

    constr = reg.get(classname, None)
    if constr is None:
        raise ValueError(f'classname not found in constructor register: {classname} in {constructor_class}; available keys are: {list(reg.keys())}')

    if isinstance(constr, functools.partial):
        constr = _deferred_constructor_update_from_dict(constr)
        return constr

    if not isinstance(constr, SerialiseToDictProtocol):
        if not hasattr(constr, '__name__'):
            raise AttributeError(f'class {type(constr)} does not implement SerialiseToDictProtocol')
        else:
            raise AttributeError(f'class {constr.__name__} does not implement SerialiseToDictProtocol') # pyright: ignore[reportAttributeAccessIssue]

    return constr.from_dict

class NewsegsComponent(
    SerialisedConfigurationMixin,
    metaclass = ABCMeta
):
    """
    Base class of a NewSEGS (meta)model component.

    Provides common functionality for model components including unique identification,
    serialization/deserialization, and configuration synchronization checks.
    """

    _name: str = 'Model component'
    _version: str = '0.0.1'

    # Override of SerialiseToDictMixin _constructor_class
    _constructor_class = 'NewsegsComponent'

    _serialisation_settings = dict(
        state_excludes = 'excluded_and_components'
    )

    _component_ids: dict[str, str]
    """IDs of subcomponents for reconstruction of component."""

    # NB - all ID generating attributes are now in ConfigurationMixin   

    @classmethod
    def set_state_exclusion_policy(cls, excludes: _STATE_EXCLUDES = 'excluded_and_components'):
        """Set which attributes are left out of the dictionary made by `to_dict`.

        Applies to the class. The default leaves out the attributes which are themselves components, which are stored separately; `to_dict_repr` temporarily includes them.

        Args:
            excludes: `'excluded'` omits the attributes excluded from the state; `'excluded_and_components'` also omits the attributes which are components, which are saved and reattached separately.
        """
        cls._serialisation_settings['state_excludes'] = excludes

    def __init__(self, *args, name: Optional[str] = None, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs) 
        self.uuid = str(mod_uuid.uuid4())
        if name is not None:
            self.name = name
        self._component_ids = {}

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        """Name of the type of component.
        """
        return self._name

    @name.setter
    def name(self, name: str) -> None:
        self._name = name

    @property
    def version(self) -> str:
        """Version of the component; changes when the structure of the configuration changes.
        """
        return self._version

    @property
    def config(self) -> DataWithRevision:
        """The revision-tracked configuration object.
        """
        return self._config

    @override
    def get_excluded_attributes(self) -> set[str]:
        excluded = super().get_excluded_attributes()
        if self._serialisation_settings['state_excludes'] == 'excluded_and_components':
            component_property_names = self.get_component_attributes()
            excluded = excluded.union({'_' + x for x in component_property_names})        
        return excluded

    @override
    def _prepare_object_state(self):
        super()._prepare_object_state()
        self.update_component_id_dict()

    @override
    def _get_state_class_values(self):
        values = super()._get_state_class_values()
        values['version'] = self._version
        return values

    @override
    def _preupdate_from_dict(self, config):
        # A dictionary without a version was saved before versions were recorded; it is loaded
        # with the defaults of anything added since. A newer version cannot be understood.
        version = config.pop('version', UNVERSIONED_COMPONENT_VERSION)
        if parse_component_version(version) > parse_component_version(self._version):
            raise ValueError(
                f'{type(self).__name__} was saved at version {version}, which is newer than the version '
                f'this app supports ({self._version}). Update the app to load it.'
            )
        super()._preupdate_from_dict(config)

    def to_dict_repr(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """A dictionary reproduction of the component including child components (not references)."""
        type_ = type(self)
        type_.set_state_exclusion_policy('excluded')
        odict = self.to_dict()
        type_.set_state_exclusion_policy('excluded_and_components')
        return odict

    def json_dumps_repr(self) -> str:
        """Serialise the representation made by `to_dict_repr` (including child components) to a JSON string.

        Returns:
            The JSON string.
        """
        return json.dumps(self.to_dict_repr(), cls = jsonfuncs.NumpyEncoder)

    def _repr_represent(self, value):
        if isinstance(value, object) and hasattr(value, 'to_dict_repr'):
            return value.to_dict_repr() # pyright: ignore[reportAttributeAccessIssue]
        return self._represent(value)

    @override
    def __setstate__(self, state: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        state = copy.copy(state)
        compnames = self.get_component_attributes()
        for cn in compnames:
            if '_'+ cn in state and not cn in state:
                state[cn] = state['_' + cn]
                del state['_' + cn]

        super().__setstate__(state)

    def __deepcopy__(self, memo):
        cls = self.__class__
        result = cls.__new__(cls)
        memo[id(self)] = result

        cls.set_state_exclusion_policy('excluded')
        state = copy.deepcopy(self.__getstate__())
        cls.set_state_exclusion_policy('excluded_and_components')

        result.__setstate__(state)

        return result

    @staticmethod
    def _anonymise_id_sequence(seq: SequenceNotStr):
        for x in seq:
            if isinstance(x, NewsegsComponent):
                x.anonymise_ids()
            elif isinstance(x, Mapping):
                NewsegsComponent._anonymise_id_sequence(tuple(x.values()))
            elif not isinstance(x, str) and isinstance(x, Sequence):
                NewsegsComponent._anonymise_id_sequence(x) # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]

    @override
    def anonymise_ids(self):
        super().anonymise_ids()
        self._anonymise_id_sequence(self.get_components())            

    def get_component_attributes(self) -> tuple['str', ...]:
        """A tuple of all the attributes of the object that are themselves NewsegsComponents"""
        type_ = type(self)

        # Strip out dunders and single unders - the properties will not have a leading underscore
        atts = tuple(k for k in dir(type_) if not k.startswith('_'))
        atts = tuple(k for k in atts if isinstance(getattr(type_, k), ComponentPropertyInterface))
        return atts

    @staticmethod
    def _recursive_get_component(atts: NewsegsComponent | Iterable) -> list['NewsegsComponent']:
        rlist = []

        if isinstance(atts, NewsegsComponent):
            rlist.append(atts)
        elif isinstance(atts, Mapping):
            for x in atts.values():
                rlist.extend(NewsegsComponent._recursive_get_component(x))
            #(rlist.extend(NewsegsComponent._recursive_get_component(x)) for x in atts.values())
        elif isinstance(atts, Iterable):
            for x in atts:
                rlist.extend(NewsegsComponent._recursive_get_component(x))
            #(rlist.extend(NewsegsComponent._recursive_get_component(x)) for x in atts)
        return rlist                

    def get_components(self, component_group: Optional[PREFIX_GROUP_KEY] = None) -> tuple['NewsegsComponent', ...]:
        """A tuple of all subcomponents that would require saving to store and reattaching after deserialisation."""
        attnames = self.get_component_attributes()
        excl = self._excluded_attributes
        attnames = (x for x in attnames if '_'+x not in excl)

        atts = []
        for nm in attnames:
            try:
                atts.append(getattr(self, nm))
            except AttributeError:
                pass

        components = self._recursive_get_component(atts)

        if component_group is not None:
            prefixes = set(x+'-' for x in PREFIX_GROUPS[component_group])
            # Creatig a generator function doesn't seem to work
            sublist = []
            for x in components:
                if any(x.id.startswith(y) for y in prefixes):
                    sublist.append(x)
            components = sublist
            #components = (x for x in components if not any(x.id.startswith(y) for y in prefixes))

        return tuple(components)

    def update_component_id_dict(self):
        """Update ._component_ids prior to serialisation."""
        self._component_ids.clear()
        att_names = self.get_component_attributes()
        for att in att_names:
            comp = getattr(self, att)
            if isinstance(comp, NewsegsComponent):
                self._component_ids[att] = comp.id

    def reattach_components(
        self,
        component_provider: NewsegsComponentProviderInterface
    ):
        """Using the component_provider, find all components for reattachment."""
        r0 = self.revision
        prefixes = tuple(x+'-' for x in PREFIX_GROUPS['component_configs'])
        for att_name, comp_id in self._component_ids.items():
            if any(comp_id.startswith(y) for y in prefixes):
                comp = component_provider.get_component(comp_id)
                setattr(self, att_name, comp)
        # Ensure that revision is not incremented due to reattachment
        self.revision = r0

    def _get_component_properties(self):
        # Stage 1 - strip out the dunders
        comp_props = [x for x in dir(self) if not x.startswith('__')]
        # Stage 2 - check has attribute
        comp_props = [x for x in comp_props if hasattr(self, x)]
        # Stage 3 - check has '_last_syncronised'
        comp_props = [x for x in comp_props if hasattr(getattr(self, x), '_last_syncronised')]
        # Stage 4 - keep only the single underscore versions
        comp_props.sort()
        r_props = set()
        for x in comp_props:
            if not '_' + x in r_props:
                r_props.add(x)
        return r_props

    def reset_revision(self, chain: bool = True):
        """Set the revision to 0 and _last_syncronised to -1

        If chain, also perform this for all ComponentProperties
    """
        if chain:
            comps = self.get_components()
            for att in comps:
                if hasattr(att, 'reset_revision'):
                    att.reset_revision(chain = chain)
                else:
                    att._revision = 0
                    att._last_syncronised = -1

            # Also go through the root attributes to get the containers
            comp_atts = self.get_component_attributes()
            for attname in comp_atts:
                att = getattr(self, attname)
                # No need to repeat for non-containers
                if not att in comps:
                    if hasattr(att, 'reset_revision'):
                        att.reset_revision(chain = chain)
                    else:
                        if att is not None:
                            att._revision = 0
                            att._last_syncronised = -1
        self._config._revision = 0
        self._config._last_syncronised = -1

    @property
    def dirty(self):
        """Whether the component, or any of its children, has been modified since it was last synchronised with storage.
        """
        return self.chain_modified

class DataWithRevision(SubscriptionRevisionNotifierMixin, serialisation.SerialiseToDictMixin, metaclass = RevisionDataMeta):
    """Base class for all revision-tracked dataclasses."""
    _constructor_class = 'DataWithRevision'
    _excluded_attributes = serialisation.SerialiseToDictMixin._excluded_attributes.union({'_children', '_subscribers'})

    @override
    def update(self, config: dict[str, Any] | type[T]):
        if not isinstance(config, dict):
            return super().update(config) # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]

        type_ = type(self)
        config = config.copy()
        classname = config.pop('class', None)
        if not classname is None:
            if self.__class__.__name__ != classname:
                raise ValueError(f'Configuration for class {classname} cannot be applied to an instance of class {self.__class__.__name__}')

        # Get rid of constructor class string for this instance
        config.pop('constructor_class', None)

        config = type_.unserialise_dict(config)

        # Store revision so it can be reset after property set
        r0 = config.get('_revision', None)

        # Check existing attributes to see if they can be updated
        conf_keys = config.keys()
        has_update = {}
        for k, v in vars(self).items():
            if k in conf_keys:
                if hasattr(v, 'update'):
                    has_update[k] = config[k]

        # Attributes that can be updated should not be set
        for k in has_update.keys():
            config.pop(k)

        # Attributes that can be updated should be set using setattr, for custom logic
        for v, k in config.items():
            setattr(self, v, k)

        # Updatable attributes are now set
        for k, v in has_update.items():
            getattr(self, k).update(v)

        # Set revision to as recorded
        if r0 is not None:
            self._revision = r0


    @classmethod
    @override
    def from_dict(cls, config):
        inst = cls.__new__(cls)
        inst._children = []
        inst._subscribers = []
        inst.update(config)
        return inst

class NewsegsComponentProviderInterface(metaclass = ABCMeta):
    """Interface for providing components when given their ids."""

    @overload
    @abstractmethod
    def get_component(self, component_id: str) -> NewsegsComponent:
        ...

    @overload
    @abstractmethod
    def get_component(self, component_id: SequenceNotStr[str]) -> SequenceNotStr[NewsegsComponent]:
        ...

    def get_component(self, component_id: str | SequenceNotStr[str]) -> NewsegsComponent | SequenceNotStr[NewsegsComponent]:
        """Get the component with an id, or components with a sequence of ids.

        Args:
            component_id: Id(s) of the component(s).

        Returns:
            The component, or sequence of components.
        """
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    def duplicate_component(self, component_id: str | NewsegsComponent) -> NewsegsComponent:
        """Make a copy of a component with new ids.

    def add_component(self, component: NewsegsComponent) -> str:
        """Add a component to the provider.

        """Get the default component of a type.

        Args:

            index: Which instance of the component type to return, in the order added; -1 is the most recent.

    def get_component_metadata(
        self,
        component_id: str | SequenceNotStr[str],
        metadata_ids: str | SequenceNotStr[str]
    ) -> dict[str, Any] | dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
        """Get metadata of components, e.g. the label or revision, without constructing them.

        Args:
            component_id: Id(s) of the component(s).
            metadata_ids: Name(s) of the metadata field(s) wanted.

        Returns:
            Dictionary of metadata for a single component, or a dictionary of these by component id.
        """
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    def set_component_metadata(
        self,
        component_id: str,
        metadata_id: str,
        metadata_value: Any
    ):
        """Directly set a field in the table. Use with caution!"""

class DictionaryComponentProvider(NewsegsComponentProviderInterface):
    """Component provider which holds the components in a dictionary by id.
    """
    def __init__(
        self,
        comp_dict: dict
    ) -> None:
        self.comp_dict = comp_dict

    @overload
    def get_component(self, component_id: str) -> NewsegsComponent:
        ...

    @overload
    def get_component(self, component_id: SequenceNotStr[str]) -> SequenceNotStr[NewsegsComponent]:
        ...

    def get_component(
        self, 
        component_id: str | SequenceNotStr[str]
    ) -> NewsegsComponent | SequenceNotStr[NewsegsComponent]:
        """Get the component with an id, or components with a sequence of ids.

        Raises `KeyError` if a component is not found.

        Args:
            component_id: Id(s) of the component(s).

        Returns:
            The component, or list of components.
        """
        if isinstance(component_id, str):
            return self.comp_dict[component_id]
        else:
            return[self.comp_dict[x] for x in component_id]

    def duplicate_component(
        self, 
        component_id: str | NewsegsComponent
    ) -> NewsegsComponent:
        """Make a deep copy of a component.

        Args:
            component_id: Id(s) of the component(s).

        Returns:
            The copy.
        """
        if isinstance(component_id, str):
            return copy.deepcopy(self.comp_dict[component_id])
        else:
            return copy.deepcopy(component_id)

    def add_component(
        self,
        component: NewsegsComponent
    ) -> str:
        """Add a component to the dictionary under its id.

        Args:
            component: The component.

        Returns:
            The id of the component.
        """
        self.comp_dict[component.id] = component
        return component.id

    def get_default_component(
        self, 
        component_type: str, 
        index: int = -1
    ) -> NewsegsComponent:
        """Get the first component held.

        The type and index are ignored.

        Args:
            component_type: The type of the component (e.g. `model`, `finance`).
            index: Which instance of the component type to return, in the order added; -1 is the most recent.

        Returns:
            The component.
        """
        return next(iter(self.comp_dict.values()))

    def get_component_metadata(
        self, 
        component_id: str | SequenceNotStr[str], 
        metadata_ids: str | SequenceNotStr[str]
    ) -> dict[str, Any] | dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:

            metadata_ids: Name(s) of the metadata field(s) wanted.

        Returns:

    ):
        """Not supported: does nothing.

        Args:

            metadata_id: Name of the metadata field.
            metadata_value: The value to set.

    def increment_revision(self, component_id):
        self.comp_dict[component_id].revision += 1

class TableOwningMixin(_Base):
    """Mixin that adds table_config behavior to any NewsegsComponent subclass."""

    table_config = ComponentProperty(default = TableConfigNewsegsComponent)

    @override
    def _preupdate_from_dict(self, config):
        super()._preupdate_from_dict(config)
        # Table needs to be created early, for attachment by tablemodifyingproperties

        table_config_exists = hasattr(self, '_table_config')
        full_update = False

        inst_table = config.pop('_table_config', config.pop('table_config', None))
        if inst_table:
            if isinstance(inst_table, NewsegsComponent):
                self.table_config = inst_table
                table_config_exists = True
                full_update = True
            elif isinstance(inst_table, Mapping):
                if not table_config_exists:
                    full_update = True
                    table_config_exists = True
                tc = self.table_config # Should generate a default if not present
                for k, v in inst_table.items():
                    setattr(tc, k, v)
            else:
                raise TypeError(f'Unsupported type for table config update: {type(inst_table)}')

        # If the table config doesn't actually exist yet, force it to so we can reset the revision
        # after configuration completes
        if not table_config_exists:
            full_update = True

        if full_update:
            object.__setattr__(self, '_table_config_revis_0', self.table_config.revision)

    @override
    def _post_update_from_dict(self):
        if hasattr(self, '_table_config_revis_0'):
            self.table_config.revision = self._table_config_revis_0
            delattr(self, '_table_config_revis_0')
        super()._post_update_from_dict()

def parse_component_version(version: str) -> tuple[int, ...]:
    """Convert a version string, such as `'0.1.0'` or `'v0.0.1'`, to a tuple of integers for comparison.

    Args:
        version: The version string.

    Returns:
        The parts of the version as integers.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the version is not of the form `[v]major.minor.patch`.
    """
    try:
        return tuple(int(x) for x in str(version).lstrip('v').split('.'))
    except ValueError:
        raise ValueError(f'Unrecognised component version: {version}') from None

class RevisionNotifierMixin():
    """Handles part-child notifications and revision counts"""

    # The notification state of a thread which has not set one
    _rn_config = {
        'notify': 'broadcast'
    }

    def __init__(
        self, 
        children: Optional[Collection['RevisionNotifierMixin']] = None
    ):
        self._last_syncronised = 0
        self._revision = 0
        self._children = []
        if children is not None:
            for x in children:
                self._add_child(x)

    def _add_child(self, child: RevisionNotifierProtocol, subscribe: bool = True):

        if child is self:
            raise ValueError('Circular reference - cannot add self as child.')

        # Can hold multiple copies of a child - Removals MUST be performed.
        self._children.append(child)

        if subscribe and isinstance(child, SubscriptionRevisionNotifierMixin):
            child._subscribers.append(self)

    def _remove_child(self, child: RevisionNotifierProtocol):
        # Don't use remove, need to check for instance equality
        for idx, inlist in enumerate(self._children):
            if inlist is child:
                # Pop the first, then stop. If multiple entries for child, that's OK.
                self._children.pop(idx)

                # Don't like testing against an inheriting class, but it gets the job done
                if isinstance(child, SubscriptionRevisionNotifierMixin):
                    child.unsubscribe(self)

                return

    @classmethod
    def _get_notification_state(cls) -> NOTIFY_STATE:
        """The notification state of the current thread."""
        return getattr(_notification_state, 'notify', cls._rn_config['notify'])

    @classmethod
    def _set_notification_state(cls, state: NOTIFY_STATE = 'broadcast') -> NOTIFY_STATE:
        """Set the notification state of the current thread.

        Args:
            state: The state.

        Returns:
            The previous state, to restore.
        """
        prevstate = cls._get_notification_state()
        _notification_state.notify = state
        return prevstate

    @property
    def revision(self) -> int:
        """The revision number: it increases by one when the object is changed after having been synchronised.
        """
        return self._revision

    @revision.setter
    def revision(self, revision: int):
        self._revision = revision

    def _notify_change(self, trigger: Any | None = None, **kwargs):
        if self._get_notification_state() == 'disabled':
            return

        if not hasattr(self, '_revision'):
            self._revision = 0
        if not self.modified:
            self._revision += 1

    def _syncronise(self):
        """Use after saving status (to database)"""
        self._last_syncronised = self.revision

    def _chain_syncronise(self):
        self._syncronise()
        for child in self._children:
            child._chain_syncronise()

    @property
    def modified(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the object has changed since it was last synchronised (e.g. with storage).
        """
        return self._last_syncronised != self.revision

    @property
    def chain_modified(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the object, or any of its children, has changed since it was last synchronised.
        """
        return (
            self.modified 
            or any((child.chain_modified for child in self._children))
        )

    def __setstate__(self, state):

        r0 = state.pop("_revision", [])
        object.__setattr__(self, "_revision", r0)
        object.__setattr__(self, "_children", state.pop("_children", []))


        # Restore remaining state (invokes __setattr__ for each remaining key)
        for key, value in state.items():
            setattr(self, key, value)

        # Reset revision
        setattr(self, "_revision", r0)

    def __getstate__(self) -> dict:
        odict = copy.copy(vars(self))
        del odict['_children']

        return odict

class SubscriptionRevisionNotifierMixin(RevisionNotifierMixin):
    """Extends RevisionNotifierMixin to increment subscriber revisions when change occurs"""

    @classmethod
    def _wrap_value(cls, val: Any, subscribers: Iterable[RevisionNotifierProtocol]) -> Any:

        return val

        subscribers: Optional[RevisionNotifierProtocol | Iterable[RevisionNotifierProtocol]] = None,
        **kwargs
        ):
        if subscribers is not None:
            if isinstance(subscribers, RevisionNotifierProtocol):
                self._subscribers = [subscribers,]
            else:
                self._subscribers = list(subscribers)
        else:
            self._subscribers = []
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)

    @override
    def _notify_change(self, trigger: Any | None = None, broadcast: bool = True, **kwargs):
        trigger = self if trigger is None else trigger
        super()._notify_change(trigger = trigger, broadcast = broadcast, **kwargs)

        if self._get_notification_state() == 'broadcast' and broadcast:
            for subscriber in self._subscribers:
                subscriber._notify_change(trigger = trigger, broadcast = broadcast, **kwargs)

    def subscribe(self, subscriber: 'RevisionNotifierProtocol | ConfigurationMixin'):
        # Addition to subscriber list occurs in _add_child
        """Subscribe an object to the changes of this one.

        The subscriber has this object as a child, so changes here count as changes of the subscriber.

        Args:
            subscriber: The object to be notified of changes (a revision notifier or a component).
        """
        if isinstance(subscriber, ConfigurationMixin):
            subscriber._config._add_child(self, subscribe = True)
        else:
            subscriber._add_child(self, subscribe = True)

    def unsubscribe(self, subscriber: 'RevisionNotifierProtocol | ConfigurationMixin'):
        """Stop notifying a subscriber of changes.

        If the subscriber is subscribed several times, one subscription is removed.

        Args:
            subscriber: The object to be notified of changes (a revision notifier or a component).
        """
        if isinstance(subscriber, ConfigurationMixin):
            search_subscriber = subscriber._config
        else:
            search_subscriber = subscriber
        for idx, x in enumerate(self._subscribers):
            if x is search_subscriber:
                # Pop the first, then stop. If multiple entries for subscriber, that's OK.
                self._subscribers.pop(idx)
                return

    def __setstate__(self, state):

        object.__setattr__(self, "_subscribers", state.pop("_subscribers", []))
        super().__setstate__(state)

    def __getstate__(self) -> dict:
        odict =  super().__getstate__()
        del odict['_subscribers']
        return odict

class DataWithRevision(SubscriptionRevisionNotifierMixin, serialisation.SerialiseToDictMixin, metaclass = RevisionDataMeta):
    """Base class for all revision-tracked dataclasses."""
    _constructor_class = 'DataWithRevision'
    _excluded_attributes = serialisation.SerialiseToDictMixin._excluded_attributes.union({'_children', '_subscribers'})

    @override
    def update(self, config: dict[str, Any] | type[T]):
        if not isinstance(config, dict):
            return super().update(config) # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]

        type_ = type(self)
        config = config.copy()
        classname = config.pop('class', None)
        if not classname is None:
            if self.__class__.__name__ != classname:
                raise ValueError(f'Configuration for class {classname} cannot be applied to an instance of class {self.__class__.__name__}')

        # Get rid of constructor class string for this instance
        config.pop('constructor_class', None)

        config = type_.unserialise_dict(config)

        # Store revision so it can be reset after property set
        r0 = config.get('_revision', None)

        # Check existing attributes to see if they can be updated
        conf_keys = config.keys()
        has_update = {}
        for k, v in vars(self).items():
            if k in conf_keys:
                if hasattr(v, 'update'):
                    has_update[k] = config[k]

        # Attributes that can be updated should not be set
        for k in has_update.keys():
            config.pop(k)

        # Attributes that can be updated should be set using setattr, for custom logic
        for v, k in config.items():
            setattr(self, v, k)

        # Updatable attributes are now set
        for k, v in has_update.items():
            getattr(self, k).update(v)

        # Set revision to as recorded
        if r0 is not None:
            self._revision = r0


    @classmethod
    @override
    def from_dict(cls, config):
        inst = cls.__new__(cls)
        inst._children = []
        inst._subscribers = []
        inst.update(config)
        return inst

class ConfigurationMixin:
    """Mixin for components whose changeable state is held in a revision-tracked `_config` object.

    Reads and writes of the fields of the configuration are redirected to it, so setting
    `component.x = y` for a field `x` of the configuration changes `_config`, which counts the revision.
    The mixin also gives each component a unique, prefixed id and passes on the revision of the configuration.

    Attributes:
        _config: The configuration, a `DataWithRevision`.
        uuid: The unique part of the id.
    """
    _config: DataWithRevision

    _id_prefix: str = COMPONENT_PREFIXES['component']

    uuid: str = '1'
    component_type = 'abstract'

    @classmethod
    def _make_id_regex(cls):
        return re.compile(rf'^{re.escape(cls._id_prefix)}' + r'-([0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12})$')

    @classmethod
    def generate_new_id(cls) -> str:
        """A new unique id with the prefix of the component type.

        Returns:
            The id.
        """
        return cls._id_prefix + '-' + str(mod_uuid.uuid4())

    @property
    def id(self) -> str:
        """The id of the component: the prefix of the component type, and the unique id.
        """
        return self._id_prefix + '-' + self.uuid

    @id.setter
    def id(self, id: str) -> None:
        uid = self._make_id_regex().search(id)
        if uid is None:
            raise ValueError(f'id: {id} is not a valid {type(self)} identifier')
        uid = uid.group(1)
        self.uuid = uid

    def anonymise_ids(self):
        """Replace the id with a new one, e.g. after copying a component.
        """
        self.id = self.generate_new_id()

    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        self._config = self._generate_config(*args, **kwargs)

    def _generate_config(self, *args, **kwargs) -> DataWithRevision:
        """Return an implementation of DataWithRevision in order to set _config"""
        return NoConfig(*args, **kwargs)

    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Any:
        # Called ONLY when 'name' is not found on the Component instance or class
        # ... in theory, anyway

        config = self.__dict__.get('_config')
        if config is not None and hasattr(config, name):
            return getattr(config, name)

        raise AttributeError(f'"{type(self).__name__}" object has no attribute "{name}"')

    def __setattr__(self, name: str, value: Any):
        # We end up here even if a setter has been created on the main component, so need to check
        # for that.
        if hasattr(self.__class__, name):
            att = getattr(self.__class__, name)
            if hasattr(att, 'fset'):
                return getattr(att, 'fset')(self, value)

        # Bypass custom logic for internal private attributes or initial _config setup
        if name == '_config' or name.startswith('_'):
            super().__setattr__(name, value)
            return

        config = getattr(self, '_config', None)
        # If attribute belongs to _config dataclass, set it on _config
        if config is not None and hasattr(config, name):
            setattr(config, name, value)
            return

        # Default to setting attribute directly on Component instance
        super().__setattr__(name, value)

    def __copy__(self):
        # Create a new instance without triggering __init__
        cls = self.__class__
        new_obj = cls.__new__(cls)

        # Shallow copy the instance dict to preserve attributes
        new_dict = self.__dict__.copy()

        # Create a shallow copy of _config instead of sharing the reference
        if '_config' in new_dict and new_dict['_config'] is not None:
            new_dict['_config'] = copy.copy(new_dict['_config'])

        # Update the new instance dict using object.__setattr__ / dict.update
        # to avoid triggering custom __setattr__ logic
        new_obj.__dict__.update(new_dict)

        return new_obj

    @property 
    def revision(self) -> int:
        """The revision number of the configuration.
        """
        return self._config.revision

    @revision.setter
    def revision(self, revision: int):
        """Use with caution - direct setting of the revision number"""
        self._config._revision = revision

    @property
    def modified(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the configuration has changed since it was last synchronised.
        """
        return self._config.modified

    @property
    def chain_modified(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the configuration, or any of its children, has changed since it was last synchronised.
        """
        return self._config.chain_modified

    def syncronise(self):
        """Mark the configuration as synchronised (e.g. after saving it to storage).
        """
        self._config._syncronise()

    def chain_syncronise(self):
        """Mark the configuration and all its children as synchronised.
        """
        self._config._chain_syncronise()

class ObservableList(list, SubscriptionRevisionNotifierMixin):
    """List wrapper that triggers revision increment on mutation."""

    def __init__(
        self, 
        iterable = (), 
        subscribers: Optional[
            RevisionNotifierProtocol
            | ConfigurationMixin 
            | Iterable[RevisionNotifierProtocol| ConfigurationMixin]
        ] = None,
        **kwargs
    ):
        if subscribers is None:
            subscribers = []
        elif isinstance(subscribers, RevisionNotifierProtocol) or isinstance(subscribers, ConfigurationMixin):
            subscribers = [subscribers]

        subscribers = [
            subscriber._config if isinstance(subscriber, ConfigurationMixin) else subscriber 
            for subscriber in subscribers
        ]

        SubscriptionRevisionNotifierMixin.__init__(self, subscribers = subscribers)

        # Wrap to all subscribers, not just self
        wrapped = [self._wrap_value(item, [self,]) for item in iterable]
        super().__init__(wrapped)

        # Also add self as a child to all subscribers
        for subscriber in self._subscribers:
            subscriber._add_child(self, subscribe = False)

    def __setitem__(self, index, value):
        old_val = super().__getitem__(index)
        new_val = self._wrap_value(value, [self] + self._subscribers)
        if old_val != new_val:
            recursive_remove_children(self, old_val)
            super().__setitem__(index, new_val)
            self._notify_change()

    def append(self, item):
        """Append an item, counting a change.

        Args:
            item: The item.
        """
        super().append(self._wrap_value(item, [self]))
        self._notify_change()

    def extend(self, iterable: Iterable) -> None:
        """Append items, counting a change.

        Args:
            iterable: The items.
        """
        wrapped = [self._wrap_value(item, [self]) for item in iterable]
        if wrapped:
            super().extend(wrapped)
            self._notify_change()

    def insert(self, index, item):
        """Insert an item, counting a change.

        Args:
            index: Which instance of the component type to return, in the order added; -1 is the most recent.
            item: The item.
        """
        super().insert(index, self._wrap_value(item, [self]))
        self._notify_change()

    def pop(self, index: SupportsIndex = -1):
        """Remove and return an item, counting a change and releasing the item.

        Args:
            index: Which instance of the component type to return, in the order added; -1 is the most recent.

        Returns:
            The item.
        """
        item = super().pop(index)
        self._notify_change()

        recursive_remove_children(self, item)
        return item

    def remove(self, value):
        """Remove the first occurrence of a value, counting a change and releasing the item.

        Raises `ValueError` if the value is absent.

        Args:
            value: The value.
        """
        try:
            idx = self.index(value)
            item = self[idx]
        except ValueError:
            # Let the standard error be raised
            super().remove(value)
            return
        recursive_remove_children(self, item)

        super().remove(value)
        self._notify_change()

    def clear(self):
        """Remove all items, counting a change.
        """
        if len(self) > 0:
            super().clear()
            self._children = []
            self._notify_change()

    def __reduce_ex__(self, protocol):
        items = list(self)

        # Return constructor, positional args, state dict, and list iterator
        # Pickle will reconstruct instance -> set state -> extend items
        state = self.__getstate__()

        return (self.__class__, (), state, iter(items))

class ObservableDict(dict, SubscriptionRevisionNotifierMixin):
    """Dictionary wrapper that triggers revision increment on mutation."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        mapping = (),
        subscribers: Optional[
            RevisionNotifierProtocol 
            | ConfigurationMixin 
            | Iterable[RevisionNotifierProtocol | ConfigurationMixin]
        ] = None,
        **kwargs
    ):
        if subscribers is None:
            subscribers = []
        elif isinstance(subscribers, RevisionNotifierProtocol) or isinstance(subscribers, ConfigurationMixin):
            subscribers = [subscribers]

        subscribers = [
            subscriber._config if isinstance(subscriber, ConfigurationMixin) else subscriber 
            for subscriber in subscribers
        ]

        SubscriptionRevisionNotifierMixin.__init__(self, subscribers = subscribers)
        initial = dict(mapping, **kwargs)

        wrapped = {k: self._wrap_value(v, [self,]) for k, v in initial.items()}
        super().__init__(wrapped)

        # Also add self as a child to all subscribers
        for subscriber in self._subscribers:
            subscriber._add_child(self, subscribe = False)

    def _safe_remove_child_value(self, val):
        """Call after deleting a value from the dict to delete the child if not referenced by another key"""
        if not isinstance(val, IMMUTABLE_TYPES):
            # NB - if old val is an immutable, it won't have been added as a child
            recursive_remove_children(self, val)

    def __setitem__(self, key: Any, value: Any) -> None:
        exists = key in self
        old_val = self.get(key) if exists else None
        new_val = self._wrap_value(value, [self])

        if isinstance(old_val, IMMUTABLE_TYPES):
            equal = old_val == new_val
        else:
            equal = old_val is new_val

        if not exists or not equal:
            super().__setitem__(key, new_val)
            self._notify_change()
            self._safe_remove_child_value(old_val)

    def __delitem__(self, key):
        old_val = self.get(key)

        super().__delitem__(key)
        self._safe_remove_child_value(old_val)

        self._notify_change()

    def update(self, *args, **kwargs):
        """Update from a mapping, counting a change if a value is new or different.

        Args:
            *args: Further positional arguments.
            **kwargs: Further keyword arguments.
        """
        other = dict(*args, **kwargs)
        changed = False
        for k, v in other.items():
            wrapped_v = self._wrap_value(v, [self])
            if k not in self or self[k] != wrapped_v:
                old_val = self.get(k)
                super().__setitem__(k, wrapped_v)
                self._safe_remove_child_value(old_val)
                changed = True
        if changed:
            self._notify_change()

    def pop(self, key, *args):
        """Remove and return an item, counting a change and releasing the item.

        As `dict.pop`, a default may be given.

        Args:
            key: The key.
            *args: Further positional arguments.

        Returns:
            The item.
        """
        if key in self:
            item = super().pop(key)
            self._notify_change()
            self._safe_remove_child_value(item)
            return item
        return super().pop(key, *args)

    def clear(self):
        """Remove all items, counting a change.
        """
        if len(self) > 0:
            for item in self.values():
                self._safe_remove_child_value(item)
            super().clear()
            self._children = []
            self._notify_change()

    def __reduce_ex__(self, protocol):
        dict_items = dict(self)

        # Return constructor, positional args, state dict, and list iterator
        # Pickle will reconstruct instance -> set state -> extend items
        state = self.__getstate__()

        # Return (cls, positional_args, state, key_value_iterator)
        return (self.__class__, (), state, None, iter(dict_items.items()))

class ObservableOrderedDict(ObservableDict, OrderedDict):
    """An ObservableDict that maintains key insertion order using OrderedDict."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        mapping = (),
        subscribers: Optional[
            RevisionNotifierProtocol
            | ConfigurationMixin 
            | Iterable[RevisionNotifierProtocol| ConfigurationMixin]
        ] = None,
        **kwargs

        if subscribers is None:
            subscribers = []
        elif isinstance(subscribers, RevisionNotifierProtocol) or isinstance(subscribers, ConfigurationMixin):
            subscribers = [subscribers]

        subscribers = [
            subscriber._config if isinstance(subscriber, ConfigurationMixin) else subscriber 
            for subscriber in subscribers
        ]

        SubscriptionRevisionNotifierMixin.__init__(self, subscribers = subscribers)
        initial = dict(mapping, **kwargs)

        OrderedDict.__init__(self)
        initial = OrderedDict(mapping, **kwargs)
        for k, v in initial.items():
            self[k] = v  # Trigger __setitem__ wrapping and subscriber setup

        self.revision = 0

        # Also add self as a child to all subscribers
        for subscriber in self._subscribers:
            subscriber._add_child(self, subscribe = False)

        if key in self:
            item = super().pop(key)

            self._safe_remove_child_value(item)

        return super().pop(key, *args, **kwargs)

class TableModifyingObservableOrderedDict(ObservableOrderedDict):

    """An observable ordered dictionary whose changes also change the table configuration of its owner.

    Subscribes both the configuration of the owner and its `table_config`, so that a change here makes the results tables out of date.

        self, 
        mapping=(), 
        subscribers: Optional[
            RevisionNotifierProtocol
            | ConfigurationMixin 
            | Iterable[RevisionNotifierProtocol| ConfigurationMixin] 
        ] = None, 
        **kwargs
    ):
        if subscribers is None:
            subscribers = []
        elif isinstance(subscribers, RevisionNotifierProtocol) or isinstance(subscribers, ConfigurationMixin):
            subscribers = [subscribers]

        # Subscribers should be both the _config and the table_config for eligible types
        working_subscribers = []
        for subscriber in subscribers:
            if isinstance(subscriber, ConfigurationMixin):
                # Only subscribe to the table if available, under the assumption that the config will be subscribed to the table.
                if hasattr(subscriber, 'watcher'):
                    working_subscribers.append(subscriber.watcher)
                if hasattr(subscriber, 'table_config'):
                    working_subscribers.append(getattr(subscriber, 'table_config'))
                else:
                    working_subscribers.append(subscriber._config)
            else:
                working_subscribers.append(subscriber)

        super().__init__(mapping, subscribers = working_subscribers)

class ComponentProperty(ComponentPropertyInterface):
    """Descriptor for attributes which are Components (i.e. inherit ConfigurationMixin)"""

    def __init__(self, default: Any = None, oftype: Optional[type | tuple[type, ...]] = None):
        self.default = default
        self._propname = ""
        self.name = ""
        self.oftype = oftype

    def __set_name__(self, owner: type, name: str):
        self.name = f'_{name}' # Name as stored on object instance

    def __get__(self, instance: Optional['ConfigurationMixin'], owner: type) -> Any:
        if instance is None:
            return self
        att = getattr(instance, self.name, None)

        if att is not None:
            return att

        if isinstance(self.default, Callable):
            default_val = self.default()
        else:
            default_val = self.default

        # Note to set the value on the propname, so that it gets wrapped.
        if self.oftype and isinstance(default_val, self.oftype):
            # Perform a special set so that notification is not fired.
            # Make clear that subscription is requested, so that we know
            # who to remove from when the property is deleted or exchanged.
            instance._config._add_child(default_val._config, subscribe = True)
            setattr(instance, self.name, default_val) 

        return getattr(instance, self.name, default_val) 

    def __set__(self, instance: 'ConfigurationMixin', value: 'ConfigurationMixin'):
        if self.oftype:
            if not isinstance(value, self.oftype):
                raise TypeError(f'"{self.name}" is expected as one of {self.oftype}, is {type(value)}')
        old_val = getattr(instance, self.name, None)

        if old_val is not None:
            if old_val._config is not value._config:
                # A ComponentProperty should only be subscribed to by the _config
                # of its parent Components.
                instance._remove_child(old_val._config)


                #old_subscribers = [x for x in old_val._subscribers]
                #for subscriber in old_subscribers:
                #    subscriber._remove_child(old_val._config)

            else:
                # No real need to do anything
                setattr(instance, self.name, value)
                return

            #for subscriber in old_subscribers:
                # Form a revision loop with the old subscribers
                #subscriber._add_child(value._config, subscribe = True)

        # Form a revision loop with the parent Component config    
        instance._add_child(value._config, subscribe = True)

        # Only notify the last added subscriber
        value._config._subscribers[-1]._notify_change()
        #for subscriber in value._config._subscribers:
        #    subscriber._notify_change()

        setattr(instance, self.name, value)

class ComponentSubscriptionRevisionNotifierProperty(ComponentPropertyInterface):
    """Descriptor for attributes which are SubscriptionRevisionNotifiers
    """
    def __init__(
        self,
        default: Callable,
        type_: Type,
        oftype: Type | tuple[Type, ...] | None = None
    ):
        self.default = default
        self.type_ = type_
        self.name = ""
        self.oftype = oftype

    def __set_name__(self, owner: type, name: str):
        self.name = f'_{name}' # Name as stored on object instance

    def __get__(self, instance: Optional[ConfigurationMixin], owner: type) -> Any:
        if instance is None:
            return self
        att = getattr(instance, self.name, None)

        if att is not None:
            return att

        default_val = self.default()
        # Perform a special set so that notification is not fired.
        instance._add_child(default_val, subscribe = True)
        setattr(instance, self.name, default_val) 

        return getattr(instance, self.name, default_val)

    def __set__(self, instance: ConfigurationMixin, value: Any):
        # TODO: Handle oftype

        old_val = getattr(instance, self.name, None)
        if old_val is value:
            # Nothing to do

        if not isinstance(value, self.type_):
            value = self.type_(value)

        if old_val is not None:
            instance._remove_child(old_val)
        # Form a revision loop with the parent Component config    
        instance._add_child(value, subscribe = True)

        # Only notify the last added subscriber
        value._subscribers[-1]._notify_change()

        setattr(instance, self.name, value)

class TableModifyingComponentSRNProperty(ComponentSubscriptionRevisionNotifierProperty):
    """Property for observable containers whose changes also change the table configuration of the owner.

    Like `ComponentSubscriptionRevisionNotifierProperty`, but the container is attached to the `table_config` of the owner (if it has one),
    as well as its configuration.
    """
    @override
    def __set__(self, instance: ConfigurationMixin, value: Any):
        old_val = getattr(instance, self.name, None)
        if old_val is value:
            # Nothing to do
            return

        if not isinstance(value, self.type_):
            value = self.type_(value)

        if old_val is not None:
            if hasattr(instance, 'table_config'):
                instance.table_config._remove_child(old_val)
            else:
                instance._remove_child(old_val)
            if hasattr(instance, 'watcher'):
                instance.watcher._remove_child(old_val)

        n_subscribers = 0
        if hasattr(instance, 'table_config'):
            instance.table_config._add_child(value, subscribe = True)
            n_subscribers += 1
        else:
            instance._add_child(value, subscribe = True)
            n_subscribers += 1
        if hasattr(instance, 'watcher'):
            instance.watcher._add_child(value, subscribe = True)
            n_subscribers += 1

        # Notify new subscribers
        for idx in range(-n_subscribers, 0, 1):
            value._subscribers[idx]._notify_change()

        setattr(instance, self.name, value)

@dataclass_transform()
def revision_dataclass(cls: Type[T]) -> Type[T]:
    """Class decorator applying dataclass setup and intercepting attribute changes."""

    # 1. Transform into a dataclass first
    cls = dataclass(cls)

    # Flag that decorator was applied
    cls._is_revision_dataclass = True # pyright: ignore[reportAttributeAccessIssue]

    # Capture the dataclass-generated __init__
    orig_init = cls.__init__

    def new_init(self, *args, **kwargs):
        # Initialize internal revision tracking before dataclass assigns fields
        SubscriptionRevisionNotifierMixin.__init__(self)

        # Run standard dataclass initializer
        orig_init(self, *args, **kwargs)

        # Reset revision to 0
        self._revision = 0

    def new_setattr(self, name: str, value: Any):
        # Allow internal variables or setup prior to _revision existence

        if name.startswith("_") or "_revision" not in self.__dict__:
            object.__setattr__(self, name, value)
            return

        has_old = hasattr(self, name)
        old_val = getattr(self, name, None)
        try:
            if isinstance(
                value, 
                IMMUTABLE_TYPES#(int, float, str, bool, bytes, complex, type(None))
            ):
                equal = np.all(old_val == value)
            else:
                equal = value is old_val
        except ValueError:
            equal = False

        if not has_old or not equal:
            if has_old:
                recursive_remove_children(self, old_val)

            new_val = wrap_value(value, self)

            object.__setattr__(self, name, new_val)
            self._notify_change(self)

    # Override methods on class
    cls.__init__ = new_init
    cls.__setattr__ = new_setattr

    return cls

def wrap_value(val: Any, parent: RevisionNotifierProtocol) -> Any:
    """Wraps mutable structures or assigns children to parent objects."""
    if isinstance(val, RevisionNotifierProtocol):
        parent._add_child(val)
        return val
    elif isinstance(val, ConfigurationMixin):
        val.subscribe(parent)
        return val
    elif isinstance(val, list):
        if isinstance(val, ObservableList):
            val.subscribe(parent)
            return val
        else:
            return ObservableList(val, subscribers = parent)
    elif isinstance(val, dict):
        if isinstance(val, ObservableDict):
            val.subscribe(parent)
            return val
        else:
            return ObservableDict(val, subscribers = parent)
    elif isinstance(val, str):
        return val        
    elif isinstance(val, Iterable) and not isinstance(val, RevisionNotifierProtocol) and not isinstance(val, np.ndarray):
       for x in val:
           if isinstance(x, RevisionNotifierProtocol):
               parent._add_child(x)
    return val

def recursive_remove_children(obj, child_item):
    """Release a child, or the children within a collection, from an object.

    Strings and arrays are not searched. Used when values are replaced or removed so that stale children do not keep notifying the parent.

    Args:
        obj: The object whose children are tracked.
        child_item: The child, or collection of children, to remove.
    """
    if child_item is None:
        return
    if isinstance(child_item, RevisionNotifierProtocol):
        obj._remove_child(child_item)
    elif isinstance(child_item, ConfigurationMixin):
        obj._remove_child(child_item._config)
    elif isinstance(child_item, str):
        return
    elif isinstance(child_item, Iterable) and not isinstance(child_item, np.ndarray):
       for x in child_item:
           recursive_remove_children(obj, x)

docs.text:
Classes and mixins related to serialising and unserialising objects.

Classes inheriting the SerialiseToDictMixin are intended to be capable of following this pattern:

  • Instance creation and modification
  • Export of instance configuration to dictionary (.to_dict())
  • Serialisation of dictionary (e.g. to json)
  • Unserialisation of dictionary back to instance of original object (using constructor found by find_constructor)
  • Update of instance using another configuration dictionary or another instance of the same class.

In order to be unserialised as a SerialiseToDictMixin, the class is required to include an attribute ._constructor_class' which must be registered tocore.constructors.registers.CONSTRUCTOR_CLASS_REGISTERusing the decorator functioncore.constructors.registers.register_constructor_class`
