def basic_psa_stats(
    psa_results: pd.DataFrame,
    statistics: Sequence[PSA_FLOAT_STATISTIC] = get_args(PSA_FLOAT_STATISTIC),
    quantiles: Sequence[float] = [0.025, 0.975],
    npv_statistics = [
        'net_present_value_undiscounted',
        'net_present_value_discounted'
    ]
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Summarise the results of a PSA.

    Args:
        psa_results: The results of the PSA, from `run_psa`.
        statistics: The statistics to summarise.
        quantiles: Quantiles to report.
        npv_statistics: The net present value statistics for which to find the probability of being positive.

    Returns:
        A dataframe with a row for each statistic and columns of the deterministic value, the count, mean, median and standard deviation
        of the samples, and the quantiles; and a dataframe of the probability that each net present value is positive.
        Statistics missing from the results (e.g. results from before the statistic was added) are left out.
    """
    statistics = [s for s in statistics if s in psa_results.columns]
    res_det = (
        psa_results
        .query('deterministic == True')
        .loc[:, statistics]
        .sum()
        .to_frame()
        .rename(columns={0:'Deterministic'})
        )

    res_psa_raw = (
        psa_results
        .query('deterministic == False')
        .loc[:, statistics]
    )
    res_psa = (
        res_psa_raw
        .agg(
            ['count', 'mean', 'median', 'std']
        )
        .transpose()
        .rename(columns=lambda x: x.title())
    )
    res_psa_quants = (
        res_psa_raw
        .quantile(quantiles)
        .transpose()
        .rename(columns = lambda x: f'{100.*float(x):.1f} pctile'.replace('.','_'))
    )

    all_res = (
        res_det
        .join(res_psa)
        .join(res_psa_quants)
    )

    prob_positive_npv = (
        res_psa_raw
        .loc[:, npv_statistics]
        .gt(0)
        .mean(axis=0)
        .to_frame() # pyright: ignore[reportAttributeAccessIssue]
        .rename(columns={0:'prob_pos_npv'})
    )

    return all_res, prob_positive_npv

def synchronise_psa_selection(metamodels: Sequence[NewsegsMetaModel]) -> list[str]:
    """Make the PSA selection of variables common to several metamodels consistent.

    A variable (identified by its varid) which is selected for PSA in any of the metamodels is selected in all of
    the metamodels that have it; otherwise it is deselected in all. Only variables which are PSA-possible and
    selectable are changed. Independent instances with the same varid keep their own distributions.

    Args:
        metamodels: The metamodels.

    Returns:
        The varids of the selected variables, in the order in which they first appear in the metamodels.
    """
    order: dict[str, None] = {}
    selected: set[str] = set()
    for mm in metamodels:
        for varid, var in mm.variables.items():
            order.setdefault(varid, None)
            if _psa_variable_is_varied(var):
                selected.add(varid)

    for mm in metamodels:
        for varid, var in mm.variables.items():
            if not _psa_variable_is_candidate(var):
                continue
            is_selected = varid in selected
            if var.psa_selected != is_selected:
                var.psa_selected = is_selected

    return [x for x in order if x in selected]

Run a probabilistic sensitivity analysis across several metamodels (a whole-project PSA).

In each sample every metamodel is run with the same draw of each variable, so that the metamodels can be compared draw by draw. A variable shared by metamodels is a single instance, drawn once. Independent instances with the same varid are drawn with common random numbers - each from a generator seeded identically for the varid and draw - so that instances with the same distribution take the same value, and instances whose distributions differ only in their parameters take correspondingly correlated values. Different variables are drawn independently.

A metamodel which does not have a variable, or for which it cannot be varied, keeps the variable at its deterministic value.

def run_psa_multiple(
    metamodels: Sequence[NewsegsMetaModel],
    statistics: Sequence[PSA_FLOAT_STATISTIC] = get_args(PSA_FLOAT_STATISTIC),
    samples: int = 100,
    seed: int | None = None,
    rng: np.random.Generator | None = None,
    progress: Callable[[int, int], None] | None = None,
    cancel_status: Callable[[], bool] | None = None,
    include_deterministic: bool = True,
    precomputed_deterministic: bool = False,
    synchronise: bool = True,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Run a probabilistic sensitivity analysis across several metamodels (a whole-project PSA).

    In each sample every metamodel is run with the same draw of each variable, so that the metamodels can be
    compared draw by draw. A variable shared by metamodels is a single instance, drawn once. Independent instances
    with the same varid are drawn with common random numbers - each from a generator seeded identically for the
    varid and draw - so that instances with the same distribution take the same value, and instances whose
    distributions differ only in their parameters take correspondingly correlated values. Different variables are
    drawn independently.

    A metamodel which does not have a variable, or for which it cannot be varied, keeps the variable at its
    deterministic value.

    Args:
        metamodels: The metamodels.
        statistics: The statistics to calculate for each run.
        samples: The number of samples to draw.
        seed: Seed of the random number generator, if none is provided.
        rng: Random number generator; used in preference to the seed.
        progress: Function reporting progress, called with the number of runs completed and the total.
        cancel_status: Function returning whether cancellation has been requested; checked before each sample.
        include_deterministic: Whether to include the deterministic run of each metamodel (draw 0).
        precomputed_deterministic: Whether the metamodels already hold valid results of their deterministic runs,
            so that they need not be repeated.
        synchronise: Whether to make the PSA selection of common variables consistent first (see
            `synchronise_psa_selection`).

    Returns:
        Dataframe with a row for each metamodel for each run, and columns `metamodel` (id), `draw` (0 for the
        deterministic run), `deterministic`, the statistics, and the value of each variable selected for PSA
        (labelled by the variable; empty for a metamodel which does not vary it).

    Raises:
        InterruptedError: if cancellation is requested.
    """
    metamodels = list(metamodels)
    if cancel_status is None:
        cancel_status = lambda: False

    if synchronise:
        varids = synchronise_psa_selection(metamodels)
    else:
        order: dict[str, None] = {}
        for mm in metamodels:
            for varid, var in mm.variables.items():
                if _psa_variable_is_varied(var):
                    order.setdefault(varid, None)
        varids = list(order)

    n_calcs = len(metamodels) * (samples + (1 if include_deterministic else 0))
    prog_i = 0
    def _report():
        if progress is not None:
            progress(prog_i, n_calcs)
    _report()

    if cancel_status():
        raise InterruptedError('PSA job cancelled')

    def _result(mm, draw: int, deterministic: bool) -> dict[str, Any]:
        res = make_psa_result(mm, mm.model, mm.finance, statistics, return_draws = True)
        return {'metamodel': mm.id, 'draw': draw, 'deterministic': deterministic, **res}

    results = []
    # Shared variables are a single instance; flag each instance once
    all_variables = list({id(v): v for mm in metamodels for v in mm.variables.values()}.values())

    if include_deterministic:
        for mm in metamodels:
            if not precomputed_deterministic:
                for v in mm.variables.values():
                    v.psa_active = False
                    v.update_model(mm.model)
                    v.update_model(mm.finance)
                mm.model.run()
                mm.finance.run()
            results.append(_result(mm, 0, True))
            prog_i += 1
            _report()

    if samples > 0:
        if rng is None:
            rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        elif seed is not None:
            warnings.warn('Both a seed and a random generator are provided - existing generator will be used without reseeding')

        varied_variables = [v for v in all_variables if _psa_variable_is_varied(v)]
        for v in varied_variables:
            v.psa_active = True

        try:
            for i in range(samples):
                if cancel_status():
                    raise InterruptedError('PSA job cancelled')

                draw_seed = int(rng.integers(0, 2**63 - 1))
                for k, varid in enumerate(varids):
                    drawn: set[int] = set()
                    for mm in metamodels:
                        var = mm.variables.get(varid)
                        if var is None or id(var) in drawn or not _psa_variable_is_varied(var):
                            continue
                        # Common random numbers: the same stream for every instance of the varid in this draw
                        var.draw_psa(np.random.default_rng([draw_seed, k]))
                        drawn.add(id(var))

                for mm in metamodels:
                    for v in mm.variables.values():
                        if _psa_variable_is_varied(v):
                            v.update_model_psa(mm.model)
                            v.update_model_psa(mm.finance)
                    mm.model.run()
                    mm.finance.run()
                    results.append(_result(mm, i + 1, False))
                    prog_i += 1
                    _report()
        finally:
            for v in varied_variables:
                v.psa_active = False
            for mm in metamodels:
                for v in mm.variables.values():
                    v.update_model(mm.model)
                    v.update_model(mm.finance)
                mm.model.run()
                mm.finance.run()

    odf = pd.DataFrame(results)
    statistic_columns = [x for x in statistics if x in odf.columns]
    leading = PSA_MULTIPLE_INDEX_COLUMNS + statistic_columns
    return odf.loc[:, leading + [x for x in odf.columns if x not in leading]]

Compare two metamodels of a whole-project PSA: the comparator against the reference, draw by draw.

For each draw (including the deterministic run, draw 0, if present) the statistics of the reference are subtracted from those of the comparator:

  • incremental total costs and benefits: the change in total present costs and in total present benefits;
  • incremental net monetary value: incremental benefits less incremental costs (the change in net present value);
  • incremental capex and opex: the change in total capital expenditure and in total recurrent costs. These are NaN if the results do not include the capex and opex statistics.

each discounted and undiscounted. The values drawn for the variables are kept (those of the comparator, or of the reference for a variable that only the reference varies), so that increments can be related to the draws.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default results DataFrame

The results of run_psa_multiple, which must include the total present costs and benefits, discounted and undiscounted.

required comparator_id str

Id of the comparator metamodel.

required reference_id str

Id of the reference metamodel.

required

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame

Dataframe with columns draw, deterministic, the pairwise statistics and the values of the variables.

Raises:

Type Description KeyError

if a metamodel, or a required statistic, is not in the results.

Source code in src/newsegsmodelframework/newsegssensitivity/psa.py 
def psa_pairwise(
    results: pd.DataFrame,
    comparator_id: str,
    reference_id: str,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Compare two metamodels of a whole-project PSA: the comparator against the reference, draw by draw.

    For each draw (including the deterministic run, draw 0, if present) the statistics of the reference are
    subtracted from those of the comparator:

    - incremental total costs and benefits: the change in total present costs and in total present benefits;
    - incremental net monetary value: incremental benefits less incremental costs (the change in net present value);
    - incremental capex and opex: the change in total capital expenditure and in total recurrent costs. These are
      NaN if the results do not include the capex and opex statistics.

    each discounted and undiscounted. The values drawn for the variables are kept (those of the comparator, or of
    the reference for a variable that only the reference varies), so that increments can be related to the draws.

    Args:
        results: The results of `run_psa_multiple`, which must include the total present costs and benefits,
            discounted and undiscounted.
        comparator_id: Id of the comparator metamodel.
        reference_id: Id of the reference metamodel.

    Returns:
        Dataframe with columns `draw`, `deterministic`, the pairwise statistics and the values of the variables.

    Raises:
        KeyError: if a metamodel, or a required statistic, is not in the results.
    """
    required = [
        f'total_present_{x}_{y}' for x in ('costs', 'benefits') for y in ('discounted', 'undiscounted')
    ]
    missing = [x for x in required if x not in results.columns]
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(f'PSA results do not include the statistics required for pairwise comparison: {missing}')

    def _frame(mm_id):
        df = results.loc[results['metamodel'] == mm_id, :]
        if len(df) == 0:
            raise KeyError(f'Metamodel {mm_id} not found in PSA results')
        return df.set_index('draw')

    comp = _frame(comparator_id)
    ref = _frame(reference_id).reindex(comp.index)

    odf = pd.DataFrame({'deterministic': comp['deterministic']}, index = comp.index)
    for disc in ('discounted', 'undiscounted'):
        d_costs = comp[f'total_present_costs_{disc}'] - ref[f'total_present_costs_{disc}']
        d_benefits = comp[f'total_present_benefits_{disc}'] - ref[f'total_present_benefits_{disc}']
        odf[f'incremental_net_monetary_value_{disc}'] = d_benefits - d_costs
        odf[f'incremental_total_costs_{disc}'] = d_costs
        odf[f'incremental_total_benefits_{disc}'] = d_benefits
        for cost in ('all_capex_costs', 'all_recurrent_costs'):
            stat = f'{cost}_{disc}'
            odf[f'incremental_{stat}'] = comp[stat] - ref[stat] if stat in results.columns else np.nan

    variable_columns = psa_variable_columns(results)
    draws = comp.loc[:, variable_columns].combine_first(ref.loc[:, variable_columns])
    draws = draws.loc[:, [x for x in variable_columns if draws[x].notna().any()]]

    odf = odf.join(draws).reset_index()
    return odf.loc[:, ['draw', 'deterministic'] + list(get_args(PSA_PAIRWISE_STATISTIC)) + list(draws.columns)]

def psa_net_benefit(
    results: pd.DataFrame,
    metamodel_ids: Sequence[str],
    benefit_value: float = 1.,
    cost_statistic: str = 'total_present_costs_discounted',
    benefit_statistic: str = 'total_present_benefits_discounted',
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The net benefit of each metamodel in each draw of a whole-project PSA, valuing benefits by a multiplier.

    The net benefit is `benefit_value * benefits - costs`; with a multiplier of 1 it is the net present value.

    Args:
        results: The results of `run_psa_multiple`.
        metamodel_ids: Ids of the metamodels.
        benefit_value: The value of one pound of benefit.
        cost_statistic: The statistic used as costs.
        benefit_statistic: The statistic used as benefits.

    Returns:
        Dataframe indexed by draw (sampled draws only), with a column for each metamodel.

    Raises:
        KeyError: if a metamodel is not in the results.
    """
    sampled = results.loc[~results['deterministic'].astype(bool), :]
    frames = {}
    for mm_id in metamodel_ids:
        df = sampled.loc[sampled['metamodel'] == mm_id, :]
        if len(df) == 0:
            raise KeyError(f'Metamodel {mm_id} not found in PSA results')
        df = df.set_index('draw')
        frames[mm_id] = benefit_value * df[benefit_statistic] - df[cost_statistic]
    return pd.DataFrame(frames).dropna()

def psa_ceac(
    results: pd.DataFrame,
    metamodel_ids: Sequence[str],
    benefit_values: Sequence[float],
    cost_statistic: str = 'total_present_costs_discounted',
    benefit_statistic: str = 'total_present_benefits_discounted',
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cost-effectiveness acceptability curves and frontier of the metamodels of a whole-project PSA.

    For each value of benefits (see `psa_net_benefit`), the probability that each metamodel is cost-effective -
    has the greatest net benefit of the metamodels in a draw - and the frontier: the metamodel with the greatest
    expected (mean) net benefit, which is the one to choose at that value, with its probability of being cost-effective.

    Args:
        results: The results of `run_psa_multiple`.
        metamodel_ids: Ids of the metamodels compared.
        benefit_values: The values of one pound of benefit at which to evaluate the curves.
        cost_statistic: The statistic used as costs.
        benefit_statistic: The statistic used as benefits.

    Returns:
        Dataframe indexed by `benefit_value`, with a column of the probability for each metamodel, `frontier`
        (the id of the metamodel on the frontier) and `frontier_probability`.

    Raises:
        KeyError: if a metamodel is not in the results.
        ValueError: if no metamodels are given.
    """
    metamodel_ids = list(metamodel_ids)
    if not metamodel_ids:
        raise ValueError('No metamodels to compare')
    rows = []
    for benefit_value in benefit_values:
        nb = psa_net_benefit(results, metamodel_ids, benefit_value, cost_statistic, benefit_statistic)
        values = nb.to_numpy(dtype = np.float64)
        best = np.argmax(values, axis = 1)
        probabilities = np.bincount(best, minlength = len(metamodel_ids)) / max(1, len(best))
        frontier = int(np.argmax(values.mean(axis = 0))) if len(values) else 0
        row: dict[str, Any] = {'benefit_value': float(benefit_value)}
        row.update({mm_id: p for mm_id, p in zip(metamodel_ids, probabilities)})
        row['frontier'] = metamodel_ids[frontier]
        row['frontier_probability'] = probabilities[frontier]
        rows.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index('benefit_value')

def psa_marginal(
    results: pd.DataFrame,
    variable_column: str,
    statistic: str,
    bins: int = 10,
) -> PSAMarginalData:
    """Marginal (univariate) sensitivity of a statistic of a PSA to the draws of one variable.

    The other variables vary too, so the relation is that of the statistic to the variable averaged over the
    other variables. Works on the results of one metamodel or on pairwise (incremental) results.

    Args:
        results: The results: those of `run_psa`, `psa_multiple_for_metamodel` or `psa_pairwise`.
        variable_column: The column of the variable.
        statistic: The column of the statistic.
        bins: The number of quantile groups of the variable.

    Returns:
        The points, the binned means and the summary statistics. The statistics are NaN where they cannot be
        found (fewer than three draws, or a variable or statistic which does not vary).

    Raises:
        KeyError: if the variable or the statistic is not in the results.
    """
    if variable_column not in results.columns:
        raise KeyError(f'Variable {variable_column} not found in PSA results')
    if statistic not in results.columns:
        raise KeyError(f'Statistic {statistic} not found in PSA results')
    sampled = results
    if 'deterministic' in results.columns:
        sampled = results.loc[~results['deterministic'].astype(bool), :]
    points = (
        pd.DataFrame({
            'x': pd.to_numeric(sampled[variable_column], errors = 'coerce'),
            'y': pd.to_numeric(sampled[statistic], errors = 'coerce'),
        })
        .dropna()
        .reset_index(drop = True)
    )

    nan = float('nan')
    spearman = pearson = slope = intercept = r_squared = nan
    x = points['x'].to_numpy(dtype = np.float64)
    y = points['y'].to_numpy(dtype = np.float64)
    if len(points) >= 3 and np.ptp(x) > 0:
        slope, intercept = (float(v) for v in np.polyfit(x, y, 1))
        if np.ptp(y) > 0:
            pearson = float(np.corrcoef(x, y)[0, 1])
            spearman = float(points['x'].rank().corr(points['y'].rank()))
            r_squared = pearson**2
        else:
            r_squared = 0.

    if len(points):
        if np.ptp(x) > 0:
            groups = pd.qcut(points['x'], q = min(bins, len(points)), duplicates = 'drop')
        else:
            # A variable that does not vary is a single group
            groups = pd.Series(0, index = points.index)
        binned = (
            points
            .groupby(groups, observed = True)
            .agg(
                x = ('x', 'mean'),
                y = ('y', 'mean'),
                y_lower = ('y', lambda s: s.quantile(0.05)),
                y_upper = ('y', lambda s: s.quantile(0.95)),
                count = ('y', 'count'),
            )
            .reset_index(drop = True)
        )
    else:
        binned = pd.DataFrame(columns = ['x', 'y', 'y_lower', 'y_upper', 'count'])

    return PSAMarginalData(points, binned, spearman, pearson, slope, intercept, r_squared)

def get_null_psa_data(statistics: Sequence[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Placeholder PSA results, to draw plots before there are results.

    Args:
        statistics: The statistics for which to make data.

    Returns:
        A dataframe of two rows - one deterministic and one not (draws 0 and 1) - with every statistic equal to 1.
    """
    stat_dict = {
        x: [1, 1] for x in statistics
    }
    stat_dict['deterministic'] = [True, False]
    stat_dict['draw'] = [0, 1]
    return pd.DataFrame.from_dict(
            stat_dict
        )

def psa_scatter_data(
    psa_data: pd.DataFrame,
    cost_statistic: str = 'total_present_costs_discounted',
    benefit_statistic: str = 'total_present_benefits_discounted'
) -> PSAScatterData:
    """Data for the scatter plot of the costs and benefits of the samples of a PSA.

    Each sample is categorised as cost effective (`CE`) if its benefits exceed its costs.

    Args:
        psa_data: The results of the PSA.
        cost_statistic: The statistic used as costs.
        benefit_statistic: The statistic used as benefits.

    Returns:
        The samples with their category, the deterministic point and the proportion of samples that are cost effective.
    """
    scatter_data = (
        psa_data
        .query('deterministic == False')
        .loc[:, [cost_statistic, benefit_statistic]]
        .assign(
            cost_effective = lambda df: (df[benefit_statistic] > df[cost_statistic]).map({True: 'CE', False: 'Not CE'})
        )
        .assign(
            cost_effective = lambda df: pd.Categorical(df['cost_effective'], categories=['CE', 'Not CE'], ordered = True)
        )
    )

    det_point = (
        psa_data
        .query('deterministic == True')
        .loc[:, [cost_statistic, benefit_statistic]]
        .iloc[0]
    )

    ce_proportion = scatter_data['cost_effective'].eq('CE').mean()

    return PSAScatterData(scatter_data, det_point, ce_proportion)

        det_value,

    )

def psa_convergence_data(
    psa_data: pd.DataFrame,
    statistic: str,
    convergence_statistic: _CONVERGENCE_STATISTICS
):
    """Data for the plot of the convergence of a statistic of a PSA over its draws.

    For each draw, the value of the convergence statistic (e.g. the mean) of the samples so far, with its standard error.

    Args:
        psa_data: The results of the PSA.
        statistic: The statistic of the model whose convergence is plotted.
        convergence_statistic: The statistic of the samples: mean, variance, median or a decile or quartile.

    Returns:
        The convergence of the statistic with its standard error at each draw, and its final value.

    Raises:
        ValueError: if the convergence statistic is not recognised.
    """
    raw_frame = (
        psa_data
        .query('deterministic == False')
        .loc[:, ['draw', statistic]]
    )

    match convergence_statistic:
        case 'Mean':
            final_stat = raw_frame[statistic].mean()
            sample_std = raw_frame[statistic].std()
            stat_data = (
                raw_frame
                .assign(
                    cumstat = lambda df: df[statistic].expanding().mean(),
                    stderr = lambda df: sample_std / np.sqrt(df['draw'])
                )
            )
        case 'Variance':
            final_stat = raw_frame[statistic].var()
            # Assume that we have convergence and Normally distributed so SE can
            # be estimated using s^2 as sigma^2
            stat_data = (
                raw_frame
                .assign(
                    cumstat = lambda df: df[statistic].expanding().var(),
                    stderr = lambda df: np.sqrt((2. * final_stat**2) / df['draw'])
                )
            )
        case 'Median':
            final_stat = raw_frame[statistic].median()
            # https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/wrappedtools/html/se_median.html
            # https://github.com/abusjahn/wrappedtools/blob/main/R/descriptives.R
            from scipy.stats import median_abs_deviation
            mad = median_abs_deviation(raw_frame[statistic])
            stat_data = (
                raw_frame
                .assign(
                    cumstat = lambda df: df[statistic].expanding().median(),
                    stderr = lambda df: mad / np.sqrt(df['draw'])
                )
            )
        case 'First Decile':
            q = 0.1
            final_stat = float(raw_frame[statistic].quantile(q))
            stat_data = (
                raw_frame
                .assign(
                    cumstat = lambda df: df[statistic].expanding().quantile(q),
                    stderr = lambda df: quantile_stderr_cum(df[statistic], q)
                )
            )
        case 'First Quartile':
            q = 0.25
            final_stat = float(raw_frame[statistic].quantile(q))
            stat_data = (
                raw_frame
                .assign(
                    cumstat = lambda df: df[statistic].expanding().quantile(q),
                    stderr = lambda df: quantile_stderr_cum(df[statistic], q)
                )
            )
        case 'Third Quartile':
            q = 0.75
            final_stat = float(raw_frame[statistic].quantile(q))
            stat_data = (
                raw_frame
                .assign(
                    cumstat = lambda df: df[statistic].expanding().quantile(q),
                    stderr = lambda df: quantile_stderr_cum(df[statistic], q)
                )
            )
        case 'Ninth Decile':
            q = 0.9
            final_stat = float(raw_frame[statistic].quantile(q))
            stat_data = (
                raw_frame
                .assign(
                    cumstat = lambda df: df[statistic].expanding().quantile(q),
                    stderr = lambda df: quantile_stderr_cum(df[statistic], q)
                )
            )
        case _:
            raise ValueError(f'convergence_statistic not recognised: {convergence_statistic}')

    stat_data = (
        stat_data
        .assign(
            lower_bound = lambda df: final_stat - 2.0 * df['stderr'],
            upper_bound = lambda df: final_stat + 2.0 * df['stderr']
        )
    )

    return PSAConvergenceData(
        stat_data,
        final_stat
    )

def repeat_list_by_index(
    l: Sequence[T], 
    repeats: int | Sequence[int]
) -> List[T]:
    """Repeat each element of a list.

    Raises `AssertionError` if `repeats` is a sequence of a different length.

    Args:
        l: The list.
        repeats: Number of times to repeat each element, or a number for each element.

    Returns:
        The list with each element repeated.
    """
    if not isinstance(repeats, Sequence):
        repeats = [repeats] * len(l)
    assert len(l) == len(repeats), '`repeats` must be a scalar or same length as the list'
    olist = []
    for i in range(len(l)):
        olist.extend([l[i]] * repeats[i])
    return olist

@lru_cache
def get_holiday_df(start_year, end_year, holiday_country = 'GB', holiday_subdiv = 'WLS'):
    """Dataframe of the holidays in a range of years, by day.

    For Great Britain the holidays are read from the parquet files in the `data` directory; otherwise they come from the `holidays` package. Cached.

    Args:
        start_year: First year.
        end_year: Last year.
        holiday_country: Country code of the holidays.
        holiday_subdiv: Subdivision code of the holidays.

    Returns:
        Dataframe indexed by day, flagging holidays.
    """
    if holiday_country == 'GB':
        global _loaded_holidays
        hol_fn = 'gb_' + holiday_subdiv.lower() + '.parquet'
        raw_df = _loaded_holidays.get(hol_fn)
        if raw_df is None:
            raw_df = pd.read_parquet(os.path.join(STATICDATA, 'holidays', hol_fn))
            _loaded_holidays[hol_fn] = raw_df
        days = pd.date_range('{}-01-01'.format(start_year), '{}-01-01'.format(end_year + 1), freq = 'D', tz = 'utc')

        return raw_df.loc[days, :]
    else:
        import holidays
        hols = holidays.country_holidays(holiday_country, holiday_subdiv)
        days = pd.date_range('{}-01-01'.format(start_year), '{}-01-01'.format(end_year + 1), freq = 'D', tz = 'utc')
        hol_df = (
            pd.DataFrame({'datetime_day': days})
            .assign(
                is_holiday = lambda df: df.apply(lambda rw: rw['datetime_day'] in hols, axis=1)
            )
            .set_index('datetime_day')
        )
    return hol_df

def copy_name(name: str, existing: Iterable[str] = ()) -> str:
    """The name of a copy: the name with a numbered copy suffix, unique among the existing names.

    The suffix of a copy of a copy replaces the source's, so suffixes don't stack: copies of "Baseline" are
    "Baseline (copy)", "Baseline (copy 2)", "Baseline (copy 3)"..., and so are copies of those copies.

    Args:
        name: The name of the source.
        existing: The names the copy must not take, such as those of the other configurations of the project.

    Returns:
        The name of the copy.
    """
    match = _COPY_SUFFIX.match(name)
    base = match.group('base') if match else name
    taken = set(existing)
    candidate = f'{base} (copy)'
    n = 1
    while candidate in taken:
        n += 1
        candidate = f'{base} (copy {n})'
    return candidate

    """A name, or the name of a copy of it if the name is taken.

def get_cp(file_name):
    """Read a power coefficient curve and return a function interpolating it.

    The file is an Excel file with `wind_speed` and `coeff_power` columns. The function gives zero outside the range of the curve.

    Args:
        file_name: Path of the file.

    Returns:
        Function of wind speed returning the power coefficient.
    """
    cp_file = pd.read_excel(file_name)
    def interpolant(x):
        return np.interp(x, cp_file['wind_speed'], cp_file['coeff_power'], left=0.0, right=0.0)
    return interpolant

def bearing_to_category(bearings,
                        categories=BEARING_DICT,
                        offset=None):
    """Categorise bearings into compass points.

    Args:
        bearings: Bearings in degrees.
        categories: Dictionary of the maximum angle of each category.
        offset: Offset (degrees) of the categories; by default half a category width.

    Returns:
        Ordered categorical of the compass points.
    """
    if offset is None:
        offset = (360.0 / len(categories)) / 2.0

    b = (bearings + 360.0 + offset)%360.0 
    o = np.zeros_like(b, dtype=str)
    for cat, max_angle in reversed(categories.items()):
        ma = max_angle + offset
        o = np.where(b < ma, cat, o)
    o = pd.Categorical(o,categories=list(categories.keys()),ordered=True)
    return o

def get_alpha_distribution(newa_meso_data):
    """Get the value of the Prandtl log-law scaling parameter from NEWA mesoscale data"""
    z_ref = newa_meso_data.height.unique()
    assert len(z_ref) == 1, "Please provide only a single wind speed height in NEWA data"
    z_ref = z_ref[0]

    # Remove unstable atmospheres, leaving neutral and stable
    idf = newa_meso_data.query('inverse_obukhov_length >= 0.0')

    # Categorise wind speed and direction
    idf = (
        idf
        .assign(
            wd_10_cat=lambda df: bearing_to_category(df['wind_from_direction_10m']),
            ws_10_cat=lambda df: pd.cut(df['wind_speed_10m'], _WS_BINS)
        )
    )

    # Calculate alpha
    denom = np.log(z_ref) - np.log(10.0)
    idf = (
        idf
        .assign(
            alpha = lambda df: (np.log(df['wind_speed']) - np.log(df['wind_speed_10m']))/denom
        )
    )

    o1 = idf.groupby(['wd_10_cat','ws_10_cat'])['alpha'].mean()

    all_cats = expand_grid({'wd_10_cat':BEARING_DICT.keys(),
                            'ws_10_cat':pd.cut([], _WS_BINS).categories})
    o2 = (
        pd.merge(
            all_cats,
            o1,
            on=['wd_10_cat','ws_10_cat'],
            how='left'
        )
        .ffill()
        .set_index(['wd_10_cat','ws_10_cat'])
    )

    return o2

def get_alphas(wd_10, ws_10, alpha_dist):
    """The wind shear exponent for each wind direction and speed.

    Looked up from the distribution by compass point and wind speed bin.

    Args:
        wd_10: Wind directions at 10 m.
        ws_10: Wind speeds at 10 m.
        alpha_dist: Distribution of the shear exponent by wind direction and speed bin.

    Returns:
        Array of shear exponents.
    """
    idf = (
        pd.DataFrame({
            'wd_10': wd_10,
            'ws_10': ws_10
            })
        .assign(
            wd_10_cat=lambda df: bearing_to_category(df['wd_10']),
            ws_10_cat=lambda df: pd.cut(df['ws_10'], _WS_BINS)
        )
    )

    return (idf.set_index(['wd_10_cat','ws_10_cat']).join(alpha_dist)['alpha'].values)

def to_newa_datetime_string(dt: NewaDatetime) -> str:
    """Format a datetime as the New European Wind Atlas API requires, e.g. `'2005-01-01T00:00:00'`.

    The API takes UTC times without a timezone, to the second, so a timezone-aware datetime is converted to UTC
    and a naive one is taken to be UTC already.

    Args:
        dt: The datetime; a string is parsed by `pd.Timestamp`.

    Returns:
        The formatted datetime.
    """
    ts = pd.Timestamp(dt)
    if ts.tz is not None:
        ts = ts.tz_convert('UTC').tz_localize(None)
    return ts.strftime(_NEWA_DATETIME_FORMAT)

def get_wind_at_site(
    lat: float, lon: float,
    rng: np.random.Generator,
    meso_reference_height: float = 50,
    micro_reference_height: float = 50,
    dt_start: NewaDatetime = '2005-01-01T00:00:00',
    dt_stop: NewaDatetime = '2022-12-31T23:30:00',
    site_heights: Sequence[float] = EVAL_HEIGHTS,
    #site_cps = CPS,
    return_working: bool = False
) -> pd.DataFrame | dict[str, Any]:

    """Wind speeds at a site, at heights, from the New European Wind Atlas.

    Takes the mesoscale wind speed series at the reference height and maps its Weibull distribution onto the microscale Weibull distribution of the site, then scales the result to each site height by the power law with a shear exponent which depends upon the wind direction and speed.

    Args:
        lat: Latitude (degrees).
        lon: Longitude (degrees).
        rng: Random number generator, which resolves ties when the wind speeds are sorted.
        meso_reference_height: Height (m) of the mesoscale data used as reference.
        micro_reference_height: Height (m) of the microscale data used as reference.
        dt_start: Start of the period; see `to_newa_datetime_string`.
        dt_stop: End of the period; see `to_newa_datetime_string`.
        site_heights: Heights (m) at which to give the wind speeds.
        return_working: Return the intermediate data as well.

    Returns:
        The wind speed series at each height; with `return_working`, a dictionary which also holds the intermediate data.
    """
    meso_data = get_newa_meso_ts_point(lat, lon,
                                       height=meso_reference_height,
                                       dt_start=to_newa_datetime_string(dt_start),
                                       dt_stop=to_newa_datetime_string(dt_stop),
                                       variables=['wind_speed',
                                                  'wind_from_direction_10m',
                                                  'wind_speed_10m',
                                                  'inverse_obukhov_length'])

    alpha_dist = get_alpha_distribution(meso_data)

    micro_data = get_newa_micro_point(lat, lon,
                                      height=micro_reference_height,
                                      variables=['weib_A_combined',
                                                 'weib_k_combined',
                                                 'air_dens'])

    rho = micro_data['air_dens'].values[0]

    # Our reference wind time series is the mesoscale at ref height.
    ref_ts = meso_data.loc[:,['time','wind_speed','wind_speed_10m','wind_from_direction_10m']]

    # First, let's sort the wind speeds, as will need to do so regardless
    ref_ts = (
        ref_ts
        .sample(frac=1,random_state=rng)
        .sort_values('wind_speed')
    )

    # Determine Weibull parameters for this ts
    # Now get the reference Weibull parameters
    ws_ref_wb_pars = weibull_min.fit(ref_ts['wind_speed'],floc=0.0)
    ws_ref_wb_pars = dict(zip(('c','loc','scale'), ws_ref_wb_pars))
    # Based on this, we can find the empirical maximum value of the CDF achieved
    max_cdf = weibull_min.cdf(x=ref_ts['wind_speed'].max(),**ws_ref_wb_pars)

    # Generate the wind speeds across the probability distribution at micro reference height
    ws_site_ref = weibull_min.ppf(q=np.linspace(0,max_cdf,len(ref_ts)),
                                  c=micro_data['weib_k_combined'].values[0],
                                  loc=0.0,
                                  scale=micro_data['weib_A_combined'].values[0])

    # Augment ref ts with the local 50 m wind speed and the alpha parameter
    ref_ts = (
        ref_ts
        .assign(
            ws_ref_local=ws_site_ref,
            alpha=lambda df:get_alphas(df['wind_from_direction_10m'].values, df['wind_speed_10m'].values, alpha_dist)
        )
    )

    # Extrapolation function
    def get_wind_speed_at_height(z):
        return (
            ref_ts
            .copy()
            .assign(
                ws_hub = lambda df: df['ws_ref_local'] * (z / micro_reference_height) ** df['alpha'],
            )
            .sort_values('time')
            .assign(hub_height=z)
    )

    #def get_specific_wind_power_at_height(z, cp_func):
    #    return (
    #        ref_ts
    #        .copy()
    #        .assign(
    #            ws_hub = lambda df: df['ws_ref_local'] * (z / micro_reference_height) ** df['alpha'],
    #            sp_power = lambda df: 0.001 * 0.5 * rho * cp_func(df['ws_hub']) * df['ws_hub']**3
    #        )
    #        .sort_values('time')
    #        .assign(hub_height=z)
    #)

    olist = []
    for z in site_heights:
        olist.append(get_wind_speed_at_height(z))


    odata = pd.concat(olist)

    if return_working:
        return {
            'site_ts': odata,
            'ref_ts': ref_ts,
            'alpha_dist': alpha_dist,
            'micro_weibull_pars': micro_data,
            'meso_weibull_pars': ws_ref_wb_pars
        }
    else :
        return odata

docs.title: Variable
docs.text:
A Variable is a container for data associated with an Energy Model or Finance Model parameter. Principally, they exist to hold data related to sensitivity analysis of a Metamodel i.e. whilst the Model and Finance hold current parameters for analysis, the Variables list holds the metaparameters which indicate how those parameters are to be varied in Deterministic (One-Way) Sensitivity Analysis and Probabilistic Sensitivity Analysis.

Glossary: - Parameter: An item of data which influences the outcome(s) of a model (e.g. fixed cost per kW wind generation installed). - Value: A number, string, or vector of numbers or strings which can be used as a Parameter of a Model or Finance (e.g. £1,000 / kW). - Variable: A container holding data allowing for the production of Values used to parameterise a Model (e.g. an object identifying itself as associated with the parameter "fixed per-unit cost of wind" within an Energy Model, where that parameter is uncertain with a probability density described by a Gamma distribution with mean £1,000 / kW and standard deviation of £100 / kW). - Metaparameter: An item of data used to parameterise a Variable (e.g. the standard deviation of the fixed per-unit cost of wind). - Metavalue: A number, string, or vector of number or strings which can be used as a Metaparameter of a Variable (e.g. £100 / kW).

The data a Variable carries serves the following purposes:

  1. Naming and presenting the Variable (i.e. a name, a unit, an icon_name).
  2. Hierarchically identifying the associated parameter for presentation in a User Interface:
    • configuration_type: 'model' or 'finance'
    • interface_section: e.g. 'gen_input' for generation configuration input
    • interface_key: e.g. 'pv_capacity' for the value in kWp of PV installed
    • interface_subindex: e.g. 0 to indicate this is the value for the 0-indexed PV array aspect, which might be 180° (south) whilst index 1 might be an array at 90° (east).
  3. Hierarchically identifying the associated parameter within the Model or Finance object:
    • configuration_type: 'model' or 'finance' (shared with the Interface purpose)
    • model_section: e.g. 'mod_gen' for the generation Module of a Model.
    • model_parameter: e.g. 'pv_capacity' for the value in kWp of PV installed.
  4. Identifying the statistical distribution used for its Value(s).
  5. Storing Metaparameters to provide a fixed (deterministic / mean values) Value to its associated Parameter.
  6. Storing Metaparameters for use in DSA (i.e. whether the Parameter is to be varied, and the values to which to set the associated Parameter).
  7. Storing Metaparameters for use in PSA (i.e. whether the Parameter is to be varied, and the distribution characteristics of the Parameter).

A single unit of variation in a model.

May be associated with a single parameter, or a group of parameters that must co-vary (e.g. the parameters of a statistical distribution, or a set of probabilities which form a simplex). A Variable is a NewsegsComponent so is serialisable and revision-tracked.
